Number of n-step self-avoiding walks on a 2D square lattice where the first visited lattice point is directly visible from the last visited lattice point, and were both the visited lattice points and the path between these points are considered when determining the visibility of points.
a(n) = n-th elementary symmetric function of {1, prime(1), prime(2), ..., prime(n)}.

a(n) = 1 if for 1 <= i < j <= h, all sigma(p_i^e_i), sigma(p_j^e_j) are pairwise coprime, otherwise 0. Here n = p_1^e_1 * ... * p_h^e_h, where each p_i^e_i is the maximal power of prime p_i dividing n.
a(n) is the least k such that k concatenated with k + n is prime.
Number of pairs 1 <= x <= y <= n-1 such that gcd(x,n) = gcd(y,n) = gcd(x+y,n) = 1 and 1/x + 1/y == 1/(x+y) mod n.
a(n) is the smallest natural number k such that the concatenation (n+k)||k is a prime number.
Smallest 7-smooth number beginning with n.
Number of partitions of 2n into the sum of two twin primes.
Number of nondecreasing tuples (x_1, ..., x_k) of positive integers (or integer partitions) such that the multinomial coefficient (x_1 + ... + x_k)!/(x_1! * ... * x_k!) equals n.
a(n) = (sum of proper prime factors of n) + Sum_{d = proper composite factor of n} a(d).
T(n,k) = binomial(n,k)*binomial(n+k,k), 0 <= k <= n, triangle read by rows.
Triangle defined by g.f. A(x,q) such that: A(x,q) = 1 + x*A(q*x,q)*A(x,q), as read by terms k=0..n*(n-1)/2 in rows n>=0.
Totients phi(m) having one or more solutions m to phi(m)^2 = phi(phi(m)*m).
4-brilliant numbers: numbers which are the product of four primes having the same number of decimal digits.

Start with a(0)=0; thereafter, look left and identify the least frequent digit d so far (in case of a tie, choose the smallest d): after then a(n) = 10c + d, where c > 0 is the number of times d has appeared so far.
Length of shortest path (in Chebyshev distance) that touches all cells in an n X n grid.
Length of shortest addition-multiplication-composition chain for n, starting with 1 and x.
Number of prime powers p^m <= n such that p | n.
Length of shortest addition-composition chain for n, starting with 1 and x.
a(n) is the maximal size of a set S of points in {0,1}^n in real n-dimensional Euclidean space such that every angle determined by three points in S is acute.
a(n) = n mod 2 + n mod 4 + ... + n mod 2^k, where 2^k <= n < 2^(k+1).
Irregular triangle read by rows where row k lists the lengths of maximal anti-runs (increasing by more than 1) in the binary indices of n.
a(n) is the largest integer m such that s/(m!-1) is an integer, where s is the sum of all previous terms; a(1)=1.
List of juxtaposed reverse-lexicographically ordered partitions of the positive integers.
Numbers for which the differences between consecutive divisors (ordered by size) are not distinct.
Number of regions formed when n points are placed in general position on each edge of a square and a chord is drawn from each point to the 3*n points on the other three sides.
a(n) is the smallest integer greater than a(n-1) such that all consecutive products in a(1)..a(n) are distinct, with a(1) = 2.
Number of composite numbers c such that c * sigma_n(c) == 2 (mod phi(c)).
Numbers k > 1 with the smallest prime divisor p, where the sum of divisors d in the range 1 < d < k/p is less than k/p.
Numbers k > 1 with the smallest prime divisor p, where the sum of divisors d in the range 1 < d < k/p is at least k/p, but no subset of these divisors sums to k/p.
Table T(n,k) = k^n read by upwards antidiagonals (n >= 1, k >= 1).
Array T(i,j) read by antidiagonals, where T(i,j) is the concatenation of i and j (1<=i, 1<=j).
Semiperfect numbers that cannot be represented as a sum of their nontrivial divisors.
a(n) is the sum of positions of 1's minus sum of positions of 0's in the binary expansion of n.
The smallest prime whose square divides n, 1 if n is squarefree.
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) is the total number of standard Young tableaux over all basic skew shapes with n boxes whose major index is congruent to k modulo n. (n >= 1, 0 <= k <= n-1).
'Brazilian' numbers ('les nombres brésiliens' in French): numbers n such that there is a natural number b with 1 < b < n-1 such that the representation of n in base b has all equal digits.
Weak Ackermann numbers: H_n(n,n) where H_n is the n-th hyperoperator.
a(n) = chi_{n,-1}(-1), where chi_{n,-1} is the Dirichlet character modulo n with label -1 in the Conrey labeling system.
Numbers k such that h(k) = h(k+1), where h(k) is the length of k, f(k), f(f(k)), ..., 1 in the Collatz (or 3x + 1) problem. (The earliest '1' is meant.)
a(n) = 5*F(n)^2 - 5*F(n) + 1, where F(n) = Fibonacci(n).
a(n) = 5*F(n)^2 + 5*F(n) + 1, where F(n) = Fibonacci(n).
In repeated iterations of function m -> m/2 if m even, m -> 3m+1 if m odd, a(n) is maximum value achieved if starting from n.
Numbers of form 3^i*8^j, with i, j >= 0.
a(n) = n * prime(n).
3-Knödel numbers or D-numbers: numbers m > 3 such that m | k^(m-2)-k for all k with gcd(k, m) = 1.
Fancy primitive repdigit polygonal numbers (with multiplicity).
a(n) = sigma_2(a(n-1)): sum of squares of divisors of a(n-1) with a(1)=2.
Expansion of 1/(1-4*x)^(7/2).
Triangle read by rows: row n gives coefficients in expansion of Product_{i=1..n} (x - (2i)^2), highest powers first.
Composite numbers n such that the sum of divisors of n, sigma(n), divided by the number of divisors, d(n) and sigma(n) minus n are both rational squares.
Triangular array read by rows: T(m,n) = n + n+1 + ... + m = (m+n)(m-n+1)/2.
Triangular array T, read by rows: T(n,k) = (n+1) mod floor((k+1)/2), k = 1..n and n >= 1.

Triangular array T given by rows: T(n,k)=sum of quotients when Euclidean algorithm acts on n and k; for k=1,2,...,n; n=1,2,3,...; also number of subtraction steps when computing gcd(n,k) using subtractions rather than divisions.
Triangular array T read by rows: T(n,k)=number of distinct numbers that appear when Euclidean algorithm acts on n,k, for k=1,2,...,n; n=1,2,3,...
Triangular array T read by rows: T(n,k) = sum of numbers c in the form c = bq + r when Euclidean algorithm acts on n, k, for 1 <= k <= n, n >= 1.
Products of two Fibonacci numbers with distinct indices.
Numbers of the form Fibonacci(i)*Fibonacci(j).

Sequence of 719 adjacent transpositions (a[n] a[n]+1), which, when starting from the identity permutation and applied successively, produce a Hamiltonian circuit/path through all 720 permutations of S_6, in such a way that S_{n-1} is always traversed before the rest of S_n.
Iterative 'rewrite' sequence of binary plane trees.
Binary encodings of the Catalan mountain ranges with exactly one sea-level valley, i.e., the rooted plane trees with root degree = 2.
Largest order of even permutation of n elements, or maximal order of element of alternating group A_n.
Numbers k such that 2 is a square mod k.
Smallest number with exactly n nonprime divisors.
a(0)=0, a(1)=2, a(n) = smallest number such that sequence b(n) = {a(n-1) BITWISE OR a(n)} is strictly monotonically increasing.
a(0) = 1, a(1) = 3, a(n) = smallest number such that sequence b(n) = a(n) OR a(n+1) is strictly monotonically increasing.
a(0)=2, a(1)=5, a(n) = smallest number such that sequence b(n) = a(n) OR a(n+1) is strictly monotonically increasing.
a(1) = 0; for n >= 2, a(n) = n - (largest prime <= n).
Permutation of Z, folded to N, corresponding to the site swap pattern ...26120123456... which ascends infinitely after t=0.

Limits of the recursion b(i+1)=B_[i](b(i)), where b(1)=n and B_[k+1](j) = B_[k](j), if j <= k; B_[k+1](j) = B_[k](j) + k, if j < k and (j mod 2k) >= k; B_[k+1](j) = B_[k](j) - k, if j < k and (j mod 2k) < k. Set a(n)=0 if b tends to infinity.
Number of 'Reverse and Add' steps needed to reach a palindrome starting at n, or -1 if n never reaches a palindrome.
Number of values of s, 0 < s <= n-1, such that s^s == s (mod n).
3-smooth numbers in their natural position, gaps filled with 0.
Triangular array read by rows associated with Schroeder numbers: T(1,k) = 1; T(n,k) = 0 if k < n; T(n,k) = T(n,k-1) + T(n-1,k-1) + T(n-1,k).
Decimal expansion of Product_{p prime >= 3} (1 - (p+2)/p^3).
Lesser of twin primes whose average is 6 times a prime.
Smallest number that is palindromic (with at least 2 digits) in n bases.
Sum of divisors of square numbers.
Prime cascade: multiplicative with a(prime(m)^k) = prime(m-1) * prime(m)^(k-1).
String formed from first n binary digits found in decimal expansion of Pi.
String formed from first n quaternary digits found in decimal expansion of Pi.
Smallest k such that sigma(n+k) = sigma(k).
a(n) is the minimal difference between primes p and q whose sum is 2n.
List of smallest solutions for some k of x = f^k(x), n <> f^j(n) for j < k, where f: m -> |m - reverse(m)|.
a(n) = binomial(3*n+1,n)/(n+1).
n is such that partial sum of pi(k) from 1 to n is divisible by n.
Greatest common divisor of n and the n-th composite number.
Numbers k that divide the sum of the first k composite numbers.
Number of distinct remainders arising when n is divided by all primes up to n.
Number of steps to reach an integer starting with (n+1)/n and using the map x -> x*ceiling(x); or -1 if no integer is ever reached.
Rearrangement of Fibonacci numbers such that sum of two consecutive terms is a prime.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest even number not already in the sequence such that a(1) + ... + a(n) is a prime.
Rearrangement of natural numbers such that a(k)*a(k+1) + 1 is a prime for all k.
Group the even numbers so that the product of the terms in each group + 1 is a prime: (2), (4), (6), (8, 10, 12, 14), (16), (18), ... Sequence gives number of terms in each group.
Generating function A(x) satisfies A(x) = (1+x)^2*A(x^2)^2, with A(0)=1.
Smallest positive triangular number not included earlier that is a multiple of n (a permutation of the triangular numbers).
a(1)=1 and then odd numbers rearranged such that a(n) is prime if n is composite else vice versa.
a(n) = Lucas(4n+3) + 1, or 5*Fibonacci(2n+1)*Fibonacci(2n+2).
Deletable primes: primes such that removing some digit leaves either the empty string or another deletable prime (possibly preceded by some zeros).

Smallest partial quotients of a series of continued fractions that have a sum of unity, where the n-th continued fraction term is [0; a(n),a(n-1),...,a(1)], so that sum(n>0, [0; a(n),a(n-1),...,a(1)] ) = 1, with a(1)=2.
Smallest squares such that partial sums of the sequence plus 11 are primes.
Smallest squares such that partial sums of the sequence plus 5 are primes.
Smallest squares such that partial sums of the sequence plus 17 are primes.
a(n) = n+r where r is the smallest number such that n divides (n+1)(n+2)(n+3)...(n+r).

Triangle read by rows in which the n-th row contains n terms of an arithmetic progression with a common difference of (n-1) and the first term of (n+1)-th row is 1 more than the last term of the n-th row.
a(n) = smallest number which can be expressed as the sum of n of its distinct divisors, or 0 if no such number exists.

Consider the smallest number m which can be expressed as the sum of n distinct numbers coprime to m. Sequence gives triangle (read by rows) of the set of coprime numbers pertaining to m. When there is a choice, use the lexicographically earliest solution.
Triangle read by rows in which row n consists of 1 and the n-1 smallest positive numbers having common factors with n.
Triangle, read by rows, in which the n-th row contains n smallest n-digit numbers.
Number of partitions of a 2n-set into even blocks.
Pascal-(1,2,1) array read by antidiagonals.
Pascal-(1,4,1) array.
Pascal-(1,5,1) array.
a(n) = ceiling((1 + sum of preceding terms) / 2) starting with a(0) = 1.
Smallest number == 0 mod (n+1)-th prime and == 1 mod all smaller primes.
a(n) is the smallest integer k such that floor((1+1/n)^(k+1))/floor((1+1/n)^k) = 1+1/n.
a(1)=1; for n>1, a(n)=a(n-1)-3 if n is already in the sequence, a(n)=a(n-1)+5 otherwise.
Triangle in which n-th row contains the first n numbers beginning with n.
Triangle read by rows in which row n gives n smallest palindromic numbers of n digits each.
In the following triangle the n-th row contains n numbers relatively prime to n and not occurring in a previous row. a(1) = 1. Sequence contains the triangle by rows.
Coefficient triangle of generalized Laguerre polynomials (a=1).
Prime productive numbers m: Let the digits of m be abcd. Then the numbers bcd*a+1, cd*ab+1, d*abc+1, abcd+1 etc. are all primes. If m is a k-digit number it produces k such primes.

Symmetric square table of coefficients, read by antidiagonals, where T(n,k) is the coefficient of x^n*y^k in f(x,y) that satisfies: f(x,y) = g(x,y) + xy*f(x,y)^4 and where g(x,y) satisfies: 1 + (x+y-1)*g(x,y) + xy*g(x,y)^2 = 0.
Triangle, read by rows, of coefficients for the second iteration of the hyperbinomial transform.
Hyperbinomial transform of the sequence of 1's.
Primes of the form smallest multiple of n followed by a 1.
Semiprimes of the form 2^k + k.
a(n) is the least semiprime > n!.
a(n) is the least semiprime >= n^n.
Catalan-Larcombe-French sequence.
Numbers n with property that n + 1 as well as the (product of digits of n) + 1 are primes.
Square array, read by antidiagonals, where the n-th row is the n-th binomial transform of the factorials, starting with row 0: {1!,2!,3!,...}.
Square array, read by antidiagonals, where the n-th row is the n-th binomial transform of the natural numbers, with T(0,k) = (k+1) for k>=0.
Nonsquare perfect powers.
Expansion of 1/((1 - 2*x + 2*x^2)*(1-x)).

Number of solutions (excluding rotations and reflections) for a series of 9 consecutive primes beginning with the n-th prime arranged in a 3 X 3 square such that all row, column and diagonal totals are primes.
Contains exactly once every pair (i,j) of positive integers.
a(1)=1; for n > 1, a(n) = Sum_{1<=j<n, gcd(j,n)=1} a(j)*a(n-j).
Fibonacci regression array: For n>=2 and 1<=k<=n-1, T(n,k) is the last term before the first nonpositive term in the sequence n, k, n-k, 2k-n, 2n-3k, 5k-3n, ...
a(n) = (n-th prime) - (n-th nonprime).
Successive digits of even numbers.
Triangle of permutations of [1..n] made by alternatively reversing terms counted from the left and right. (See comment.)
Describe n from right to left.
a(n+1) = if a(n) is even then a(n)/2 else (a(n) + number of earlier occurrences of a(n)), a(1) = 1.
Numbers j such that m = 216*j + 108 satisfies sigma(m) != 2*usigma(m).
Triangle T(n,k) read by rows: see formula lines for definition.
Chebyshev U(n,x) polynomial evaluated at x=339=2*13^2+1.
Number of rooted planar bridgeless cubic maps with 2n nodes.
Number of rooted cubic maps with 2n nodes and a distinguished Hamiltonian cycle: (2n)!(2n+1)! / (n!^2*(n+1)!(n+2)!).
a(n) = Sum_{ k >= 0 such that n + k == 0 mod 2^k } 2^(k-1).
Triangle, row sums = (Fibonacci numbers - 2).
Moebius transform of multiplication table, read by antidiagonals.
Esanacci (hexanacci or '6-anacci') numbers.
Numbers of the form 2^j (mod 10^k), where j >= 0 and k >= 1, with leading zeros suppressed.
Square table T, read by antidiagonals, where T(n,k) gives the number of n-th generation descendents of a node labeled (k) in the tree of tournament sequences.
Square table T, read by antidiagonals, where T(n,k) gives the number of n-th generation descendents of a node labeled (k), in the tree of 3-tournament sequences, for n>=1.
Square table T, read by antidiagonals, where T(n,k) gives the number of n-th generation descendents of a node labeled (k) in the tree of 4-tournament sequences.
Square table T, read by antidiagonals, where T(n,k) gives the number of n-th generation descendents of a node labeled (k) in the tree of 5-tournament sequences.
a(1) = 3; for n > 1, a(n) = 4*phi(n); given a rational number r = p/q, where q>0, (p,q)=1, define its height to be max{|p|,q}; then a(n) = number of rational numbers of height n.
Triangle T(n,k), 0<=k<=n, of coefficients of polynomials P_n(x) related to convolution of the k-fold factorials.
Record gaps between prime quadruplets.
Triangle read by rows: n-th row is the lexicographically earliest arithmetic progression of n numbers all having the same prime signature.
Numbers formed by arranging the digits of n in increasing order concatenated with arranging the digits in decreasing order.
A Fielder sequence.
a(n) is the composite between p(n) and p(n+1), where p(n) is the n-th prime, which is divisible by (p(n+1)-p(n)).

A variant of Golomb's sequence interpreted as a triangle: Start with a(1)=1 as first row, filled from left to right; fill row n+1 with the natural numbers continuing from row n in alternating order, with multiplicity according to the numbers given in row n in alternating order.
Primes having initial digits '10' in binary representation.
Primes having initial digits '11' in their binary representation.
Squares k such that k + pi(k) is a prime.
Number of matrices of any size up to column permutations, with n different elements, zero elsewhere and with no zero row or column.
Primes seen in the decimal expansion of Pi (disregarding the decimal point) that are contiguous, smallest and distinct.
Triangle T, read by rows, where column k equals column k of T^(2^k) shift down 1 row, with T(n,n)=T(n+1,n)=1 for n>=0.
Triangle of triangular binomial coefficients, read by rows, where column k has the g.f.: 1/(1-x)^((k+1)*(k+2)/2) for k >= 0.
Orders of finite perfect groups (groups such that G = G' where G' is the commutator subgroup of G).
Pisot sequence L(4,5).
Nexus numbers (n + 1)^7 - n^7.
Sierpiński numbers of the first kind: n^n + 1.
T(n, k) = [x^k] Sum_{k=0..n} Stirling2(n, k)*RisingFactorial(x, k), triangle read by rows, for n >= 0 and 0 <= k <= n.
Triangle read by rows, giving dimensions of exceptional groups with extension to E9 as a non-simple Lie algebra.
Primes of form 10n+3.
Primes of form 10n+7.
Primes of form 10*k + 9.
Decimal expansion of proposed value for Avogadro's number, namely 602214141070409084099072 = 84446888^3.
Number of partitions of n that do not contain 2 as a part.
Rectangular array, read by descending antidiagonals: a prime separator array.
a(n) = ceiling((Sum_{k=1..n-1} a(k)) / 2) for n >= 2 starting with a(1) = 1.
Triangle, read by rows, where T(n,k) is the coefficient of q^(nk-k) in the squared q-factorial of n.
a(n) is the smallest k > 0 such that k^2 + prime(n) is prime.
Positive integers k such that sopfr(k) divides sopfr(k+1), where sopfr(k) is the sum of the prime factors of k, counting multiplicity.
The second of the pair of consecutive integers k and k+1 such that sopfr(k) divides sopfr(k+1), where sopfr(k) is the sum of the prime factors of k, counting multiplicity.
a(n) = Product_{j=1..n} Product_{k=1..n} gcd(j,k).
4-dimensional pyramidal numbers: a(n) = n^2*(n^2-1)/12.
a(n) is the smallest root m of the least perfect power q (= m^k) such that n+q is an even semiprime, or -1 if no such q exists.
Matrix (1,x)-(x,x^2) in Riordan array notation.
Number of labeled bi-point-determining graphs with n vertices.
Triangle read by rows, constructed by a Pascal-like rule with left edge = 2^k, right edge = 2^(k+1)-1 (k >= 0).
Exponential Riordan array [e^(x/(1-x)),x].
Triangle T(n,k) = k! * Stirling1(n,k), 1<=k<=n.
Sequence s_n arising in enumeration of arrays of directed blocks (see Quaintance reference for precise definition).
Sequence t_n arising in enumeration of arrays of directed blocks (see Quaintance reference for precise definition).
Sequence h_n arising in enumeration of arrays of directed blocks (see Quaintance reference for precise definition).
a(n) = a(floor(n/2)) + floor(n/2) with a(1) = 1.
a(n) = n^3 if n is odd, n^3 + 1 otherwise.

Number of paths from (0,0,0) to (n,n,n) such that at each step (i) at least one coordinate increases, (ii) no coordinate decreases, (iii) no coordinate increases by more than 1 and (iv) all coordinates are integers.
Even squares: a(n) = (2*n)^2.
Nearest integer to log n.
a(1)=1; at n>=2, a(n) = least square > a(n-1) such that sum a(1)+...+a(n) is a prime number.
Prime numbers n such that n = p1^3 + p2^3 + p3^3, a sum of cubes of 3 distinct prime numbers.

Triangle T(n,k), 1 <= k <= n, read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of permutations in the symmetric group S_n having k multiplicative 3-excedances. Equivalently, the number of permutations of the set {3,6,9,...,3n} with k excedances.
Divisors of nonprimes not occurring earlier.
Primes that are simultaneously of the forms 24i+7 and 7j+24.
Triangle read by rows, T(n,k) = T(n-1, k-1) - T(n-k, k-1); with leftmost term in each row = sum of all previous terms.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = T(n-1, k-1) - T(n-k, k-1) for k > 1 with T(n,1) = 2^(n-1).
First denominator and then numerator (left to right) of Leibniz's harmonic-like triangle.
Sum of every 4th entry of row n in Pascal's triangle, starting at 'n choose 1'.
Year numbers: numbers n such that phi(n) = 2 phi(sigma(n)).
Numbers that are the products of 2 or more consecutive integers.
A transform of the Fibonacci numbers.
a(n) is the smallest integer > a(n-1) such that {Pi^a(n)} < {Pi^a(n-1)}, where {x} = x - floor(x), a(1)=1.
Numbers in base 3.
Partition number array, called M31hat(-2).
Partition number array, called M31hat(-3).
Partition number array, called M31hat(-4).
Partition number array, called M31hat(-5).

Subsequence of 'Fermat near misses' which is generated by a simple formula based on the cubic binomial expansion along with formulas for the corresponding terms in the expression, x^3 + y^3 = z^3 + 1.
Number of ground-state 3-ball juggling sequences of period n.
a(n) = the largest divisor of n! such that (sum{k=1 to n} a(k)) is a divisor of n!.
Even-indexed Chebyshev U-polynomials evaluated at sqrt(10)/2.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,0) = T(n,n) = 1 and for 0<k<n: T(n,k) = 2*T(n-1, k-1) + T(n-1,k).
Numerator of the polynomial A_l(x) = sum_{d=1..l-1} x^(l-d)/d for index l=2n+1 evaluated at x=1.
Numbers k such that k^2 = p^3 + q^3, p, q primes (p<=q).
Let b(1) = 2; and for n>= 2, if b(n-1) < prime(n) then b(n) = b(n-1) + prime(n) otherwise b(n) = b(n-1) - prime(n). The sequence gives the indices n where b(n-1) < b(n) < b(n+1).
Numbers k such that for each divisor d of k, d + k/d is 'round' ('square-root smooth').
Toothpick sequence in the first quadrant.
'Exact' continued fraction for Pi.
a(n) = integer nearest e*a(n-1), where a(0) = 1.
Nonprime numbers with smallest prime factor >= 13.
Triangle T(n,k) in which n-th row gives degrees of irreducible representations of symmetric group S_n.
Triple composites.
Triangle by columns: leftmost column = (1, 0, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1, ...); columns >1 = (1, 1, 0, 0, 0, ...).
The Gould numbers.
Right shift operator generating 1's in shifted spaces.
List of primes and squares.
V-toothpick sequence starting at the corner of an infinite square from which protrudes a half toothpick with an angle = Pi/6.
Number of triangles in the Y-toothpick structure after n rounds.
V-toothpick sequence starting from a V-toothpick whose central point touch a straight line, as a V.
Numbers k whose largest divisor <= sqrt(k) equals 4.
Denominator of density of integers with smallest prime factor prime(n).
RATS(n): Reverse Add Then Sort the digits.
Perfect Digital Invariants: numbers that are the sum of some fixed power of their digits.

In binary starting with 1, prepend a 1 and as few 0's as required such that the new number is relatively prime to all previous in sequence. Thus binary 1, 11, 111, 10111, 110111, 100110111, 1100110111, 11100110111.
Triangle T(n, k) = -floor(n/k) with T(n, n) = 1, read by rows.
a(0) = 0; for n>=0, a(n+1) = a(n) + x where x is the smallest nonnegative number which is not equal to a(i) +/- a(k) or a(i)/2 for any 0<=i<=n, 0<=k<=n.
Sum of the primes from the smallest prime factor of n to the largest prime factor of n.
Values of n >= 0 such that 3*n-45+360/(n/2+8) is an integer.
a(n) is the smallest integer that takes n halving and tripling steps to reach 1 in the 3x+1 problem.
Least monotonically increasing logarithmic derivative consisting of only squares.
Sum of binomial coefficients binomial(i+j, i) modulo 2 over all pairs (i,j) of positive integers satisfying 3i+j=n.
Number of ternary squarefree words of length n.
1 followed by -1, -1, -1, ... .
Primes in whose binary expansion the number of 1-bits is less than or equal to number of 0-bits.
Form triangle of weighted Farey fractions; read denominators by rows.
Form triangle of weighted Farey fractions; read numerators by rows.
a(n) is the number of integers N=4k whose 'basin' sequence (cf. comment) ends in n^2.

Product of first n Catalan numbers.
Number of minimax trees on n nodes.
Least prime such that whenever 2*a(n) = p+q with p and q prime, one has p,q > prime(n).
Rectangular array T(n,k) = 2^n + k - 2, by antidiagonals.
Prime numbers of measurement.
Primes with consecutive digits that differ exactly by 1.
Array: T(n,k) = n-1 + min{n,k}, by antidiagonals.
Array: T(n,k)=k-n+1 for k>=n; T(n,k)=0 for k<n; by antidiagonals.
Triangle T(n,m) = 1+2*m of odd numbers read along rows, 0<=m<n.
Worst case of a Jacobi symbol algorithm.
Triangle in which n-th row lists juxtaposed lexicographically ordered partitions of n; e.g., the partitions of 3 (1+1+1,1+2,3) appear as 1,1,1,1,2,3 in row 3.
Numbers generated by the golden sieve.
a(n) = 1 + ceiling((n-1)*phi^2), phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2.
Superduperfactorials: product of first n superfactorials.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the coefficient of x^k in the polynomial P[n] defined by P[0]=1, P[1]=x-1, P[n]=(1-x)P[n-1]+xP[n-2] for n>=2. Alternatively, P[n]=-1-(-x)^n-3*Sum((-x)^k,k=1..n-1).
A Fibonacci triangle: triangle T(n,k) = Fibonacci(k+1)*Fibonacci(n-k+1), for n >= 0, 0 <= k <= n.
Unhappy numbers: numbers having period-8 2-digitized sequences.
Record (maximal) gaps between prime 5-tuples (p, p+4, p+6, p+10, p+12).
Record (maximal) gaps between prime 5-tuples (p, p+2, p+6, p+8, p+12).
A Fibonacci-Catalan triangle. Also called the Fibonacci triangle.
Coefficient triangle for the monic associated Laguerre-Sonin(e) polynomials of order one for parameter alpha=1.
Record (maximal) gaps between prime septuplets (p, p+2, p+6, p+8, p+12, p+18, p+20).
Record (maximal) gaps between prime septuplets (p, p+2, p+8, p+12, p+14, p+18, p+20).
Record (maximal) gaps between prime triples (p, p+4, p+6).
Record (maximal) gaps between prime triples (p, p+2, p+6).
Triangle, read by rows, where the g.f. of row n equals Product_{k=0..n-1} (1 + k*y + y^2) for n>0 with a single '1' in row 0.
Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct positive numbers with the property that every positive integer is a sum of distinct terms (see algorithm below).
Coefficients of a generalized Pell-Lucas polynomial read by rows.
Exponential generating function A(x) is the unique solution of the Cauchy problem: A'(x) = exp(x+A(x)^2-1), A(0) = 1.
Triangle defined by g.f.: A(x,y) = exp( Sum_{n>=1} x^n/n * Sum_{k=0..n} binomial(n, k)^n * y^k ), as read by rows.
Number of ways of writing n as a sum of 8 squares.
Theta series of direct sum of 2 copies of hexagonal lattice.
Theta series of direct sum of 4 copies of hexagonal lattice.
Expansion of phi(x^3)^3/phi(x) where phi() is a Ramanujan theta function.
Expansion of psi(-q)^3 / psi(-q^3) in powers of q where psi() is a Ramanujan theta function.
Number of solutions to a^2 + b^2 + 3*c^2 + 3*d^2 = n.
Expansion of phi(-q)^3 / phi(-q^3) in powers of q where phi() is a Ramanujan theta function.
Expansion of eta(q)^9 / eta(q^3)^3 in powers of q.
Coefficients in expansion of theta_3(q) * theta_3(q^7) in powers of q.
Expansion of (theta_3(q) * theta_3(q^7) + theta_2(q) * theta_2(q^7))^2 in powers of q.
Total area of the shadows of the three views of a three-dimensional version of the modular table of partitions with n sections.
Sum of the eight nearest neighbors of n in a right triangular type-1 spiral with positive integers.
Sum of the eight nearest neighbors of n in a right triangular type-2 spiral with positive integers.
Sum of the eight nearest neighbors of n in a right triangular type-3 spiral with positive integers.
Sum of the eight nearest neighbors of n in a triangular 'horizontal-first' spiral with positive integers.
Sum of the eight nearest neighbors of n in a triangular horizontal-last spiral with positive integers.
Length of shortest computation yielding n using addition, subtraction and multiplication (starting from 1).
Smallest number not yet in the sequence greater than n+1 and relatively prime to n.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of n^k contains two consecutive identical digits.
Triangle read by rows, arising in enumeration of permutations by cyclic valleys, cycles and fixed points.
Numbers of the form 2^r * 7^s whose decimal representation has a prime number of each digit 0-9.
Numbers of the form 3^r * 5^s whose decimal representation has a prime number of each digit 0-9.
Numbers of the form 3^r*7^s whose decimal representations are such that each digit 0-9 appears a prime number of times.
Numbers of the form 2^r*11^s whose decimal representations are such that each digit 0-9 appears a prime number of times.
Numbers of the form 2^r*13^s whose decimal representations are such that each digit 0-9 appears a prime number of times.
Numbers of the form 2^r*17^s whose decimal representations are such that each digit 0-9 appears a prime number of times.
Numbers of the form 5^r*7^s whose decimal representations are such that each digit 0-9 appears a prime number of times.
Numbers of the form 2^r*19^s whose decimal representation contains each digit 0-9 a prime number of times.
Numbers of the form 3^r*13^s whose decimal representation has a prime number of copies of each digit 0-9.
Theta series of diamond.
Theta series of diamond with respect to midpoint of edge.
Theta series of diamond with respect to deep hole.
A smoothed version of A091587.
Difference between the n-th and the first (identity) permutation of (0,...,m-1), interpreted as a decimal number, divided by 9 (for any m for which 10! >= m! >= n).
Bases of plain and extended interbase translation of 234099253 to a new prime number in base 10.
Increasing gaps between semiprimes.
Table of figurate numbers for the n-dimensional cross polytopes.
D-toothpick sequence of the third kind starting with a cross formed by 4 toothpicks.
a(n) = maximal value of the sum of Mobius function values over a block of n consecutive natural numbers.
The greatest common divisor of Landau g(n) and n.
Number of daughters to wait before picking in sultan's dowry problem with n daughters.

a(1) = greatest k such that H(k) - H(2) < 1/1 + 1/2; a(2) = greatest k such that H(k) - H(a(1)) < H(a(1)) - H(2); and for n>2, a(n) = greatest k such that H(k) - H(a(n-1)) < H(a(n-1)) - H(a(n-2)), where H = harmonic number.
a(n) is the minimum prime (or 1) needed to write integer n into the form n = a + b such that all prime factors of a and b are smaller or equal to a(n).
a(0) = 0; for n>0, a(n) = denominator(1/4 - 4/n^2).
Integer nearest n * e, where e is the natural log base.

Irregular array read by rows: A(n,k) = number of first coronas of a fixed rhombus r_{n,k} with characteristics of n-fold rotational symmetry in the Euclidean plane, n>=2, 1<=k<=floor(n/2), as explained below.
Sum of remainders of n modulo all smaller composite numbers.
Lonely numbers: distance to closest prime sets a new record.
In balanced ternary notation, if prepending same numbers of zeros, reverse digits of a(n) equals to -a(n).
In balanced ternary notation, either a palindrome or becomes a palindrome if trailing 0's are omitted.
R(n) - prime(2n), where R(n) is the n-th Ramanujan prime and prime(n) is the n-th prime.
Array read by antidiagonals upwards: T(n,k) (n>=1, k>=1) is the solution to the (n,k) stick problem.
Number of toothpicks and D-toothpicks after n-th stage in a D-toothpick 'wide' triangle (see Comments lines for definition).
Toothpick sequence on hexagonal net starting from the vertex of a 60-degree wedge (see Comments lines for precise definition).
Prime p with prime gap q - p of n-th record merit, where q is smallest prime larger than p and the merit of a prime gap is (q-p)/log(p).
Irregular table enumerating partitions; n-th row has partitions in previous row with each part incremented, followed by partitions in previous row with an additional part of size 1.
A pseudo-random sequence.
Irregular triangle read by rows in which row n lists the parts of the symmetric representation of sigma(n).
Number of compositions of n such that no two adjacent parts are equal (these are sometimes called Carlitz compositions).
Triangle T00, T10, T01, T20, T11, T02, etc., where Tmn = number of distinct products ij with min(m,n) <= i,j <= max(m,n).
Number of primes with odd exponents in the prime power factorization of n!.
Anti-Fibonacci numbers: start with a(0) = 0, and extend by the rule that the next term is the sum of the two smallest numbers that are not in the sequence nor were used to form an earlier sum.
a(1)=1, a(2)=2; thereafter a(n) = a(n-1-(number of even terms so far)) + a(n-1-(number of odd terms so far)).
a(1)=1, a(2)=2; thereafter a(n) = a(n-1) + a(n-1-(number of even terms so far)) + a(n-1-(number of odd terms so far)).
Triangular array:  Row n shows the coefficients of polynomials p(n,x) defined in Comments.
Number of trailing equal digits in binary representation of n.
Hexanacci numbers with a(0) = ... = a(5) = 1.
Prime numbers n such that 2^n-1 can be written in the form a^2+7*b^2.
Numbers of form x^2 + 7y^2.
Numbers k whose base 3 expansion matches (0|1)*(02)?(0|1)* (no more than one '02' allowed in midst of 0's and 1's).
Number of primes in the interval [prime(n), prime(n)^2].
Multiples of 7 coprime to 30.
Powers of 7: a(n) = 7^n.
a(n) + a(n+1) is never prime; lexicographically earliest such sequence of distinct positive integers.
A 10th-order Fibonacci sequence.
Decimal expansion of Sum_{i >= 0} (i!)^2/(2*i+1)!.
10th-order Fibonacci numbers: a(n+1) = a(n)+...+a(n-9) with a(0) = ... = a(8) = 0, a(9) = 1.
a(1)=1. a(n) = the smallest positive integer not occurring earlier such that a(n)-a(n-1) doesn't equal a(k)-a(k-1) for any k with 2 <= k <= n-1.
a(1)=5, q=a(n) is the smallest prime > a(n-1) such that q-2*n = p prime.
Prime powers p^m with p <= m.

Permutation of nonnegative integers obtained by traversing the tendrils (finite side-trees) of the binary beanstalk in depth-first order, with also each number in the infinite trunk visited, but only after its sister branch has been traversed first.
Sequence (a(n)) generated by Rule 3 (in Comments) with a(1) = 0 and d(1) = 1.
An 11th-order Fibonacci sequence: a(n) = a(n-1) + ... + a(n-11).
Diagonals of Pascal's triangle mod 2 interpreted as binary numbers.
List of binary palindromes of even length (written in base 10).
Crandall numbers: (2/Pi)^4 Integral_{t>=0} ([Pi I_0(t)]^2 - [K_0(t)]^2) I_0(t) [K_0(t)]^5 (2t)^(2n-1) dt.
Number of positive solutions to the equation A x B = C, where A, B and C are made from (contiguous) substrings of the binary representation of n.
Spiro-Fibonacci numbers, a(n) = sum of two previous terms that are nearest when terms arranged in a spiral.
Repeatedly perform x^2 -> x+1 reduction for polynomial (with nonnegative integer coefficients) encoded in prime factorization of n, until the polynomial is at most degree 1.
Numbers in order in which they appear in Pascal's triangle.
Numbers that are the sum of 2 nonzero squares in 2 or more ways.
Number of solutions to the congruence y^2 == x^3 + x^2 + 4*x + 4 (mod p) as p runs through the primes.
Coefficient table for Chebyshev polynomials T(2*n,x) (increasing even powers x, without zeros).
Multiplicative with a(p^e) = p^(e XOR 2e), where XOR is bitwise-xor.
Numbers that are a product of distinct Lucas numbers (1,3,4,7,11,...)
Sum of numbers <= n which have common prime factors with n.
Product of numbers <= n that have a prime factor in common with n.
a(n+1) = a(n-a(n)) if a(n-1) < a(n), otherwise a(n+1) = 2*a(n); a(1) = a(2) = 1.
a(n) = (2*n-1)! * [x^(2*n-1)] S(x), where S(x) = Integral (1 + S(x)^2)^2 dx.
Least positive integer m with pi(m*n) = m + n, where pi(x) denotes the number of primes not exceeding x.
E.g.f. C(x) satisfies C(x) = cosh( Integral C(x)^4 dx ).
Expansion of Product_{k>=1} 1/(1+x^k)^(k^2) in powers of x.
Smallest number k such that (k+1)^n - k^n is divisible by a square greater than 1.
Period 3: repeat [0, 1, 1].
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->001, 10->011, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->001, 10->100, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->010, 10->000, starting with 00.
Write n = m^k with m, k integers, k >= 1, then a(n) is the smallest possible choice for m.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->010, 10->001, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->010, 10->011, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->010, 10->100, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->011, 10->100, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->011, 10->000, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->011, 10->001, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->011, 10->010, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->100, 10->011, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->100, 10->010, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->0010, 01->100, 10->100, starting with 00.
a(n) = Catalan(n) - n.
Catalan numbers minus 2.
Expansion of 1/(x + sqrt(1-4x)).
The first of a pair of coprime numbers whose factorizations depend on the ternary representation of n (see Comments for precise definition).
The second of a pair of coprime numbers whose factorizations depend on the ternary representation of n (See Comments for precise definition).
a(n) = binomial(n,3) mod n.
Prime exponents of composite Mersenne numbers.
Solution of the complementary equation a(n) = 2*a(n-1) + a(n-2) - b(n), where a(0) = 3, a(1) = 5, b(0) = 1, b(1) = 2, b(2) = 4, and (a(n)) and (b(n)) are increasing complementary sequences.
a(1)=0, n-1 if n is prime, else largest proper divisor of n.
Triangle T(n,k) (n>=0, 0<=k<=n) read by rows: use T(n,k)=T(n,k-1)+T(n-1,k-1) rule except left edge is the sequence read by rows, initial values are T(0,0)=T(1,0)=1.
Triangle T(n,k) (n>=0, 0<=k<=n) read by rows: use T(n,k)=T(n,k-1)+T(n-1,k-1) rule except left edge is the sequence read by rows, initial values are T(0,0)=0, T(1,0)=1.
Concatenation of first n binary numbers.

Solution (a(n)) of the near-complementary equation a(n) = a(1)*b(n-1) - a(0)*b(n-2) + n, where a(0) = 1, a(1) = 2, b(0) = 3, b(1) = 4, and (b(n)) is the increasing sequence of positive integers not in (a(n)).  See Comments.
Long legs of primitive Pythagorean triangles sorted on semiperimeter.
Short leg of primitive Pythagorean triangles sorted on semiperimeter.
Wieferich primes: primes p such that p^2 divides 2^(p-1) - 1.
a(n) is the number of possible values of (x^3 + y^3) mod n, where x and y are any integers.
Squarefree values of n for which the quadratic field Q[ sqrt(n) ] is norm-Euclidean.
Number of elements in the continued fraction for prime(n+1)/prime(n).
Primes p such that p^2 divides 5^(p-1) - 1.
In primorial base: a(n) is obtained by replacing each nonzero digit of n with its product with the nonzero digits at lower indices (See Comments for precise definition).
Fixed point of the morphism 0->120, 1->110, 2->100.
a(n) = least natural number with the same prime signature Stern polynomial B(n,x) has when it is factored over Z.
Theta series of Leech lattice.
Filter sequence for the prime signature of 2n-1.
Difference between leg and hypotenuse in primitive Pythagorean triangles.
Irregular triangle T with the nontrivial solutions of 2*e2 + 3*e3 = n, for n >= 2, with nonnegative e2 and e3, ordered as pairs with increasing e2 values.
Square array read by ascending antidiagonals, A(n, k) for n >= 0 and k >= 0, related to a class of Motzkin trees.
Numbers n > 1 such that gcd(n, 2^n - 2) = 1.
a(n) is the maximum number of distinct directions between n non-attacking rooks on an n X n chessboard.
a(n) is twice the least possible area enclosed by a convex lattice n-gon.

Least q > 1 letting Josephus survive if he finds himself at position j in the circle of m persons, but is allowed to name the elimination parameter q such that every q-th person is executed, written as triangle T(m,j), m > 1, j <= m.
a(n) is the number of k with 1 < k < sqrt(n) such that n mod k^2 is prime.
Euler-Jacobi pseudoprimes: 2^((n-1)/2) == (2 / n) mod n, where (2 / n) is a Jacobi symbol.
a(n) is the least positive number which yields a multiple of n when its decimal digits (which are necessarily 0's and 1's) are read in any base.
Product of such primes p that both p and p-2 divide n, and p-2 is also prime.
Divide n by the largest factorial that divides it and repeat until an odd number is reached, which will be the result; a(0) = 0.
Smallest positive number of maximal order mod n.
Decimal expansion of sqrt(4 + sqrt(4 + sqrt(4 + sqrt(4 + ... )))).
Smallest prime factor of number of divisors of n; a(1) = 1.
Centered tetrahedral numbers.
Binary hoax numbers: composite numbers k such that sum of bits of k equals the sum of bits of the distinct prime divisors of k.
a(n) is the smallest q such that the primes<=q generate the multiplicative group modulo n.
a(n) is the determinant of the 2 X 2 matrix whose entries (when read by rows) are the n-th primes congruent to 1, 3, 5, 7 mod 8 respectively.
If n is composite, a(n) is the number represented by the list of prime factors of n (with multiplicity, sorted in nondecreasing order) in base the sum of that list.  If n is prime, a(n) = n.
Numbers m that divide 2^k + 1 for some nonnegative k.
Maximum sum of elements of an n X n matrix filled with numbers such that if a(j,k)=i, then all numbers 1 ... i-1 are represented in (a(j-1,k), a(j+1,k), a(j,k-1), a(j,k+1)).
Numbers whose divisors can be partitioned in exactly one way into two disjoint sets with the same sum.
Fecundity of n.
Number of representations of n as a sum of distinct Fibonacci numbers.
Palindromes having more divisors than all smaller palindromes.
a(n) is obtained by replacing 2^k in binary expansion of n with Fibonacci(-k-2).
Primes of the form 4*k+3 with primitive root -2.
Euclid-Pocklington primes: primes of the form Product_{i=1..k} prime(i) * prime(k+1)^m + 1 where prime(r) is the r-th prime and Product_{i=1..k} prime(i) < prime(k+1)^m.
Table read by upward antidiagonals: Given m, n >= 1, write gcd(m,n) as d = u*m+v*n where u, v are minimal; T(m,n) = u.
Maximum element in the simple continued fraction expansion of H(n) = 1+1/2+1/3+...+1/n, the n-th harmonic number.
Pairs (i,j) of positive integers with at least one common 1-bit sorted first by i+j then by i.
Fractalization of Kimberling's paraphrase of the binary number system beginning with 1.
'Even' fractal sequence for the natural numbers: Deleting every even-indexed term results in the same sequence.
Numbers with as many even as odd prime indices, counted with multiplicity.
Numbers whose abundancy index is larger than Pi^2/6.
Multiplicative with a(p^e) = phi(sigma(p^e)).
Multiplicative with a(p^e) = ((p-1)*q)^e, where q is the largest prime less than p, and 1 if p = 2.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers with no finite subset summing to a power of 2.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers with no finite subset summing to a positive Fibonacci number.
Number of cubefree divisors of n.
Number of k < n such that gcd(k, n) > 1, gcd(n^2-1, k) = 1, and rad(k) does not divide n.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that the sums Sum_{i = 1+k*2^e..(k+1)*2^e} a(i) with k, e >= 0 are all distinct.
Triangle read by rows where row n is a self-inverse permutation of 1..n formed starting from a column 1..n and sliding numbers to the right and down.
Sierpinski triangle read by rows and filled in the greedy way such that each row, each diagonal and each antidiagonal contains distinct nonnegative values.
Concatenate 1 once, 2 twice, 3 three times, up to n n times.
Decimal expansion of the solution to 127^x - 113^x = 1. This is the smallest known x such that q^x - p^x = 1 for two successive primes p, q.
Numbers whose binary expansion is an abelian square.
Number of representations of n as a sum (p*q + p*r + q*r) with three odd primes p <= q <= r.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number such that a(n) - a(n-1) = sopfr(a(n)) + sopfr(a(n-1)), where sopfr(k) is the sum of the primes dividing k, with repetition.
Expansion of e.g.f. 1/(1 + exp(x) - exp(3*x)).
Array read by antidiagonals downward where A(n,k) is the n-th term of the k-th differences of the squarefree numbers.
Array read by downward antidiagonals where A(n,k) is the n-th term of the k-th differences of nonsquarefree numbers.
Array read by antidiagonals downward where A(n,k) is the n-th term of the k-th differences of the powers of primes.

Asymptotic phase shift of the tetration base n written by juxtaposing its representative congruence classes modulo 10 (i.e., the 1, 2, or 4, distinct sfasamenti taken by starting from the minimum height such that the congruence speed of n is constant), and a(n) = -1 if n is a multiple of 10.
a(n) = n^2*Product_{p|n} (1 + 1/p).

Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) (0 <= n, 0 <= k < 2^n). An infinite binary tree with root node 0 in row n = 0. Each node then has left child (2*j) - k - 1 and right child (2*j) - k + 1, where j and k are the values of the parent and grandparent nodes respectively.
Number of polycubes of size n and symmetry class G (full symmetry).
a(n) = 2^(k+1) where 2^k is the highest power of 2 dividing n.
a(n) is the n-th self-number minus n.
Square array T(n, k) read by rising antidiagonals. Row n has the ordinary generating function (-(n*x^3-(n+1)*x^2+x) + sqrt((n*x^3-(n+1)*x^2+x)^2 - 4*(x^3-x^2)*((n+1)*x^2-x)))/(2*(x^3-x^2)).
Decimal expansion of the smallest positive real root of the equation cos(x) + x*sin(x) = 0.
Primes p such that the multiplicative order of 2 modulo p is (p-1)/2.
Array read by ascending antidiagonals: A(n, k) = Sum_{j = 0..k} binomial(k, j) * Euler(j, 0) *(2*n)^j.
Numbers k such that max{d|k, d <= sqrt(k)} + min{d|k, d >= sqrt(k)} is a square.
Least lucky multiple of 2*n+1, or 0 if no such multiple exists.
Least ludic multiple of n, or 0 if no such multiple exists.
a(1)=1, a(n+1) = p(n)^2 + q(n)^2 + 1, where p(n) and q(n) are the number of prime and nonprime numbers respectively in the sequence so far.
Number of ways to write n as a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d, where a,b,c,d are nonnegative integers with a <= b.
a(n) is the smallest positive integer k such that n*k uses none of the digits of n, or 0 if no such k exists.
The number of divisors d of n such that d^d == d (mod n).
Values of u in the quartets (2,u,v,w); i.e., values of u for solutions to 2*(2+u) = v*(v+w), in positive integers, with and v>m, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
The u sequence in quartets (3,u,v,w); i.e., values of u for solutions to 3*(3+u) = v*(v+w), in positive integers, with u,v>=3 and u>=m, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
Exponent of 2 in 3^n - 1.
Values of u in the quartets (1, u, v, w) of type 2; i.e., values of u for solutions to (1 + u) =  v(v - w), in positive integers, with v > 1, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
Table read by rows: row n gives list of lengths of runs of 1's in binary expansion of n, starting with low-order bits.

a(n) = denominator q of the fraction p/q that minimizes |m/n - p/q | with m/n != p/q, where p is 1 or prime, q is prime, q < n, and m ranges from 1 to n - 1, with this rule to ensure uniqueness: if for given n there is more than one minimizing triple (m, p, q), then choose the least such m, then least q, then least p.

Sequence of the short legs of primitive Pythagorean triples beginning with the triple (3,4,5), with each subsequent triple having as its short leg the sum of the legs of the previous triple, and with the long leg and the hypotenuse of each triple being consecutive natural numbers.
Number of lattice points inside the ball x^2 + y^2 + z^2 <= n.
Numbers that can be written as s_1^x_1 + ... + s_t^x_t, with 0 < s_1 < ... < s_t and x_1 > ... > x_t > 1 for some t > 0, with the restriction that if s_1 = 1 then x_1 is the least possible.

Middle sides y for integer-sided triangles (x <= y <= z) with an integer internal angle bisector l splitting the triangle into two integer-sided triangles; include only tuples (x, y, z; l) with gcd(x, y, z, l) = 1; ordered by z, then y, then x.

Shortest sides x for integer-sided triangles (x <= y <= z) with an integer internal angle bisector l splitting the triangle into two integer-sided triangles; include only tuples (x, y, z; l) with gcd(x, y, z, l) = 1; ordered by z, then y, then x.

Longest sides z for integer-sided triangles (x <= y <= z) with an integer internal angle bisector l splitting the triangle into two integer-sided triangles; include only tuples (x, y, z; l) with gcd(x, y, z, l) = 1; ordered by z, then y, then x.

Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = Sum_{i=0..k} Legendre(i,prime(n)).
Periodic sequence 0,1,1,0,-1,-1,...
Number of connected transitive trivalent (or cubic) graphs with 2n nodes.
a(n) = solution to the postage stamp problem with n denominations and 2 stamps.

Sequence (or tree) T of primes generated by these rules: 2 is in T; if p is in T, then the greatest prime < 2*p is in T; if p is in T, then the least prime > 2*p is in T; duplicates are deleted as they occur.
Nonprime numbers of the form 2^n - 1.
a(1)=1. a(n)=smallest integer greater than 2*a(n-1) such that the Nim sequence of the first n terms is ternary, periodic and not equal to the Nim sequence of the first n-1 terms.
Reduced division polynomials associated with elliptic curve y^2 + x*y = x^3 - x^2 - x + 1 and multiples of point (0, 1).
Binary representation of periodic binary numbers, ordered by their decimal values.
Integers c, listed with multiplicity, such that there is a solution to the equation a^2 + b^3 = c^4, with integers a, b > 0.
a(1) = 252, a(n) is a(n-1) multiplied by the smallest prime factor of a(n-1)+1.
a(n) = ((n*(n+1)/2) mod n + sigma(n) mod n + antisigma(n) mod n) / n.
a(n) = (n*(n+1)/2) mod n + sigma(n) mod n + antisigma(n) mod n.
Lesser of twin primes p1 and p2 such that 2*p1+p2 is a prime number.
Decimal expansion of the continued fraction prime(1) + prime(1)/(prime(2) + prime(2)/(prime(3) + prime(3)/(prime(4) + prime(4)/...))).
Number of formula representations of n using addition, multiplication and the constant 1.
Let Cn(x) be the n-th cyclotomic polynomial; a(n) is the least k>1 such that Cn(k) is prime.

Calculate the smallest positive residues of 2!,3!,...,(prime(n)-1)! modulo prime(n) and stop the calculation at the moment m when for the first time there appear two equal numbers. If m!==k!, then a(n)=k; but a(n)=0 if no such m exists.
a(n) is the square of the product of first n primes.
Sequence (d(n)) generated by Rule 3 (in Comments) with a(1) = 1 and d(1) = 0.
a(n) is the smallest prime different from a(k) for k < n such that sum(a(j), j=1..n) is a multiple of the n-th prime.
Irregular triangle read by rows: Stifel's version of the arithmetical triangle.

A(n,k) is the sum over all Motzkin paths of length n of products over all peaks p of (x_p+k*y_p)/y_p, where x_p and y_p are the coordinates of peak p; square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals.

A(n,k) is the sum over all Motzkin paths of length n of products over all peaks p of (k*x_p+y_p)/y_p, where x_p and y_p are the coordinates of peak p; square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals.
Arithmetic derivative of Pascal's triangle.
Smallest multiple of 7 not appearing earlier that ends with n.
Smallest multiple of 7 starting with n, that did not appear earlier.
Starting with the positive numbers, each element subtracts its value, a(n), from the next a(n) elements.
With a(1) = 1, a(n) is the smallest number not already in the sequence such that a(n)^2 + a(n-1)^2 is not squarefree.
a(n) is the sum of all numbers k for which sigma(k) = n.
McKay-Thompson series of class 18b for the Monster group.
Number of numbers whose divisors sum to n.
Palindromes in which the digits are in nondecreasing order halfway through.
Lexicographically smallest permutation of natural numbers such that in binary representation the number of ones of adjacent terms differ exactly by one.
Numbers with nonzero digits whose sum of digits as well as product of digits is a palindrome.
a(n) = a(floor(n/2)) + a(floor(n/4)) + a(floor(n/8)) + ... starting with a(0)=0 and a(1)=1.
Minimal difference between the smallest and largest of n consecutive large primes that form a symmetric n-tuplet as permitted by divisibility considerations.
Number of ON cells after n generations of the cellular automaton on the square grid that is described in the Comments.
Smallest span (difference between the start and end) of a symmetric n-tuple of consecutive primes.
Least prime p such that p-2 and 6n-p are also prime, or 0 if no such prime exists.
Triangular array read by rows: g(n,k) = 1 for n >= 0; g(n,k) = 0 if k > n; g(n,k) = g(n-1,k-1) + g(n-1,3k) for n > 0, k > 1.
Triangular array read by rows: g(n,k) = 1 for n >= 0; g(n,k) = 0 if k > n; g(n,k) = g(n-1,k-1) + g(n-1,4k) for n > 0, k > 1.
Numbers n = p_1^s_1...p_m^s_m such that (p_i^s_i - 1) | n for all 0<i<=m.
Square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals upwards, where A(n,k) = k! * [x^k] W_n(x) and W_n(x) = W_{n-1}(x)^W_n(x), with W_0(x) = exp(x).
Glaisher's chi numbers chi(p) for p a prime of the form 4m+1.
Primes p for which the period of 1/p is a power of 2.
a(n) is the minimal sum of a positive integer sequence of length n with no duplicate substrings of length greater than 1.
Oscillating orbitals over n sectors (nonpositive values indicating there exist none).
Smallest k such that (n+1)^k - n^k is divisible by a square > 1.
Numbers k such that 2^k + 1 is divisible by a square > 1.
Numbers n such that 10^n+1 is not squarefree.
a(n) is the smallest m with gcd(m, 2*n+1) = 1 such that 2*n + 2*m + 1 is composite.
Numbers n such that 2^n - 1 is not squarefree, but 2^d - 1 is squarefree for every proper divisor d of n.
Numbers k such that 3^k - 2^k is not squarefree.
Generalized Pascal triangle based on Zeckendorf representation of numbers, read by rows.
Base-2 generalized Pascal triangle P_2 read by rows (see Comments for precise definition).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct terms such that a(n)=length of first run of multiples of prime(n) in this sequence.
Numbers n such that 3^n - 2^n is not squarefree, but 3^d - 2^d is squarefree for all proper divisors d of n.
Number of partitions of n into even parts.
Decimal expansion of Pi rounded to n places.
a(n) is the largest even number k such that 6, 8, ..., k are sums of 2 of first n odd primes.
a(n) = Sum_{0 < a, b <= n and gcd(a^2 + b^2, n) = 1} (a + bi)^n  (mod n).
Numbers that contain primes to odd powers only.
Expansion of elliptic modular function lambda in powers of the nome q.
Primes together with primes multiplied by 2.

E.g.f. W = W(x,m) satisfies: W = E(x*W,m) where E(x,m) = cn(i*x,m) - i*sn(i*x,m), with sn(x,m) and cn(x,m) being Jacobi elliptic functions, read as an irregular triangle of coefficients T(n,k) of x^n*m^k for n>=0 and k=0..[n/2].
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) is the Sheffer triangle ((1 - 3*x)^(-1/3), (-1/3)*log(1 - 3*x)). A generalized Stirling1 triangle.
Smallest m such that b^m == b^n (mod n) for every integer b.
Smallest m such that 2^m == 2^n (mod n).
Solution of the complementary equation a(n) = a(n-1) + a(n-2) + b(n) + 2*n, where a(0) = 1, a(1) = 3, b(0) = 2, b(1) = 4, b(2) = 5, and (a(n)) and (b(n)) are increasing complementary sequences.

Solution b( ) of the complementary equation a(n) = a(0)*b(n) + a(1)*b(n-1), where a(0) = 1, a(1) = 2, b(0) = 3, b(1) = 4, b(2) = 5, and (b(n)) is the increasing sequence of positive integers not in (a(n)). See Comments.
a(n) is the minimal number k such that every binary word of length n can be divided into k palindromes.

a(n) is the number of distinct primes produced by starting with the n-th prime p and repeatedly looking at all the prime factors of 2p+1, and then performing the same process (double, add 1, find all prime factors) with those primes; a(n) = -1 if this produces infinitely many primes.
Numbers k whose divisors can be partitioned into three disjoint sets whose sums are all sigma(k)/3.
Number of distinct prime signatures arising among the divisors of n.
Primary Carmichael numbers.
Number of cyclic subgroups of the group C_n X C_n (where C_n is the cyclic group of order n).
Perrin sequence of order 5.
Sum of even squarefree divisors of n.

E.g.f.: A(x,y) = (cosh(x)*cosh(y) + sinh(x) + sinh(y)) / (1 - sinh(x)*sinh(y)), where A(x,y) = Sum_{n>=0} Sum_{k>=0} T(n,k) * x^n*y^k/(n!*k!), as a square table of coefficients T(n,k) read by antidiagonals.

L.g.f.: L(x,y) = log( Product_{n>=1} 1/(1 - (x^n + y^n)) ), where L(x,y) = Sum_{n>=0} Sum_{k>=0} T(n,k) * x^n*y^k / (n+k) such that L(0,0) = 0, as a symmetric square table of coefficients T(n,k) read by antidiagonals starting with T(0,0) = 0.

E.g.f. S(x,y) = Integral C(x,y)*C(y,x) dx such that C(x,y)^2 - S(x,y)^2 = 1 and C(y,x) = 1 + Integral S(y,x)*C(x,y) dy, where S(x,y) = Sum_{n>=0} Sum_{k=0..n} T(n,k) * x^(2*n+1-2*k)*y^(2*k)/((2*n+1-2*k)!*(2*k)!), as a triangle of coefficients T(n,k) read by rows.
G.f.: 1/(1-2x-15x^2)^(1/2); also, a(n) is the central coefficient of (1+x+4x^2)^n.
Greatest k such that 6^k divides n.
a(n) = Sum_{d|n} bigomega(d)*bigomega(n/d).
Truncated triangular numbers (of form n*(n-3)/2 - k^2+k*n+1 for 1<=k<n).
Heptagonal (or 7-gonal) pyramidal numbers: a(n) = n*(n+1)*(5*n-2)/6.
Expansion of 1/sqrt(1 - 10*x + x^2).
a(n) = P_n(7), where P_n is n-th Legendre polynomial; also, a(n) = central coefficient of (1 + 7*x + 12*x^2)^n.
Table read by antidiagonals: T(n, k) is the number of elements on the perimeter of an n X k matrix.
Add the odd terms and subtract the even ones, the result must always be a palindrome in base 3. This is the lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers with this property.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the product a(n)*a(n+1) is 'doubly true' (see the Comments section).
a(1) = 0, and for any n > 0, a(2*n) = a(n) + k(n) and a(2*n+1) = a(n) - k(n) where k(n) is the least positive integer not leading to a duplicate term in sequence a.
In base 2: numbers n of the form k + reverse(k) for at least one k.
Square array read by antidiagonals: Write n and m in binary with n on the left. Concatenate. a(n,m) is the decimal equivalent of the result.

Boustrophedon primes: write the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, ... in a triangle on a square grid in the boustrophedon manner, ending a row when a prime is reached; sequence lists primes that appear in the zeroth column.
Number of distinct cubic residues mod n.
The least prime factor of the numerator of Bernoulli(2*n), or 1 if the numerator is 1.
First occurrences of gaps between primes 6k+1: gap sizes.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,d) is the number of distinct properly d-dimensional polyominoes (or polycubes) with n cells (n >= 1, d >= 0).
a(n) = 6*a(n-1) + a(n-2), starting with a(0)=2 and a(1)=6.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers with the property that, for all k > 0, there is at most one j such that a(j) = a(j+k).
a(n) = Sum_{i=1..n-1} (prime(i)^2 mod prime(n)).
a(n) is the least k >= 2 such that (n+1)^k mod n^j is a perfect power > 1 for some j >= 2 with n^j < (n+1)^k.

a(n) is the number of divisors of n such that the ratio (the number of nonnegative m < n such that m^d == m (mod n))/(the number of nonnegative m < n such that -m^d == m (mod n)) is also a divisor of n.
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; for n>2, a(n) is the smallest number not already used which is a multiple of the product of the most frequently occurring distinct prime factors in a(n-1).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any n >= 0, n AND a(n) is a square (where AND denotes the bitwise AND operator).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative terms such that for any n >= 0, a(n) AND a(n+1) is a square (where AND denotes the bitwise AND operator).
a(n) = prime(n+2)*prime(n+3)-prime(n)*prime(n+1).
Difference between n and the next prime greater than n.
a(n) is the number of squares dividing n.
The maximum number of times a positive number can be added to n such that the digits in each resulting sum are distinct.
Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k), n >= 1, k >= 1, in which column k lists the odd numbers k times, and the first element of column k is in row k(k+1)/2.
Number of ordered factorizations of n into decimal palindromes > 1.
a(n) is the denominator of the average number of distinct prime factors of the divisors of n.
a(n) is the numerator of the average number of distinct prime factors of the divisors of n.
Super least prime signatures; LCM of all signatures with n factors.
a(n) = (3/2)*a(n-1) if a(n-1) is even; (3/2)*(a(n-1)+1) if a(n-1) is odd.
Positive integers k that are the product of two integers ending with 6.
a(n) is the least common multiple of the divisors d of n-1 such that d+1 is prime; a(1) = 1.
Positive integers k that are the product of two integers greater than 1 and ending with 1.
Lesser emirps (primes whose digit reversal is a larger prime).
Positive integers k that are the product of two integers ending with 3.
Record numbers of grid points in a square lattice covered by a continuously growing circular disk if the center of the disk is chosen to cover the maximum possible number of grid points.
Numbers k that divide 4^k + 3^k.
Triangle read by rows. The Faulhaber numbers. F(0, k) = 1 and otherwise F(n, k) = (n + 1)!*(-1)^(k+1)*Sum_{j=0..floor((k-1)/2)} C(2*k-2*j, k+1)*C(2*n+1, 2*j+1) * Bernoulli(2*n-2*j) / (k - j).
The canonical skew-binary numbers.
Fully multiplicative prime shift where the primes of the form 3k+2 are replaced by the previous such prime (with 2 -> 1), and primes of the form 3k and 3k+1 stay as they are.
Product of the distinct primes dividing the product of composite numbers between consecutive primes.
a(n) is the smallest k such that there exists a degree-k primitive Dirichlet characters modulo n, or -1 no such k exists.
Primes p such that (p+1)/2 is prime.
Multiplicative with p^e -> primorial(e), p prime and e > 0.
Triangle read by rows. The Bell transform of the sequence {m^m | m >= 0}.
a(n) = Sum_{i=1..n} (prime(i+n) mod prime(i)).
Point number on a 4-arm square spiral of point n on the East arm scaled up by steps of that point itself.
Pairs (i, j) of nonnegative integers whose ternary expansions have no common digit 1 sorted first by i + j then by i.
Pairs (i, j) of nonnegative integers whose ternary expansions have a common digit 1 sorted first by i + j then by i.

The Sydney Opera House sequence: a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1; for n > 0, a(n) = min(a(n-1)/n if n|a(n-1), a(n-1)-n) where a(n) is nonnegative and not already in the sequence. Otherwise a(n) = min(a(n-1)+n, a(n-1)*n) where a(n) is not already in the sequence. Otherwise a(n) = a(n-1) + n.
Products of exactly four distinct primes.

Number of words, either empty or beginning with the first letter of the ternary alphabet, where each letter of the alphabet occurs n times and letters of neighboring word positions are equal or neighbors in the alphabet.
n-th term of the crystal ball sequence for A_{n+1} lattice for n >= 0.

Let P(n) of a sequence s(1),s(2),s(3),... be obtained by leaving s(1),...,s(n) fixed and reversing every n consecutive terms thereafter; apply P(2) to 1,2,3,... to get PS(2), then apply P(3) to PS(2) to get PS(3), then apply P(4) to PS(3), etc. This sequence is the limit of PS(n).
Greatest d such that d*n+b is the least prime in the arithmetic progression k*n+b for some 0 < b < n with gcd(b, n) = 1.
Dispersion of the primes (an array read by downward antidiagonals).
Triangle of coefficients T(n,k) in g.f. A(x,y) satisfying Sum_{n=-oo..+oo} (-1)^n * (x^n + y*A(x,y))^n = 1 + (y+2)*Sum_{n>=1} (-1)^n * x^(n^2), for n >= 1, as read by rows.
Triangle of coefficients T(n,k) in g.f. A(x,y) satisfying Sum_{n=-oo..+oo} (x^n - y*A(x,y))^n = 1 - (y-2)*Sum_{n>=1} x^(n^2), for n >= 1, as read by rows.
Number of the rightmost decimal digits of n^n that are the same as those of n^(n^n).
a(n) = (T(n,n+1) - 1)/n^3 for n >= 1, where T(n,x) is the n-th Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.
Expansion of 1/((1-x)^4*(1+x)).
Numerator of probability to directly sort n uniform random values in [0,1] with perfect strategy.
Denominator of probability to directly sort n uniform random values in [0,1] with perfect strategy.
Blum integers: numbers of the form p * q where p and q are distinct primes congruent to 3 (mod 4).
Numbers with property that if any digit is deleted then the result is divisible by that digit.
a(n) is the largest number that is the digit sum of the square of an n-digit number.
a(n) is the alternating sum of the unitary divisors of n, when these divisors are starting with n and decreasing.
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = (-1)^k*Product_{j=0..k-1} (j - n)*(j + n), for 0 <= k <= n.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the least positive integer not already in the sequence such that a(n) == a(n-1) (mod 2*n-1).
The number of vertices formed when every pair of n points, placed at the vertices of a regular n-gon, are connected by a circle and where the points lie at the ends of the circle's diameter.
a(n) is the smallest even r less than n-1 such that x^r = 1 (mod n) for the least x such that gcd(x,n)=1 for n >= 4 else 0.
Greatest squarefree number <= n.
Smallest squarefree number >= n.

Array read by rows (blocks). Each row is a permutation of a block of consecutive numbers; the blocks are disjoint and every positive number belongs to some block. Row n contains 3n/2 elements if n is even, and (n+1)/2 elements if n is odd; ; see Comments.
Three even followed by one odd.
a(n) is the smallest integer k > n such that sqrt(1/n - 1/k) is a rational number; or 0 if no such k exists.
a(n) is the smallest integer k > n such that sqrt(1/n + 1/k) is a rational number; or 0 if no such k exists.
2nd largest prime factor of n-th composite number.
Discriminant of the minimal polynomial of a number whose continued fraction expansion has periodic part given by the n-th composition (in standard order).
a(n) is the least k > 0 such that (n+k)^2 + n^2 is prime.
Values of u in the quartets (2, u, v, w) of type 2; i.e., values of u for solutions to 2*(2 + u) = v*(v - w), in positive integers, with v > 1, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
If b(m) is the number of 1's in the binary representation of m, then the positive integer m is included if m = k^b(m), for some integer k.
Values of u in the quartets (3, u, v, w) of type 2; i.e., values of u for solutions to 3(3 + u) =  v(v - w), in positive integers, with v > 1, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
Base-2 Reacher numbers: numbers that are powers of the sum of their base-2 digits.
Ordered hypotenuses of Pythagorean triples that do not have the form (u^2 - v^2, 2*u*v, u^2 + v^2), where u and v are positive integers.
Triangle of Euler-Bernoulli or Entringer numbers read by rows.
Triangle read by rows, where row terms are filled depending on divisibility of n. See comments.

Values of u in the quartets (4, u, v, w) of type 2; i.e., values of u for solutions to 4(4 + u) =  v(v - w), in distinct positive integers, with v > 1, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
a(n) = sigma(n)*phi(n) + 1 (mod n).
Ordered hypotenuses of nonprimitive Pythagorean triples of the form (u^2 - v^2, 2*u*v, u^2 + v^2), where u and v are positive integers.
Numbers k such that sopf(k) and k-sopf(k) are prime, where sopf() is the sum of distinct prime factors.
Difference set of Mian-Chowla sequence in order of appearance.

Consider the following process: at step n, draw the line passing through the points (n, prime(n)) and (n+1, prime(n+1)). a(n) gives the total number of distinct single-point line intersections after step n.
Squares visited by knight moves on a diagonally numbered Q1 board and moving to the lowest available unvisited square at each step. Starting square is labeled 1.
a(n) = 1 if n is neither a multiple of 2 nor 3, and otherwise 0.
Largest denominator of greedy Egyptian fraction sum for m/n, 1 <= m <= n-1.

a(n) = denominator q of the fraction p/q that minimizes |m/n - p/q| with m/n != p/q, where p is 1 or prime, q is prime, q < n, and m ranges from 1 to n - 1, with this rule to ensure uniqueness: if for given n there is more than one minimizing triple (m, p, q), then choose the greatest such m, then greatest q, then greatest p.

Squares visited by a knight moving on a square-spiral numbered board, starting from square 1, always moving to the lowest available unvisited square while never crossing the path of any previous step.

Squares visited by a (1,2)-darter moving on a square-spiral numbered board, starting from square 1, always moving to the lowest available unvisited square that can be reached without crossing a square that has been previously visited.
Lucas-Carmichael numbers: squarefree composite numbers k such that p | k => p+1 | k+1.
A linear mapping a(n) = x + d*n of pairs of integers (x,d), where the pairs are enumerated by the counterclockwise square spiral (an axis-parallel number spiral) starting at 0.
Triangular array: T(n,k) is the number of set partitions of [n] into k labeled 3-tori.
Call d a recursive divisor of n iff the p-adic valuation of d is a recursive divisor of the p-adic valuation of n for any prime p dividing d; a(n) gives the number of recursive divisors of n.
a(1)=1. Thereafter, all terms are primes raised to the values of earlier terms of the sequence.
Square array read by ascending antidiagonals: T(n, k) = n * T(n, k-1) + (k mod 2) * T(n-1, k), and T(n, 1) = T(1, k) = 1.
Decimal expansion of the silver mean, 1+sqrt(2).
a(n) is the least product x*y of two integers 2^(n-1) <= x <= y < 2^n maximizing the Hamming weight of this product.
Number of simple graphs on n unlabeled nodes.
Squarefree numbers congruent to 3 mod 4.
Even discriminants of imaginary quadratic fields, negated.
Fully multiplicative with a(p) = [ (p+1)/2 ] for prime p.
Completely multiplicative with a(prime(k)) = floor( (prime(k+1)+1)/2 ) for k-th prime prime(k).
Fully multiplicative with a(prime(k)) = partition(k+1).
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is defined by the property that n^a(n) divides n! but n^(a(n)+1) does not.
Triangle of numbers associated with Genocchi numbers.
Number of rooted polygonal cacti (Husimi graphs) with n nodes.
2 followed by a run of n 1's.
10-factorial numbers.
Triangle read by rows giving number of ways to glue sides of a 2n-gon so as to produce a surface of genus g.
Number of mixed Husimi trees with n nodes; or rooted polygonal cacti with bridges.
Number of asymmetric rooted polygonal cacti with bridges (mixed Husimi trees).
Numbers m such that every k <= m is a sum of proper divisors of m (for m>1).
Shifts 2 places left under binomial transform.
Generalized Stirling number triangle of first kind read by rows: T(n, k) = [x^k] Product_{m=1..n} (x - m - r), with r = 5.
Generalized Stirling number triangle of first kind read by rows: T(n, k) = [x^k] Product_{m=1..n} (x - m - r), with r = 6.
Generalized Stirling number triangle of first kind read by rows: T(n, k) = [x^k] Product_{m=1..n} (x - m - r), with r = 7.
Generalized Stirling number triangle of first kind read by rows: T(n, k) = [x^k] Product_{m=1..n} (x - m - r), with r = 8.
Generalized Stirling number triangle of first kind read by rows: T(n, k) = [x^k] Product_{m=1..n} (x - m - r), with r = 9.
Consider problem of placing N queens on an n X n board so that each queen attacks precisely 2 others. Sequence gives maximal number of queens.
Consider the problem of placing N queens on an n X n board so that each queen attacks precisely 3 others. Sequence gives maximal number of queens.
Smallest number m such that 2*m - p is composite for the first n primes p.
Hadamard maximal determinant problem: largest determinant of (+1,-1)-matrix of order n.
Largest metadrome (number with digits in strict ascending order) in base n.
Riesel problem: start with n; repeatedly double and add 1 until reach a prime. Sequence gives a(n) = prime reached, or 0 if no prime is ever reached.
a(n) = binomial(n, floor((n-1)/2)).
2-boustrophedon transform applied to 1, 0, 0, 0, ...
Triangle of numbers T(n,k) = T(n-1,k-1) + ((n+k-1)/k)*T(n-1,k), n >= 1, 1 <= k <= n, with T(n,1) = n!, T(n,n) = 1; read from right to left.
Array of values of Jordan function J_k(n) read by antidiagonals (version 1).
Triangle T(n,k) (1 <= k <= n) of tangent numbers, read by rows: T(n,k) = coefficient of x^n/n! in expansion of (tan x)^k/k!.
Primes p such that 2p+1 is composite.

Variation of Boustrophedon transform applied to 1,1,1,1,... Fill an array by diagonals, all in the 'up' direction. The first column is 1,1,1,1,.... For the next element of a diagonal, add to the previous element the elements of the row and the column the new element is in. The first row gives a(n).
a(n) = [[(k^2)*n]-(k*[k*n])], where k = sqrt(2) and [] is the floor function.
a(n) = bin_prime_sum(n).
a(n) = |{m : multiplicative order of 2 mod m = n}|.
