Primes that are concatenations of two consecutive primes.
Hilbert curve constructed by greedy algorithm, such that each element is the smallest positive integer possible and that all rows, columns, and diagonals contain distinct numbers.
a(n) = Product_{i=1..n} (10^i - 1).
Primes of form 3*2^k - 1.
The sum (in nondecreasing order) of the two numbers in an amicable pair.
Table T(n,m) = 1 + n*m*(m+1)/2 read by antidiagonals: centered polygonal numbers.
Nearest integer to imaginary part of Riemann zeta zeros divided by 2*Pi.
Spiral constructed on the nodes of the triangular net in which each new term is the least nonnegative integers distinct from its neighbors.
G.f. A(x) satisfies: 1 = ...(((((A(x) - x)^(1/2) - x^2)^(1/2) - x^3)^(1/2) - x^4)^(1/2) - x^5)^(1/2) -...- x^n)^(1/2) -..., an infinite series of nested square roots.
a(n) = number of distinct nonzero digits in factorial base representation of n.
Numbers whose sum of divisors is prime.
Number of non-unitary prime divisors of n.
Quartan primes: primes of the form x^4 + y^4, x > 0, y > 0.
Squarefree numbers k such that 2^k - 1 is divisible by a square > 1.
Unique sequence with a(1)=0, a(2)=1, representing an array T(i,j) read by antidiagonals in which every row is this sequence itself.
Numbers k such that 3^k - 1 is not squarefree.
Numbers having exactly one non-unitary prime factor.
Numbers of the form (square + 1) that are not squarefree.
Square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals, where column k is the expansion of Product_{j>=1} 1/(1-x^j)^(j^(k*j)) in powers of x.
Number of subsets of {1,2,...,n} which sum to 0 modulo n.
Product of numbers m with 2 <= m <= n whose prime divisors all divide n.
Least b>1 such that n, when expressed in base b and then interpreted in base b^2, yields a multiple of n.
Fixed point of the morphism 0 -> 1, 1 -> 1010.
Fixed point of the morphism 0 -> 1, 1 -> 10101.
Number of Motzkin n-paths avoiding even-numbered steps that are flat steps.
Expansion of (eta(q^5) / eta(q))^6 in powers of q.
Number of 5-core partitions of n.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that for any n > 0, a(n) is coprime to a(2*n) and to a(2*n+1).
a(n) = phi(2n+1).
Trajectory of 270 under repeated application of k -> (phi(k)+sigma(k))/2.
G.f. A(x,y) satisfies: A( x - x*y*A(x,y), y)  =  x + x*(1-y)*A(x,y), where the coefficients T(n,k) of x^n*y^k form a triangle read by rows n>=1, for k=0..n-1.
Number of ways to write n as n = a*b*c*d*e with 1 <= a <= b <= c <= d <= e <= n.
Triangle, read by rows, where the g.f. of row n equals Product_{k=0..n-1} (1 + (2*k+1)*x + x^2) for n>0 with a single '1' in row 0.
Number of ways to write n as n = a*b*c*d with 1 <= a <= b <= c <= d <= n.
Least positive number k such that n+k and n+k^2 are both prime.
Chebyshev even-indexed U-polynomials evaluated at sqrt(7)/2.
Coordination sequence for planar net 3.3.3.3.6 (also called the fsz net).
Coordination sequence for planar net 3.6.3.6. Spherical growth function for a certain reflection group in plane.
Coordination sequence for planar net 3.12.12.
Coordination sequence for planar net 4.8.8.
a(n) is the smallest composite number whose sum of prime divisors (with multiplicity) is divisible by prime(n).
a(n) is the smallest composite number whose prime divisors (with multiplicity) sum to prime(n); n >= 3.
Determinant of the square matrix whose rows are the cyclic permutations of the digits of n.
a(n) = a(n-1) + 3*a(n-2) if n even, or 2*a(n-1) + 4*a(n-2) if n odd, starting with 0, 1.
a(n) is the minimum number of iterations of the form x -> x + x^j (where j is a nonnegative integer and need not be identical in each iteration) required to reach n starting from 1.
Numbers of form 2^i*6^j, with i, j >= 0; equivalently, numbers of the form 2^i*3^j with 0 <= j <= i.
A fractal binary sequence: For all n >= 1, underline the term with index n + a(n) + 1; then the two subsequences of underlined terms and of non-underlined terms are both equal to the sequence itself.
A twisted enumeration of the nonnegative integers.
a(n) is prime and sum of all primes <= a(n) is prime.
A permutation of the nonnegative integers: one odd, two even, four odd, eight even, etc.; extended to nonnegative integer with a(0) = 0.
Coefficients in expansion of E_6/E_4.
Coefficients in expansion of E_8/E_6.
Greatest prime divisor of prime(n) - 1.
Denominator of cototient(n)/totient(n).
a(n) is the number of recursively self-conjugate partitions of n.
Denominator of (Sum(m^(n-1),m=1..n-1)+1)/n.
The fixed point reached when map x -> 1+(x-(largest divisor d < x)) is iterated, starting from x = n.
Choix de Bruxelles (version 1): irregular table read by rows in which row n lists all the legal numbers that can be reached by halving or doubling some substring of the decimal expansion of n.
Expansion of x/(1-3*x-8*x^2).
Irregular triangle read by rows: row n lists the numbers that can be obtained from the binary expansion of n by either deleting a single 0, or inserting a single 0 after any 1, or doing nothing.
Flower garden sequence (see Comments for precise definition).

Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that for any v > 0, the value v appears up to v times, and the associate function f defined by f(n) = Sum_{k = 1..n} a(k) * i^k for n >= 0 is injective (where i denotes the imaginary unit).

Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that for any v > 0, the value v appears up to v^2 times, and the associate function f defined by f(n) = Sum_{k = 1..n} a(k) * m(k) for n >= 0 is injective (where {m(k)} corresponds to knight's moves, see Comments for precise definition).
Irregular triangle in which first row is 1, n-th row (n > 1) lists distinct prime factors of n.
Positive numbers of the form u * v where the binary representations of u and of v have the same number of 0's and the same number of 1's.
Positive numbers of the form u * v where the ternary representations of u and of v have the same number of digits d for d = 0..2.
Positive numbers of the form u * v where the decimal representations of u and of v have the same number of digits d for d = 0..9.
The greater of bigomega(n) and maximal prime index in the prime factorization of n.
a(n) = (p-1)/x, where p = prime(n) and x = ord(3,p), the smallest positive integer such that 3^x == 1 mod p.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = (-1)^(n+k)*(n+k+1)*binomial(n,k)*binomial(n+k,k) for n >= k >= 0.
Let S = smallest missing positive number, adjoin S, 2*S, 4*S, 8*S, 16*S, ... to the sequence until reaching a term that has S as a substring; reset S to the smallest missing positive number, repeat.
Numbers of the form (x^2) OR (y^2) with x, y >= 0 (where OR denotes the bitwise OR operator).
The total number of elastic collisions between a block of mass n, a block of mass 1, and a wall.
Numbers k that divide the sum of the first k nonzero Fibonacci numbers.
a(n) = 2^(prime(n)-1) mod prime(n)^2.
Binary self or Colombian numbers: numbers that cannot be expressed as the sum of distinct terms of the form 2^k+1 (k>=0), or equivalently, numbers not of form m + sum of binary digits of m.
Sum of the products formed by multiplying together the smaller and larger parts of each Goldbach partition of 2n.
Number of distinct prime numbers necessary to represent a natural number n > 1.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) gives the number of domino towers of height k consisting of n bricks.
If n = p_1 * ... * p_m with primes p_i <= p_{i+1}, a(n) = Sum_{k<m} Product_{j <= k} p_j.
If n = p_1 * ... * p_m with primes p_i <= p_{i+1}, a(n) = Sum_{j=1..m-1} p_1*...*p_j + Sum_{j=2..m} p_j*...*p_m.
Pseudo-lucky numbers.
a(n) = n + sod(n, sod(n, 10)), where sod(n,b) is the sum of base-b digits of n.
Sophie Germain degree of n: number of iterations of n under f(k) = 2k+1 before we reach a number that is not a prime.
1 appears three times, other numbers twice.
Primes congruent to {2, 3} mod 8.

A binary sequence defined as follows: a(1)=0; thereafter choose a(n) so as to minimize the number of final consecutive repeated words, and if there is a choice, minimize the length of the repeated word.
a(n) = Sum_{d|n} gcd(d, n/d).
a(n) = Sum_{d|n} psi(n/d) * phi(d).
Number of divisors of n^2-1.
Half-period primes, i.e., primes p for which the decimal expansion of 1/p has period (p-1)/2.
Square array T(n,k) in which row n lists the 3x+1 sequence starting at n, read by antidiagonals upwards, with n >= 1 and k >= 0.
Let p_k = k-th prime, let f((p_k)^n) = m where m is the largest power of p_(k+1) < (p_k)^n. a(n) = number of iterations of f to reach 1, starting from n and starting from k = 1.
Number of polygons formed when every pair of vertices of a regular n-gon are joined by an infinite line.

A variant of the inventory sequence: record the number of terms >= 0 thus far in the sequence, then the number of terms >= 1 thus far, then the number of terms >= 2 thus far, and so on, until a zero is recorded; the inventory then starts again, recording the number of terms >= 0, etc.
Irregular triangle T(n,k) starting with n followed by e_k = floor(log_p_k(p_(k-1)^e_(k-1))) such that e_k > 0.
Least k such that there exists an n-element subset S of {1,2,...,k} with the property that all products i * j are distinct for i <= j.
Irregular triangle read by rows where each row is the level sequence of a rooted tree in Beyer and Hedetniemi's iteration.
Table read by rows, coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of the tangent matrices.
Longest run of halving steps in the trajectory from n to 1 in the Collatz map (or 3x+1 problem), or -1 if no such trajectory exists.
Number of numbers expressible as b(1)*b(2)*...*b(n) with 1 <= b(i) <= i for each i.

A positive integer n is included if n, when written in binary, is made of run-lengths (lengths of runs of 0's as well as of runs of 1's) that form a permutation of some number of consecutive positive integers starting with 1.
The positive integer moduli a(n) for which the congruence x*(x + 1) == -4 (mod a(n)) is solvable for integer x (representatives from {0, 1, ..., a(n)-1}); in increasing order.
An array A of the positive odd numbers, read by antidiagonals upwards, giving the present triangle T.

a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number whose sum a(n) + a(n-1) is distinct from all previous sums, a(i) + a(i-1), i=1..n-1, whose product a(n) * a(n-1) is distinct from all previous products, a(i) * a(i-1), i=1..n-1, and whose difference |a(n) - a(n-1)| is distinct from all previous differences, |a(i) - a(i-1)|, i=1..n-1.

Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of positive numbers such that, for n>2, a(n) has a common factor with a(n-1), no common factor with a(n-2), and the product a(n)*a(n-1) is distinct from all previous products, a(i)*a(i-1), i=2..n-1.
Decimal expansion of Gamma(1/3)*Gamma(5/6)/Gamma(1/6).
n-th chunk consists of the numbers 1, ..., 2^n.
Sparsely totient numbers; numbers n such that m > n implies phi(m) > phi(n).
a(n) = 1 if the smallest b > 1 such that b^(p-1) == 1 (mod p^2) is prime, 0 otherwise, with p = prime(n).
Periodic sequence [0,1,1,1] of length 4; Characteristic function of numbers that are not multiples of 4.
Expansion of 1/((1 - x)*(1 - 2*x^2)).
a(1)=1. a(n) = a(n-1) + (sum of terms, from among terms a(1) through a(n-1), which are prime or 1).
Smallest integer not yet present in the sequence such that the sum of the first a(n) terms of the sequence is a prime.
a(n) is the denominator of binomial(n^3 + 6*n^2 - 6*n + 2, n^3 - 1)/n^3.
Least nonnegative integer k such that (gpf(n)!)^k is divisible by n, where gpf(n) is the greatest prime factor of n.
The run lengths transform of the ternary expansion of n corresponds to the run lengths transform of the binary expansion of a(n).
The run lengths transform of the balanced ternary expansion of n corresponds to the run lengths transform of the binary expansion of a(n).
Expansion of e.g.f. 1/(1 + exp(2*x) - exp(3*x)).
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = (-8)^k*binomial(2*n, 2*k)*Euler(2*k, 1/2).
Concatenate first n nonzero Fibonacci numbers in reverse order.
a(0)=1; a(n) = sum of all previous terms, eliminating repeated digits (starting from the left).
The binary expansion of a(n) corresponds to the ordinal transform (reduced modulo 2) of the binary expansion of n.

a(0) = 0; thereafter a(n) is the least integer (in absolute value) not yet in the sequence such that the absolute difference between a(n-1) and a(n) is a square > 1; in case of a tie, preference is given to the positive value.
Decimal expansion of the smallest number greater than 1 whose decimal and binary expansions have the same succession of digits.
G.f. A(x,y) satisfies 1/x = Sum_{n=-oo..+oo} A(x,y)^n * (A(x,y)^n + y)^(n+1), as a triangle of coefficients T(n,k) of x^n*y^k in A(x,y), read by rows.
Sum of divisors of n that are not divisible by 4.
a(n) = n*sigma(n).

a(1) = 2. For n > 1, a(n) = smallest prime factor of c=2*a(n-1)+1 that is not in {a(1), ..., a(n-1)}; if all prime factors of c are in {a(1), ..., a(n-1)}, then we try the next value of c, which is 2*c+1; and so on.
a(n) is the largest digit sum of all n-digit fifth powers.

List of x coordinates of prime numbers in a Cartesian grid, where the first prime 2 is placed at the origin (0,0) and the second prime 3 at (1,0). For the n-th prime prime(n), n >= 3, take a unit step in the direction (prime(n)-3)*45 degrees counterclockwise from the positive x-axis.
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = Sum_{i=0..n-k} (-1)^(n - k - i) * binomial(n - k, i) * binomial(k + 2*i, i) * (k + 1) / (k + 1 + i).
a(n) is the largest number that is the digit sum of an n-digit cube.
Number of primitive roots modulo n.
Elements of an interval of natural numbers whose product is divisible by the square of the largest prime factor.
Number of segments lit to display the number n on a 7-segment display (as in pocket calculators): variant where '6', '7' and '9' use 6, 4 resp. 5 segments.
Number of ways to choose a sequence of distinct strict integer partitions, one of each prime index of n.
Decimal expansion of Pi/3.

Values of u in the quartets (2, u, v, w) of type 3; i.e., values of u for solutions to 2*(2 - u) = v*(v - w), in distinct positive integers, with v > 1, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
The length of the maximal common prefix of the binary expansions of n and sigma(n), where sigma is the sum of divisors function.
Almost practical numbers.

Numbers k that can be written as k = s_1^x_1 + ... + s_t^x_t, with 1 < s_1 < ... < s_t and {s_1,..., s_t} = {x_1,..., x_t} for some t > 0 such that for all possible representations of k the permutations connecting (s_1,...,s_t) with (x_1,...,x_t) are cyclic.
a(1) = 1. For n > 1, a(n) is the smallest number obtainable by rearranging the digits of n whose value has the largest prime factor among all such rearrangements.
Primes p such that p-1 has a prime factor q > p^(2/3).
a(n) is the greatest product x*y of two integers 2^(n-1) <= x <= y < 2^n maximizing the Hamming weight of this product.
a(n) is the number of vertices of the convex hull of the finite point set {(k, prime(k)), k = 1..n} (where prime(k) denotes the k-th prime number).
Largest integer of the form r^k whose base-n alternating digital root is r and whose number of base-n digits is k.
Smallest member 'a' of the primitive Pythagorean triples (a,b,c) ordered by increasing c, then b.
Number of Q(chi) for chi running through the Dirichlet characters modulo n, where Q(chi) is the field generated by the values of chi.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of Schroeder paths of semilength n containing exactly k peaks but no peaks at level one (n >= 1; 0 <= k <= n-1).
a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} binomial(n,k)^2 * binomial(2*k,k) * (n-k)!.
Numbers k such that the k-th prime divides the sum of the first k primes.
Numbers n such that, in the binary expansion of n, reading from right to left, the number of 1's never exceeds the number of 0's.
Upper prime of a difference of 6 between consecutive primes.
Triangle T(n,k) (n >= 1, k >= 1) giving dimension of bigrading of Hopf algebra of rooted trees.
Riesel problem: start with n; repeatedly double and add 1 until reaching a prime. Sequence gives number of steps to reach a prime or 0 if no prime is ever reached.
Number of ways to write n as the unordered sum of two nonzero triangular numbers.
Lower prime of a difference of 12 between consecutive primes.
Lower prime of a pair of consecutive primes having a difference of 14.
Lower prime of a difference of 18 between consecutive primes.
Lower prime of a difference of 20 between consecutive primes.
Number of characters in the English name of n, including spaces and hyphens.
Number of prime knots with n crossings.
Number of prime satellite knots with n crossings.
Number of torus knots with n crossings.
Revert transform of 1 - x - x^3.
Triangle of generalized sum of divisors function, read by rows.

The periodic point counting sequence for the toral automorphism given by the polynomial of (conjectural) smallest Mahler measure. The map is x -> Ax mod 1 for x in [0,1)^10, where A is the companion matrix for the polynomial x^10+x^9-x^7-x^6-x^5-x^4-x^3+x+1.
Denominators of Bernoulli numbers B_0, B_1, B_2, B_4, B_6, ...
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = T(n-1,k-1) + k^2*T(n-1,k), 1 < k <= n, T(n,1) = 1.
Least common multiple of differences between consecutive divisors of n (ordered by size).
Smallest prime p such that there is a gap of 2n between p and previous prime.
Number of different score sequences that are possible in an n-team round-robin tournament.
Numbers with mirror symmetry about middle.
Numbers that are divisible by exactly 5 different primes.
Number of terms in continued fraction for sqrt(n), excl. 2nd and higher periods.
Rearrangement of even numbers such that a(k)*a(k+1) + 1 is a prime for all k.
Group the natural numbers so that the n-th group contains the smallest set of n relatively prime numbers: (1), (2, 3), (4, 5, 7), (6, 11, 13, 17), (8, 9, 19, 23, 25), (10, 21, 29, 31, 37, 41), ...
Image of n after 3k iterates of '3x+1' map (k large).
Limit of the image of n after 2k iterates of `(3x+1)/2' map as k grows.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the power of 2 in denominator of coefficients of Legendre polynomials, where n >= 0 and 0 <= k <= n.
Squared radii of the spheres around (0,0,0) that contain record numbers of lattice points.
Third-order composites.
a(n) is the smallest number k such that primorial(k)^2 > primorial(n).
Number of different cycles of digits in the decimal expansions of 1/p, 2/p, ..., (p-1)/p where p = n-th prime different from 2 or 5.
a(n) = n^2 * phi(n).
a(1) = 1 and then distinct numbers such that the sum as well the absolute difference of successive terms is a prime.
a(1) = 1; then distinct numbers such that both the product of two successive terms + 1 and the ratio of the larger to the smaller of two successive terms + 1 is a prime.
Primes that are the sum of two squares and which set a record for the gap to the next prime of that form.
Decimal expansion of the imaginary part of the first nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function.
Positive numbers of the form y^2 - x^3, x and y >= 1.
Rearrangement of natural numbers such that the n-th term is coprime to n and the sum of n terms starting from the n-th term is a multiple of n.
Odd numbers with exactly 3 ones in binary expansion.
Fermat base-2 pseudoprimes whose prime factors do not divide any smaller pseudoprime.
Average of three successive primes squared, (prime(n)^2+prime(n+1)^2+prime(n+2)^2)/3, n>=3.
Numbers n such that 2*prime(n)^2 - 1 is prime.

Sorting by prefix reversal (or 'flipping pancakes'). You can only reverse segments that include the initial term of the current permutation; a(n) is the number of reversals that are needed to transform an arbitrary permutation of n letters to the identity permutation.

Take n sheets of paper, arrange them into piles, write on each sheet the cardinality (number of sheets) of its pile. Do this again, so each sheet is labeled by an ordered pair of positive integers. How many ways can this be done so that every sheet has a unique label? (Only distinct sets of labels count, not every permutation of the labels or sheets.).
Concatenate odd primes in decreasing order.
Number of 321-hexagon-avoiding permutations in S_n, i.e., permutations of 1..n with no submatrix equivalent to 321, 56781234, 46781235, 56718234 or 46718235.
Permutation of integers a(a(n)) = n. In binary representation of n, transformation of inner bits, 1 <-> 0, gives binary representation of a(n).
Triangle, read by rows, such that the convolution of each row with {1,2} produces a triangle which, when flattened, equals this flattened form of the original triangle.
Smallest prime of the form n(n-1)(n-2)...(n-k)-1, or 0 if no such prime exists.
Smallest prime of the form n(n-1)(n-2)...(n-k)+1, or 0 if no such prime exists.
Least k such that (k-1)/n and k*n + 1 both are primes.
Maximum k <= n such that 1, 2, ..., k are all relatively prime to n.
Maximum run of white (or OFF) cells in generation n of the Rule 30 elementary cellular automaton.
Number of n-celled polyominoes with minimum perimeter.
Unique sequence with a(1)=1 where each a(n) occurs in the same order a(n) times consecutively in its sequence of first differences which contains no other terms.

G.f. A(x) satisfies: 3^n - 1 = Sum_{k=0..n} [x^k]A(x)^n and also satisfies: (3+z)^n - (1+z)^n + z^n = Sum_{k=0..n} [x^k](A(x)+z*x)^n for all z, where [x^k]A(x)^n denotes the coefficient of x^k in A(x)^n.

G.f. A(x) satisfies: 4^n - 1 = Sum_{k=0..n} [x^k] A(x)^n and also satisfies: (4+z)^n - (1+z)^n + z^n = Sum_{k=0..n} [x^k](A(x)+z*x)^n for all z, where [x^k] A(x)^n denotes the coefficient of x^k in A(x)^n.
Slanted Catalan convolution table, read by rows of 2*n+1 terms in row n, where T(n,k) = C(n+2*k-[k/2],k)*(n-[k/2])/(n+2*k-[k/2]).
Start with positive integers in order. At m-th iteration, let a(k) become a(k-1) for m+1<=k<=p_m and let a(m) become a(p_m), where p_m is the m-th prime. Record the limiting sequence.

For each single digit {0,1,...,9} record the smallest prime made up of copies of that digit (if there is one); repeat for all of the C(10,2) = 45 pairs of distinct decimal digits; then for all triples; etc.
Triangle read by rows, based on array described below.
Let f(n) = n + sum of the digits of n. If f(n) is multiple of n then a(n)= f(n) else a(n) = f(f(f(n)))... until one gets a multiple of n; a(n) = 0 if no such number exists.
n occurs n times, as early as possible subject to the constraint that two successive occurrences of n are separated by at least by n terms.
a(n) = 1 iff 6*n+1 and 6*n-1 are both prime numbers (0 otherwise).
Sequence is defined by property that (a0,a1,a2,a3,...) = binomial transform of (a0,a0,a1,a1,a2,a2,a3,a3,...).
Triangle of numbers {a(n,k), n >= 0, 0<=k<=n} defined by a(0,0)=1, a(n,0)=a(n-1,n-1), a(n,k)=a(n,k-1) + Sum_{i=0..k-1} a(n-1,i).
Triangle T(n,k) read by rows giving number of underdiagonal lattice paths from (0,0) to (n,k) using only steps R = (1,0), V = (0,1) and D = (3,1).
Theta series of D_4 lattice; Fourier coefficients of Eisenstein series E_{gamma,2}.
Prime corresponding to largest prime power factor of n, a(1)=1.
Triangle read by rows, T(n, k) = [x^k] (1-x)^(n+1)*Sum_{j=0..n} binomial(n + n*j + j, n*j + j)*x^j.
Number triangle T(n,k) = Sum_{j=0..n-k} binomial(k,j)*binomial(n-j,k)*((j+1) mod 2).
Triangle read by rows, 0 <= k <= n: T(n,k) = binomial(n-[(k+1)/2],[k/2])*(-1)^[(k+1)/2].
Number of added unique known entries when going from the n X n to the (n+1) X (n+1) multiplication table.
Square array, read by antidiagonals, where row n equals the crystal ball sequence for D_n lattice.
Primary pretenders: least composite c such that n^c == n (mod c).
a(n) = 2*binomial(n,3).
Expansion of (1+2*x)/(1-6*x+x^2).
Numbers k such that the standard deviation of 1,...,k is an integer.
Numbers k such that k^2 is centered hexagonal.
Square array, read by antidiagonals, where row n equals the coordination sequence of B_n lattice, for n >= 0.
Primes that have the property that deleting some digit results in a prime with the same multiplicative order, or period (repeating length of 1/p).
Triangle read by rows: even numbers as sums of two odd primes.
Numbers having fewer prime factors than at least one smaller number.

Triangle T, read by rows, such that the m-th matrix power satisfies T^m = I + m*(T - I), where T(n,k) = [T^-1](n-1,k) + [T^-1](n-1,k-1) for n>k>0, with T(n,0)=T(n,n)=1 for n>=0 and I is the identity matrix.
Even Fibonacci numbers; or, Fibonacci(3*n).
a(1)=1; for n>1, a(n) = least positive integer not appearing earlier such that {a(k) | 1 <= k <= n} and {a(k) XOR a(k-1) | 1 <= k <= n} are disjoint sets of distinct numbers.
Difference triangle of factorial numbers read by upward diagonals.
n coded as binary word of length=n with k-th bit set iff k is prime (1<=k<=n), decimal value.
Numbers k such that 2^k == 4^k (mod k).

Szekeres's sequence: a(n)-1 in ternary = n-1 in binary; also: a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2, and thereafter a(n) is smallest number k which avoids any 3-term arithmetic progression in a(1), a(2), ..., a(n-1), k.
a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1, and for any n > 1, a(n) is the number of iterations of the map x -> x - gpf(x) (where gpf(x) denotes the greatest prime factor of x) required to reach 0 starting from n.
n-th Gosper hyperfactorial of n.
Denominators of convergents to the square root of the golden ratio.
Largest integer m satisfying Omega(m) + pi(gpf(m)) - [m<>1] = n.
a(n) is the n-digit positive number with no trailing zeros and coprime to its digital reversal R(a(n)) at which abs(R(a(n))/a(n)-Pi) is minimized.
a(n) is the n-digit positive number with no trailing zeros and coprime to its digital reversal R(a(n)) at which abs(a(n)/R(a(n))-Pi) is minimized.
Product of any number of consecutive primes; squarefree numbers with no gaps in their prime factorization.
Sum modulo the base of all the digits of n in every base from 2 to n-1.
Wythoff representation of natural numbers.
a(n) = n! * number of partitions of n.
a(n) is the period of the n-th diagonal, from the right, of Rule 30 (begun from an initial black cell).
Numbers with six distinct prime divisors.
a(n) is the least k such that 2^k + n is not squarefree.
Numbers k such that Sum_{d|k, d<k, d not occurring before} d > k.
Triangle T read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of partitions of n in which k is the least integer that is not a part and there are more parts > k than there are < k (n >= k > 0).
a(n) is the smallest nonnegative number k such that the decimal expansion of 2^k contains the string n.
Digitally balanced numbers in base 3: equal numbers of 0's, 1's, 2's.
Triangle with subscripts (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(3,1),(2,2),(1,3), etc. in which entry (i,j) is [ i/j ].

Irregular table read by rows: Starting with an empty stack of numbers successively add each integer n and then stabilize the stack using the rules given in the Comments. T(n,k) gives the number in the k-th layer after adding n.
Legendre's triangle read by rows. T(n, k) = L(n / prime(k)) where L(n/p) is the Legendre symbol, for n >= 0 and 2 <= k <= n + 2.
Number of digits in 2^n.
Number of odd digits in decimal representation of n.
Number of even digits in decimal representation of n.
a(n) is the largest digit sum of all n-digit fourth powers.
a(n) is the largest digit sum of all n-digit sixth powers.
Zero-one version of Golay-Rudin-Shapiro sequence (or word).
Array read by ascending antidiagonals: A(n,k) = n! * [x^n] 1/(1 - x*exp(x))^k.
Number of residues r such that p^m is congruent to r (mod n), where prime p | n and m >= 0.
Concatenate sum and product of decimal digits of n.
Decimal expansion of 9 * Product_{p prime >= 5} (1-3/p)/(1-1/p)^3.
Sum of prime indices of n (with multiplicity) minus sum of distinct prime indices of n.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, if n = Product prime(k)^e(k), then a(n) = Product (k)^(e(k)-1).
Largest k such that there are no two subsets of the k consecutive integers n..(n+k-1) with the same product.
Numbers k such that sigma(k) >= 3*k.
If n = p_1^e_1 * ... * p_k^e_k, p_1 < ... < p_k primes, then a(n) = p_k^e_k.
One half of the even Markoff numbers.
The odd Markoff numbers.
Triangle read by rows: number of terms in unit fraction representation of k/n using the greedy algorithm, 1<=k<=n-1.
a(1)=2, a(2)=3; for n>=3, a(n) = prime nearest to a(n-1) + a(n-2), with ties broken by taking the smaller prime.
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = Sum_{i=0..n} binomial(2*i, i) * binomial(n - 2*i, k - i).
Squares visited by a knight moving on an upper half-plane spiral numbered board, starting from square 1, and where the knight moves to the smallest numbered unvisited square.
Rectangular table of coefficients T(n,k) of x^k/k! in F(n,x) that satisfies F(n,x) = x * exp( F^n(n,x) ) for n >= 1, as read by ascending antidiagonals.
E.g.f. f(x) satisfies f(x*f(x)) = exp(x).
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = x + x*A(A(A(x))).
E.g.f. A(x) satisfies A'(x) = exp(A(A(x))), with A(0) = 0.
Number of ways of writing n as a+b where a is abundant (or perfect), b is deficient (or perfect) and s(a)-a=b-s(b) (s(x)=sigma(x)-x).
Number of ways of writing n=a+b where |s(a)-a|=|s(b)-b|, s(x)=sigma(x)-x.
If n is composite, replace n with the concatenation of its nontrivial divisors, otherwise a(n) = n.
Additive persistence: number of summations of digits needed to obtain a single digit (the additive digital root).
Imaginary part of (1+2i)^n.
Primes from products of split even-digit primes.
Definition: A kara B = C, where C is the least nonnegative integer such that C * B >= A and C * (B-1) < A. a(n) is the smallest k such that n kara k is undefined.
Number of primes having exactly the same digits as appear in first n primes.
Rows of triangle formed using Pascal's rule except begin and end n-th row with (n+1)st prime.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = T(n,k-1) + T(n-1,k-1) for k >= 2 with T(n,1) = n.
Numbers k such that k - phi(k) is prime.
Hit polynomials; convolution of natural numbers with Fibonacci numbers F(2), F(3), F(4), ....
Nearest integer to (n+1)^3/9.
Number of solutions to y^2 + y = x^3 - x^2 modulo n.
Table read by descending antidiagonals where T(n,k) = T(n,k-1) + T(n,k-1)^2/k^2 and T(n,0)=n.
Array read by antidiagonals: T(n,k)=T(n,k-1)*(T(n,k-1)+k-1)/k with T(n,1)=n.
Multiplication table read by antidiagonals: T(i,j) = i*j (i>=0, j>=0). Alternatively, multiplication triangle read by rows: P(i,j) = j*(i-j) (i>=0, 0<=j<=i).

a(n) is smallest number A such that there is an equality of the form (A=Product of n distinct primes) = (B=Product of n distinct primes) + (C=Product of n distinct primes) with gcd(A,B) = gcd(B,C) = gcd(A,C) = 1, B < C.
Composite numbers k such that k - phi(k) divides sigma(k) - k.
Sum of the digit reversals of the first n natural numbers.
Product of digits of n-th prime.
Numbers j such that j^2 + k^2 is a cube for some k > j.
Composites c, such that when iteration of f(k) = phi(sigma(k)-phi(k)) is started at c it ends at a fixed point > 1.
Ordered differences without repetitions between two successive prime powers of prime numbers.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the k-th prime = 1 (mod n).
Triangle in which n-th row contains the first n numbers, not already present, that begin with n.
Number of binary trees of height n; or products (ways to insert parentheses) of height n when multiplication is non-commutative and non-associative.
Triangle in which the n-th row contains n palindromes beginning with n.
Triangle in which the n-th row contains n distinct composite numbers with the least product and has least number of prime divisors. No member of a row is a multiple of another member of the row.
Triangle read by rows in which the n-th row contains n numbers starting with n and not coprime to n, except the first row is {1}.
a(n) = floor(phi*n) - 2*floor(phi*n/2) where phi is the golden ratio.
Let S(0)={1,1,2} S(n)={S(n-1), S(n-1)-{x},{3-x}} where x is the last element of S(n-1), then sequence is S(infinity).
Minimal k > n such that (4*k+3*n) * (4*n+3*k) is a square.
Sort the numbers 2^i and 3^j. Then a(n) is the exponent of the n-th term.
Sort the numbers 2^i and 3^j. Then a(n) is the base of the n-th term. Set a(1)=1.
Number of factorials between two primorials.
Numbers which are the sum of 3 nonzero 4th powers.
Symmetric square array, read by antidiagonals: T(k, k) = T(0, k + 1) = Sum_{m = 0..k} C(k, m)*T(m, k - m) for k >= 0; T(0, 0) = 1; T(n, k) = T(n - 1, k) + T(n, k - 1) for n, k >= 1.
Product of parts in n-th partition in Abramowitz and Stegun order.
Alternate digits 1 and 0.
For n > 1: a(n) = p if n = p^e with p prime and e > 1, otherwise a(n) = (n-m)-th prime, where m = number of nonprime prime powers <= n; a(1)=1.
Decimal expansion of number with continued fraction 2 + 3/5 + 7/11 + 13/17 + 19/23 + ...
a(n) is the smallest integer such that the sum of any three ordered terms a(k), k <= n, is unique.
a(n) = smallest integer > n where mu(n) = mu(a(n)).
A squarefree (or Thue-Morse) ternary sequence: closed under 1->123, 2->13, 3->2. Start with 1.
Square array, read by antidiagonals, where column (k+1) equals the self-convolution of row k, with row 0 and column 0 consisting of all 1's.
Triangle, read by rows, such that diagonal n is equal to the Euler transform of row n, where each row starts with 1.
Lower triangular matrix, read by rows, defined as the convergent of the concatenation of matrices using the iteration: M(n+1) = [[M(n),0*M(n)],[M(n),M(n)^2]], with M(0) = [1].
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) represents the number of lozenge tilings of an (n,1,n)-hexagon which include the non-vertical tile above the main diagonal starting in position k+1.
'Truncated Mertens function': values of -1 at primes are left out, that is, summatory Moebius when argument runs through nonprimes.
n-th row of the following triangle contains n terms of an arithmetic progression with the first term 1 such that the sum is the least possible n-th power. Sequence contains the leading diagonal.
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = 10^(n-1) - 1 + k*floor(9*10^(n-1)/n), for 1 <= k <= n.
a(n) is the unique odd positive solution x of 2^n = 7x^2+y^2.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = number of planar trivalent (or cubic) loopless multigraphs with 2n nodes and exactly k double bonds, for 0 <= k <= n.
a(n) = n-th prime of Erdős-Selfridge classification n-.
a(n) = floor(1/frac(n*e)).
Iccanobif numbers: add reversal of a(n-1) to a(n-2).
Iccanobif numbers: add a(n-1) to reversal of a(n-2).
Smallest square that is equal to the sum of n not-necessarily-distinct primes plus 1.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = number of functions from [1,2,...,n] to [1,2,...,n] such that the image contains exactly k elements (0<=k<=n).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k), for k=-n..n-1, is the scaled (by 2^n n!) probability that the sum of n uniform [-1, 1] variables is between k and k+1.
Array read by antidiagonals: T(n,k) = Porta-Stolarsky star product T(n,k) = n * k = nk + floor(phi n) floor(phi k) where phi = (1 + sqrt(5))/2.
a(2n-1) = 1; a(2n) = a(n)th smallest positive integer not among the earlier terms of the sequence.
Numbers that are divisible by exactly 10 primes with multiplicity.
Weight distribution of [ 18,9,8 ] self-dual code over GF(4).
a(1) = 2; a(2n) = least common multiple of all previous terms + 1. a(2n+1) = least common multiple of all previous terms - 1.
Start with S = {}. For m = 0, 1, 2, 3, ... let u be the binary expansion of m. If u is not a substring of S, append the minimal number of 0's and 1's to S to remedy this. Sequence gives S.

Number of inequivalent binary sequences of length n, where two sequences are said to be equivalent if they have the same set of phrases in their Ziv-Lempel encodings (the phrases can appear in a different order in the two sequences).
For all k: the first k numbers followed by the first k primes.
Number of primes of the form n - 2^k.
Number triangle binomial(n+2k,3k).
Number triangle binomial(n+3k,4k).
Riordan array (1,x(1-x)^2).
Let the height of a polynomial be the largest coefficient in absolute value. Then a(n) is the maximal height of a divisor of x^n-1 with integral coefficients.
Triangle T, read by rows, where matrix inverse T^-1 has -3^n in the secondary diagonal: [T^-1](n+1,n) = -3^n, with all 1's in the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
Triangle T, read by rows, that satisfies matrix equation: T - (T-I)^2 = C, where C is Pascal's triangle.
Values of n for which Leech's problem 'Find two rational right-angled triangles on the same base whose heights are in the ratio n:1' has a solution.
a(n) = prime(n) modulo semiprime(n).
Lexicographically earliest permutation of prime powers such that the exponents of succeeding terms increase at most by 1.
a(n) = smallest positive integer not occurring earlier in the sequence such that Sum_{k=1..n} a(k) is coprime to n.
Primes that are the sum of three consecutive primes.
Number triangle 2^abs(L(C(n,2)/3) - L(C(k,2)/3))*[k<=n] where L(j/p) is the Legendre symbol of j and p.
Inductive sum-and-difference sequence.
Least k such that k*2^n +/- 1 are twin primes.
Triangular array read by rows: T(n,k) = number of binary vectors of length n whose longest run of consecutive 1's has length k, for n >= 0, 0 <= k <= n.
Array L(k,n) read by antidiagonals: k-step Lucas numbers.
The interspersion T(2,3,0), by antidiagonals.
The interspersion T(2,3,1), by antidiagonals.
The interspersion T(3,2,0), by antidiagonals.
The interspersion T(3,2,1), by antidiagonals.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = C(n,k) + 3*C(n,k+1) + 2*C(n,k+2) (0<=k<=n).
Triangle of coefficients of shifted Chebyshev's S(n,x-2) = U(n,x/2-1) polynomials (exponents of x in decreasing order).
Numerator of Sum_{k=1..n} (-1)^(k+1) * 1/(k*(k+1)).
a(n) = semiprime(n)^prime(n).
Smallest primes such that a(j) - a(k) are all different.
A B_2 sequence: a(n) = least value such that sequence increases and pairwise sums of distinct elements are all distinct.
Triangle read by rows: (1, 2, 2, 2, ...) on the main diagonal and the rest zeros.

G. J. Chaitin's numbers of s-expressions of size n are given by the coefficients of polynomials p(k, x) satisfying p(k, x) = Sum[p(j, x)*p(k - j, x), {j, 2, k - 1}]. The coefficients of these polynomials give the triangle shown here.
Convolve Fibonacci and Pell numbers.
a(n) = least 2k such that p is the least prime in a Goldbach partition of 2k, where p = prime(n).
Emirps with only prime digits (i.e., 2, 3, 5, 7).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = number of partitions of binomial(n,k) into parts k and n, 1<=k<=n.
a(n) is the smallest positive square such that pairwise sums of distinct elements are all distinct.
A B_2 sequence: a(n) is the smallest square such that pairwise sums of not necessarily distinct elements are all distinct.
Integers written in base phi, with the 'decimal point' omitted.
Number of connected 2-colored parking functions.
Period 6: repeat [0, 0, 1, 0, 0, -1].
Periodic sequence: Repeat 2,6.
Table of q-derangement numbers of type A, by rows.
a(n) is the smallest number >= 1 not occurring earlier and not the sum of cubes of two distinct earlier terms.
a(n) = Sum_{d|n} binomial(n/d+d-2, d-1).
Generalized Wilson quotients (or Wilson quotients for composite moduli).
Even numbers without the squares.
a(n) = L(3*n)/L(n), where L(n) = Lucas number.
Summatory Pascal triangle T(n,k) (0 <= k <= n) read by rows. Top entry is 1. Each entry is the sum of the parallelogram above it.
Decimal expansion of (70*exp(Pi*sqrt(163)))^2.
a(n) = p(3*n), where p(n) = number of partitions of n into parts that correspond to areas of distinct pieces of Archimedes' ostomachion.
An aerated Catalan triangle.
a(n) = product of the remainders when the n-th prime is divided by primes up to the (n-1)-st prime.
Ultrafactorials: a(n) = n!^n!.
a(n) = the smallest integer > n that is divisible by exactly the same number of distinct primes as n is.
Numbers m such that 2^m-m is a semiprime.
Odd numerators of the fractions (1/4-1/n^2), n>= -2.
Number of divisors d of n such that d+1 is not a divisor of n.
a(n) = period of x^n + x + 1 over GF(2), i.e., the smallest integer m>0 such that x^n + x + 1 divides x^m + 1 over GF(2).
Number of solutions to n=x*y*z, x+y-z=1 with ordered triples (x,y,z), x,y,z>=1.
a(n) = Sum_{k|n} k*mu_2(n/k).
a(n) = floor(3*n*phi) - floor(2*n*phi) - floor(n*phi), where phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2, the golden ratio.
Primes of the form 2^t-2^k-1, k>=1.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = Sum_{c in composition(n,k)} lcm(c).
Expansion of (1 - x + x^2) / (1 - x)^2 in powers of x.
Riordan matrix (1+x/sqrt(1-4*x),(1-sqrt(1-4*x))/2).
Triangle T(n,k) read by rows of the smallest n-gonal number greater than 1 that is also k-gonal, or 0 if none exists, for 3 <= k <= n.
Values square, differences triangular.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) (n >= 0, 1 <= k <= n+1) are the signed Hultman numbers.
Fixed point of the morphism 0->01, 1->001.
a(n) = n + floor(nr/t) + floor(ns/t) with r=1, s=arctan(1/2), t=arctan(2).
Irregular pairs (p,2k) ordered by increasing k.
Extended Catalan triangle read by rows.
Decimal expansion of xo, where P=(xo,yo) is the point nearest O=(0,0) in which a line y=mx meets the curve y=cos(x+Pi/6) orthogonally.
Lerch quotients of odd primes: ((Sum_{k=1..p-1} q_p(k)) - w_p)/p, where q_p(k) = (k^(p-1)-1)/p is a Fermat quotient, w_p = ((p-1)!+1)/p is a Wilson quotient, and p is the n-th prime, with n > 1.
Fermat-Wilson quotients of non-Wilson primes: q_p(w_p), where q_p(k) = (k^(p-1)-1)/p is a Fermat quotient, w_p = ((p-1)!+1)/p is a Wilson quotient, and p is a non-Wilson prime.
a(n) = s(k)-s(j), where (s(k),s(j)) is the least pair of distinct triangular numbers for which n divides their difference.
s(k)-s(j), where (k,j) is the least pair for which n divides s(k)-s(j), and s(j)=Fibonacci(2j-1).
Least nonnegative integer y such that Kronecker(y^2 - 4, p(n)) == -1 and (x+2)^(p(n)+1) == 5 -+ 2*y (mod p(n), mod x^2 +- y*x + 1).
Least nonnegative integer y such that Kronecker(y^2 - 4, n) == -1 and (x+2)^(n+1) == 5 -+ 2*y (mod n, mod x^2 +- y*x + 1), or -1 if there is no such y.
T(n,k)=Number of nXk 0,1 arrays with the row and column sums nondecreasing.
a(n) = n!/ceiling(n/2)!.
Numbers k for which 2 divides s(k)-s(j) for some j<k; each k occurs once for each such j; s(k) denotes the (k+1)-st Fibonacci number.
Expansion of eta(q)^5 / eta(q^5) in powers of q.
Start with first run [1,2] then, for n >= 2, the n-th run is a(n) times [a(1),...,a(n-1)].
Positive integers repeated three times.
Irregular triangle read by rows: coefficients c(n,k) (n>=2, 0<=k<= floor((n-2)/2)) in formula for number of restricted partitions.
Transform of Catalan numbers whose Hankel transform gives the Somos-4 sequence.
Least number k0 such that (prime(k+1) / prime(k))^n < 2 for all k >= k0.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = h^2, c(h) = (n-1+h)^2, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = h^3, c(h) = (n-1+h)^3, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = h^2, c(h) = m*(m+1)/2, m=n-1+h, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = h, c(h) = (n-1+h)^2, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 2^(h-1), c(h) = (n-1+h)^2, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = -1 + 2^h, c(h) = b(n-1+h), n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 2*h-1, c(h) = -1 + 2^(n-1+h), n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = -1 + 2^h, c(h) = 2*n - 3 + 2*h, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 1+[h/2], c(h) = [(n+h)/2], n>=1, h>=1, [ ] = floor, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 2^(h-1), c(h) = 2*n-3+2*h, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = h, c(h) = 1+[(n-1+h)/2], n>=1, h>=1, [ ] = floor, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array: (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 3*h-2, c(h) = 3*n-5+3*h, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 3*h-1, c(h) = 3*n-4+3*h, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 3*h-2, c(h) = 3*n-4+3*h, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 2*h-1, c(h) = 4*n-7+4*h, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
Rectangular array:  (row n) = b**c, where b(h) = 2*h-1, c(h) = 4*n-5+4*h, n>=1, h>=1, and ** = convolution.
The Collatz (3x+1) iteration mod 2 with bits combined.
The most significant digit in base n representation of n!.
Smallest of the first four consecutive primes that comprise two sets of primes with difference 2*n.
Smallest of the first six consecutive primes that comprise three sets of primes with difference 2*n.
An enumeration of all k-tuples containing positive integers.
Triangle in which n-th row lists unitary divisors of n.
Number of zeros in the longest string of consecutive zeros in the binary representation of n.
Length of longest contiguous block of 1's in binary expansion of n.
Smallest number m such that all the n numbers np(m+k-1), 0 < k < n+1 are equal, where np(t) is number of primes p with prime(t) < p < prime(t)^(1+1/t).
a(n) is obtained by flipping every second bit in the binary representation of n starting at the second-most significant bit and on downwards.
Number of reducible GF(2)[X]-polynomials in range [0,n].
Number of nodes in rooted tree with Matula-Goebel number n.
Number of Lyndon words on {1,2,3} with an odd number of 1's and an odd number of 2's.
Number of ON cells at generation n of 5-celled totalistic CA defined by Rule 780.
Table with T(1,1) = 1; for n>1, T(n,k) is the number of k's in rows 1 through n-1.
a(n) = bitwise XOR of all the bit numbers for the bits that are set in n, using number 1 for the LSB.
7th-order Fibonacci numbers with a(0)=...=a(6)=1.
Rectangular array A read by upward antidiagonals in which row A(n) is the sequence of all numbers divisible by no prime exceeding prime(n).
Numbers that begin a run of an odd number of consecutive integers whose cubes sum to a square.
The infinite trunk of Zeckendorf beanstalk. The only infinite sequence such that a(n-1) = a(n) - number of 1's in Zeckendorf representation of a(n).

Triangle read by rows, where row n contains the n smallest available numbers of primality opposite to that of n, subject to the restriction that in the whole triangle each number k can be used only k times.

Number of steps needed when starting from (3^(n+1))-1 and repeatedly applying the map that replaces k with k - (sum of digits in base-3 representation of k) to encounter the first number whose base-3 representation begins with a digit other than 2.
Irregular triangle T(n, k) of number of connected bisymmetric n X n matrices B_n with 0 or 1 entries, B_n[1,1] = 1 = B_n[1,n], and k islands of 0's.
Positive integers D such that the generalized Pell equation X^2 - D Y^2 = 2 is soluble.
a(1) = 1; a(n+1) is the smallest number not occurring earlier and coprime to Sum_{j=1..n} a(j).
Maximum number of distinct squares in arithmetic progression modulo prime(n).
Decimal expansion of Lehmer's constant (also known as the Salem constant).
a(n) is the smallest nonzero number that is not a substring of n in its binary representation.
In base 3, 0, together with numbers of the form i00j00k00m00... where i = 1 or 2 and j,k,m,... are 0, 1, or 2.
Successively add the smallest ternary number that is not a substring.

a(n) = smallest number (in absolute value) not yet in the sequence such that the arithmetic mean of the first n terms a(1), a(2), ..., a(n) is an integer; a(1)=1. No two numbers with the same absolute value may appear. Preference is given to positive values of a(n).

If n is even, divide by 2; otherwise, add the next larger prime.
Cubefree part of n.

Primes which divide numbers of the form 3^k + 2 for k >= 1.
The number of numbers with the same prime signature and set of distinct prime factors as n (including n).
a(n) = distance from n to nearest Fibonacci number.
Triangle read by rows: sum of digits of n in base k, for 2<=k<=n.
Order of 2 modulo the n-th prime.
Squares visited by a (1,3)-leaper on a spirally numbered board and moving to the lowest available unvisited square at each step, squares labelled >=0.
The prime q>=5 such that n divides p-q, where p>q is the least prime for which such a prime q exists.

Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = number of triangles of zeros with side length k in the XOR-triangle with first row generated from the binary expansion of n.
Numbers whose binary expansion generates rotationally symmetric XOR-triangles.
Scan the binary representation of n from left to right; at each 1, reverse the bits to the left and including this 1. The resulting binary representation is that of a(n).
Lexicographically earliest permutation of the positive integers such that a(n), a(n+1) and the product a(n)*a(n+1) have in common at least one identical substring.
Scan the binary representation of n from right to left; at each 1, reverse the bits to the right and excluding this 1. The resulting binary representation is that of a(n).
a(n) = Sum_{i+j>=m+1} d_i * d_j, where d_1 < ... < d_m are the divisors of n.

Numbers that are primitively represented by x^2 + xy + y^2.
Number of divisors of n that are not divisors of other divisors of n.
a(n) is the integer k in the interval [2,n] at which log(n)*log(k) is closest to an integer.
Numbers k such that k divides 2^4 + 3^4 + 5^4 + ... + prime(k)^4.

Irregular table read by rows: the first entry of n-th row is length of run of rightmost identical bits (either 0 or 1, equal to n mod 2), followed by length of the next run of bits, etc., in the binary representation of n, when scanned from the least significant to the most significant end.
The array L(n,k) of Barcucci et al. (2021) read by antidiagonals.
Maximum number of consecutive integers starting at n such that any pair (k, k+1) among these shares at least one digit with its sum k + (k+1) = 2k + 1.
Numbers k such that k and number of divisors d(k) are relatively prime.
For any nonnegative number n with runs in binary expansion (r_1, ..., r_w), a(n) = Sum_{k = 1..w} 2^(r_1 + ... + r_k - 1).
a(n) is multiplicative with a(p^e) = Sum_{d|e} p^(e-d).

The number of two-term Egyptian fractions of rational numbers, x/y, 0 < x/y < 1, ordered as below.  The sequence is the number of (p,q) pairs such that x/y = 1/p + 1/q where p and q are integers with p < q.

The number of three-term Egyptian fractions of rational numbers x/y, 0 < x/y < 1, ordered as below. The sequence is the number of (p,q,r) such that x/y = 1/p + 1/q + 1/r where p, q, and r are integers with p < q < r.

The number of four-term Egyptian fractions of rational numbers, x/y, 0 < x/y < 1, ordered as below. The sequence is the number of (p,q,r,s) such that x/y = 1/p + 1/q + 1/r + 1/s where p, q, r, and s are integers with p < q < r < s.
Sum of (1+e)-divisors of n. Let n = Product_i p(i)^r(i) then (1+e)-sigma(n) = Product_i (1 + Sum_{s|r(i)} p(i)^s).
There are a(n) numbers m such that 1 <= m <= n and gcd(m,n) is cubefree.
Number of distinct values that can be produced by splitting n and adding the parts.
Expansion of Sum_{k>=1} k * x^k / (1 - x^(2*k))^2.
a(n) = sigma(n) * mu(n).
Primorial mod sum-of-primes.

Triangle read by rows: row 1 is [1]; for n >= 1, row n gives coefficients of expansion of (-1 - x + x^2 + x^3)*(1 + x + x^2 + x^3)^(n-1) in order of increasing powers of x.
Numbers k such that there is a number m with m + s_4(m) = k, where s_b(m) = sum of digits in base-b expansion of m.
Modified lexicographic ordering of all pairs i,j with 1 <= i <= j; every pair i,j of positive integers occurs exactly once.

Numbers whose decimal digits are in strictly increasing order.

a(n) is the smallest integer k such that n*k is the smallest multiple of k with twice as many divisors as k, or 0 if no such number is possible.
Triangle read by rows, T(n,k) = (-1)^k*(2*n)!*P[n,k](1/(n+1)) where P is the P-transform, for n>=0 and 0<=k<=n.
Triangle read by rows, T(n,k) = (-1)^k*(2*n)!*P[n,k](n/(n+1)) where P is the P-transform, for n>=0 and 0<=k<=n.

Inventory of positions as an irregular table; row 0 contains 0, subsequent rows contain the 0-based positions of 0's, followed by the position of 1's, of 2's, etc. in prior rows flattened.
a(n) is the maximum Hamming weight of squares k^2 in the range 2^n <= k^2 < 2^(n+1).
a(n) is the smallest k such that the square root of k*n rounds to a prime.
Numbers k such that the largest square dividing k is a unitary divisor of k.

Number of partitions of n in which the sequence of the sum of the same summands is increasing.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct numbers such that no sum of consecutive terms is a square or higher power of an integer.
a(1) = 1, and for any n > 0, a(n+1) is the k-th positive number not yet in the sequence, where k is the Hamming weight of a(n).
Decimal expansion of value of the continued fraction 1/(2+3/(4+5/(6+7/....
List of free polycubes in binary code (see comments), ordered first by the number of cells, then by the value of the binary code.
Least m > 0 such that n - m divides n^2 + m.
Number of steps for iteration of map x -> (5/3)*floor(x) to reach an integer > n when started at n, or -1 if no such integer is ever reached.
Number of steps for iteration of map x -> (5/3)*round(x) to reach an integer > n when started at n, or -1 if no such integer is ever reached.

Numbers k such that if k = Product p_i^e_i then p_i = e_i for all i.

Length of the n-th maximal antirun of squarefree numbers differing by more than one.

Least nontrivial exponent e such that n is a substring of n^e.

a(0)=0, a(n)=1 if n is 1 or is a prime, otherwise sum of prime factors of n with multiplicity.
Length of the n-th maximal antirun of nonsquarefree numbers differing by more than one.
Number of primes congruent to 1 modulo 3 dividing n (with multiplicity).

Triangle read by rows, where T(n,k) is the coefficient of x^n*y^k in f(x,y) that satisfies f(x,y) = 1/(1-x)^2 + xy*f(x,y)^2.
Primes that divide at least one term in every Fibonacci sequence.

For an oriented graph D, let X_m(D) be the number of copies of D in a random tournament (i.e., a complete graph, each of whose edges is directed randomly with probability 1/2 for each direction) on m vertices. The variance of X_m(D) is a polynomial in m, and a(n) is the minimum degree of this polynomial over all weakly connected oriented graphs D on n vertices. a(n) = 0 if the variance of X_m(D) is identically 0 for some such D.
a(1) = 2; thereafter, if a(n-1) is prime then a(n) = prime(n) + 1; otherwise a(n) = 2*a(n-1) - 1.
If a(n-1) is not a prime, then a(n) = 2*a(n-1) + S; otherwise set S = -S and a(n) = prime(n) + S; start with a(1) = S = 1.
a(n) = floor(n/tau), where tau = (1 + sqrt(5))/2.
a(n) is the number of distinct positive integers that can be obtained by starting with n!, and optionally applying the operations square root, floor, and ceiling, in any order.
If n mod 2 = 0 then a(n) = floor(n^(1/3)) else a(n) = floor(n^(4/3)).
a(n) is the smallest k > 0 for which a nondegenerate integer-sided triangle (k, k + n, c >= k + n) with an integer area exists.
Size of the largest subset {x(1),x(2),...,x(k)} of {1,2,...,n} with the property that all differences |x(i)-x(j)| are distinct.
Numbers which are a power of their digital root.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that for any t and k, with k>=1, where t = a(n) = a(n+k) = a(n+2*k), only one occurrence of k, for a given t, appears anywhere in the sequence.

Let T_n be a rooted tree constructed in the following way. With k_0 = n as the root, let k_i be a vertex of depth i. For each prime divisor p of k_i, the children of k_i are those m = k_i + (-1)^i*k_i/p, where m >= 1 and m does not appear in the path from k_0 to k_i. a(n) is the number of paths in T_n.
Number of repeating Harshad algorithm steps until a non-Harshad number or a power of 10 is reached.
Numbers c such that a! * b! * c! is a perfect square for some 1 <= a < b < c.
a(n) is the first k such that the fractional part of k^(1/3) starts with n.
The number of irreducible balanced subsets of [n].
The number of partitions of [n] into a set of irreducible balanced subsets.

a(n) is the number of edges in the graph PG(n) with one node for each free n-celled polyiamond and edges between nodes corresponding to polyiamonds that can be obtained from each other by moving one cell, where the intermediate polyform (the set of cells remaining when the cell to be moved is detached) is not required to be a connected polyiamond.

a(n) is the number of edges in the graph PG(n) with one node for each free n-celled polyiamond and edges between nodes corresponding to polyiamonds that can be obtained from each other by moving one cell, where the intermediate polyform (the set of cells remaining when the cell to be moved is detached) is required to be a connected polyiamond.

Let PG(n) be the graph with one node for each free n-celled polyhex and edges between nodes corresponding to polyhexes that can be obtained from each other by moving one cell, where the intermediate polyform (the set of cells remaining when the cell to be moved is detached) is not required to be a connected polyhex. a(n) is the number of edges in PG(n).

a(n) = j if n is the j-th prime, else a(n) = k if n is the k-th composite.

Triangle of coefficients of characteristic polynomial of negative Pascal matrix with (i,j)-th entry -C(i+j-2,i-1).
Diagonals and antidiagonals of the prime-composite array, B(m,n) which are zeros from the Third Borve Conjecture.
a(n) = M(n) + m(n) for n >= 2, where M(n) = max{ a(i) + a(n-i): i = 1..n-1 }, m(n) = min{ a(i) + a(n-i): i = 1..n-1 }.
a(n) = M(n) - m(n) for n >= 2, where M(n) = max{ a(i) + a(n-i): i = 1..n-1 }, m(n) = min{ a(i) + a(n-i): i = 1..n-1 }.
Number of labeled spanning trees in the complete hypergraph on n vertices (all hyperedges having cardinality 2 or greater).
Last position reached by winner of n-th Littlewood Frog Race.
3-wave sequence starting with 1, 1, 1.
Number of antichains in the product of a fence poset with n elements and a chain with 3 elements; also number of paths with n turns when light is reflected from 4 glass plates.
Number of antichains in the product of a fence poset with n elements and a chain with 4 elements; also number of paths with n turns when light is reflected from 5 glass plates.

Alternating sums of vertically aligned numbers in Pascal's triangle: T(n,k) = C(n,k) - C(n-2,k-1) + C(n-4,k-2) - ... +- C(n-2[n/2],m).
n consecutive primes differ by 4 or more starting at a(n), or n consecutive primes with no twin primes.
a(n) is the minimal prime q such that n*(q+1)-1 is prime, that is, the smallest prime q so that n = (p+1)/(q+1) with p prime; or a(n) = -1 if no such q exists.
2nd level triangle related to Eulerian numbers and binomial transforms (triangle of Eulerian numbers is first level and triangle with Z(0,0)=1 and Z(n,k)=0 otherwise is 0th level).
A discrete version of the Mangoldt function: if n is prime then floor(log(n)) else 0.

Di-Boustrophedon transform of all 1's sequence: Fill in an array by diagonals alternating in the 'up' and 'down' directions. Each diagonal starts with a 1. When going in the 'up' direction the next element is the sum of the previous element of the diagonal and the previous two elements of the row the new element is in. When going in the 'down' direction the next element is the sum of the previous element of the diagonal and the previous two elements of the column the new element is in. The final element of the n-th diagonal is a(n).
Generalized Catalan array FS(3; n,r).
Boris Stechkin's function.
Least hypotenuse of n distinct Pythagorean triangles.

Number of inequivalent n-gons.
