Number of paths from (0,0) to (3n,0) that stay in first quadrant (but may touch horizontal axis), where each step is (2,1),(1,2) or (1,-1) and start with (2,1).
Triangular matrix, read by rows, that satisfies: T(n,k) = [T^2](n-1,k) when n>k>=0, with T(n,n) = (2*n+1).
Least k >= 2 with n^(kn) == n (mod kn), also n^(kn-1) == 1 (mod k).
a(n)=least positive integer not a(k) or a(k)+floor(k/2) for any k<n.
Smallest m greater than n such that m^2 contains n^2 in its decimal representation.
Triangular matrix, read by rows, where row n is formed from the first differences of row (n-1) of its inverse matrix square, with an appended '1' for the main diagonal.
Triangle read by rows: the numbers B_2(n,k) from the Harju and Nowotka paper.
Square array of expansions of 1/sqrt(1-4x-4*k*x^2), read by antidiagonals.
Riordan array (1/sqrt(1-6x+5x^2),(1-3x-sqrt(1-6x+5x^2))/(2x)).
Triangle of generalized central trinomial coefficients.
Cone C(n,m,k) read by planes and rows, for 1 <= k <= m <= n: minimal number of knights needed to cover a k X m X n board.
Triangular array read by rows: the n-th row contains the first n multiples of n not included earlier that are coprime to n-1 and n+1.
Least sum (n+1) + (n+2) + ... + (n+k) that is a multiple of the n-th triangular number, n(n+1)/2.
Sum of all n-digit multiples of n.
Triangle, read by rows, which shifts one column left under matrix inverse.
Symmetric number square associated to ceiling(k^n/n^k), read by antidiagonals.
First differences contain a(n) n's, in order, starting with a(0)=1.
a(1)=1, then a(n)=2*a(n-1) if n is prime, a(n)=2*a(n-1)+1 if n not prime.
T(n,k) = 2^k*binomial(n,2k+1), where 0 <= k <= floor((n-1)/2), n >= 1.
Number of integer solutions to n = x^2 + (2y)^2 + z(z+1)/2.

Let S_n be the infinite sequence formed by starting with n and repeatedly reversing the digits and adding 4 to get the next term. Sequence gives number of steps for S_n to reach a cycle, or -1 if no cycle is ever reached.
Start with 1 and repeatedly reverse the digits and add 1 to get the next term.
Define sequence S_n by: initial term = n, reverse digits and add 2 to get next term. It is conjectured that S_n always reaches a cycle. Sequence gives number of steps for S_n to reach a cycle.
Define sequence S_n by: initial term = n, reverse digits and add 3 to get next term. It is conjectured that S_n always reaches a cycle. Sequence gives number of steps for S_n to reach a cycle.
Triangle T(n,k) = T(n-1, k-1) + T(n-1, k) + Sum_{i >= 1} T(n-2*i, k-i), with T(n, 0) = T(n, n) = 1, read by rows.
Triangle where T(n,k) = n!/(n-k)!*[x^k] ( x/(2*x + log(1-x)) )^(n+1), for n>=k>=0, read by rows.
Triangle T that satisfies the matrix products: C*[T^-1]*C = T and T*[C^-1]*T = C, where C is Pascal's triangle.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of Schroeder paths of length 2n and having k platforms (i.e., UHD, UHHD, UHHHD, ..., where U=(1,1), D=(1,-1), H=(2,0)).
Benjamin Franklin's 16 X 16 magic square read by rows.
Triangle, read by rows, where T(n,k) = C( C(n+2,3) - C(k+2,3) + 2, n-k) for n>=k>=0.
Triangle, read by rows, where T(n,k) = C( C(n+2,3) - C(k+2,3) + 3, n-k) for n>=k>=0.
Triangle, read by rows, where row n lists coefficients of q in F(n,q) that satisfies: F(n,q) = Sum_{k=0..n-1} C(n-1,k)*F(k,q)*F(n-k-1,q)*q^k for n>0, with F(0,q) = 1.
Arithmetic mean of two consecutive balanced primes (of order one).
Arithmetic mean of two consecutive prime interprimes of second order: interprimes of third order.
Number of invariants in Hilbert basis for binary forms of degree n.
Triangle read by rows: row n (n>=0) has g.f. Sum_{i=1..n} n!*x^i*(1+x)^(n-i)/(n+1-i).
G.f. A(x) satisfies: [x^n] A(x)^(2^n) = 4^n for n>=0.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,0) = 1, T(n,k) = 3*binomial(n,k) if k>=0 (0<=k<=n).
Integral quotients of partial sums of primes divided by the number of summations.
a(0) = 2; for n > 0, a(n) = the smallest prime which is > a(n-1) such that a(n-1) + a(n) is a multiple of n.
G.f. L(x) satisfies: L(x) = L(exp(x)-1)*(1-exp(-x))/x = Sum_{n>=1} a(n)*x^n/(n!*(n+1)!).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = (2^(n+1)-1)*binomial(n,k).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,m) = 2^(m+1)*binomial(n,m) if m!=n, and T(n,n) = 2^(n+2)-3 .
a(n) = a(n-1) + a(n - 1 - number of even terms so far).
a(n) is the smallest positive integer such that the numerator of (Sum_{k=1..n} 1/a(k)) is prime (or 1).
a(1)=1, a(n) = (p-1)*a(n-1), if n is even, otherwise a(n) = p*a(n-2), where p = 5.
Number of subwords of length n in infinite word generated by a -> aab, b -> b.
a(n) = prime(n)!.
List of pairs (n,m) with n < m such that the decimal expansion of m is a cyclic shift of that of n and m^2 is a cyclic shift of n^2.
a(n) = n * binomial(n-1, floor((n-1)/2)) = n * max_{i=0..n} binomial(n-1, i).
Smallest square number with exactly n zero digits whose square root does not contain any zero digits.

Self-power numbers (or SPN's): numbers n with property that for each single digit d of n, we can also see the decimal expansion of the d-th power of some number as a substring of n and also n contains no 0's or 1's.
Number of permutation symbols of type a(n) for hyperbolic archimedean tessellations of rank n.
Weakly prime numbers (changing any one decimal digit always produces a composite number). Also called digitally delicate primes.
G.f. A(x) satisfies: A(x)^2 = 1/AGM(1, 1 - 8*x/A(x)^2 ).
Numerator of 1/64 - 1/n^2.
Primes p such that Floor[p/3]+p is prime.
Non-repdigit composite numbers not divisible by 2, 3, 5 or 11.
Triangle read by rows, left border = natural numbers repeated (1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, ...); all other columns = (1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, ...).
Number of times Sum_{i=1..u} J(i,4n+1) obtains value zero when u ranges from 1 to (4n+1). Here J(i,k) is the Jacobi symbol.
a(n) = First odd number 2k+1, for which Sum_{i=1..u} J(i,2k+1) obtains value zero exactly n times when u ranges from 1 to (2k+1). Here J(i,k) is the Jacobi symbol.
Primes congruent to {3, 5} mod 6.
a(n) = Sum_{i=0..(2n+1)} J(i,12n+7), where J(i,k) is the Jacobi symbol.
Irregular triangle read by rows: floor(j^2 / p) for p prime and j = 1 to p-1.
Exponential Riordan array [1+x*tan(x/2),x].
Exponential Riordan array [1+x*arctanh(x), x].
Positive integers n where (the largest divisor of n that is <= sqrt(n)) divides (the smallest divisor of n that is >= sqrt(n)).
Primes which are not the smallest or largest prime in an interval of the form (2*prime(k),2*prime(k+1)).

Number of partitions of n in SPM(n): these are the partitions obtained from (n) by iteration of the following transformation: p -> p' if p' is a partition (i.e., decreasing) and p' is obtained from p by removing a unit from the i-th component of p and adding one to the (i+1)-th component, for any i.
G.f.: S(x) = Sum_{n>=0} -log(1 - 2^(2n+1)*x)^(2n+1)/(2n+1)!, a power series in x with integer coefficients.
G.f.: C(x) = Sum_{n>=0} log(1 - 2^(2n)*x)^(2n)/(2n)!, a power series in x with integer coefficients.
Even numbers without 2.
Numbers that are prime or one less than a prime.
Sum of balanced ternary digits in n. Replace 3^k with 1 in balanced ternary expansion of n.
Number of perfect partitions of n.
Periodic sequence: repeat (1,64).
Decimal expansion of Golomb-Dickman constant.
Integers whose decimal representation consists of three distinct digits, one appearing once, one appearing twice, and one appearing three times.
Number of graphical partitions (degree-vectors for simple graphs with n vertices, or possible ordered row-sum vectors for a symmetric 0-1 matrix with diagonal values 0).
Inverse binomial transform of a math magic problem.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of permutations of {1,2,...,n} having exactly k entries that are midpoints of 321 patterns (0 <= k <= n-2 for n >= 2; k=0 for n=1).
Table of partitions that do not contain 1 as a part for even integers.
Table of the partitions that do not contain 1 as a part for odd integers.
Squarefree semiprimes together with primes.
Triangular array read by rows: [T(n,k),k=1..tau(n)] = [-n!/(d*(-(n/d)!)^d), d|n].
Generalized Bell numbers based on the rising factorial powers; square array read by antidiagonals.
Triangle of binomial coefficients binomial(3*n-k+1,3*n-3*k+1).
Even numbers k (written in binary) such that in base-2 lunar arithmetic, the sum of the divisors of k is a number containing a 0 (in binary).
Triangle of binomial coefficients binomial(3*n-k,3*n-3*k).

Number of permutations of [n] having exactly 1 circular succession. A circular succession in a permutation p of [n] is either a pair p(i), p(i+1), where p(i+1)=p(i)+1 or the pair p(n), p(1) if p(1)=p(n)+1.
a(n) = [n*u+n*v]-[n*u]-[n*v], where u=e, v=1/e, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u+n*v]-[n*u]-[n*v], where u=sqrt(2), v=1/u, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u+n*v]-[n*u]-[n*v], where u=sqrt(3), v=1/u, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u+n*v]-[n*u]-[n*v], where u=sqrt(5), v=1/u, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u + n*v] - [n*u] - [n*v], where u=sqrt(6), v=1/u, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u + n*v] - [n*u] - [n*v], where u=sqrt(7), v=1/u, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u + n*v] - [n*u] - [n*v], where u=sqrt(8), v=1/u, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u + n*v] - [n*u] - [n*v], where u=sin(Pi/3), v=cos(Pi/3), and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u + n*v] - [n*u] - [n*v], where u=sin(Pi/5), v=cos(Pi/5), and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u + n*v] - [n*u] - [n*v], where u=sin(2*Pi/5), v=cos(2*Pi/5), and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u+n*v] - [n*u] - [n*v], where u=sin(Pi/8), v=cos(Pi/8), and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u + n*v] -[n*u] -[n*v], where u=1/2, v=(1+sqrt(5))/2, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u + n*v] - [n*u] - [n*v], where u=e^(Pi/2), v=1/u, and []=floor.
a(n) = [n*u+n*v]-[n*u]-[n*v], where u=sqrt(2), v=sqrt(3), and []=floor.
a(n) = [nu+nv]-[nu]-[nv], where u=sqrt(2), v=2u, and []=floor.
Second term in continued fraction for zeta(n).
[(bn+c)r]-b[nr]-[cr], where (r,b,c)=(golden ratio,4,0) and []=floor.
Number of ways of writing n as a sum of 6 squares.
a(n) = [(b*n+c)*r] - b*[n*r] - [c*r], where (r,b,c)=(sqrt(3),2,0) and [ ] = floor.
Triangle T read by rows: matrix product of Pascal and Catalan triangle.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules: a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 2x-1 and 3x-1 are in a.
a(n) = [2*n*e] - 2*[n*e], where [ ] = floor and e is the natural logarithm base.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 2x and 3x-1 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 2x and 3x+1 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 2x and 3x+2 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 2x+1 and 3x-1 are in a.
Smallest multiple of n with more than twice as many divisors as n.

Consider a cellular automaton on the square grid where we start at time 1 with a finite collection of cells in state 1 and with all cells in state 0. At any time t, if a cell is in state 0 and the sum of the states of its neighborhood is t, the cell switches to state t. At any time t, if no cell switches to state t, the growth stops. The sequence gives the largest lifetime of any configuration starting from n cells which are rook connected.
Triangle T(n,k) (n >= 2, 1 <= k <= n) read by rows: number of linearly inducible orderings of n points in k-dimensional Euclidean space.
Base-2 digital convolution sequence.
Smallest positive k such that n+k(n-1) is prime.
Numbers that are not the sum of 2 nonzero squares.
The odd numbers as a triangle read by rows.
Nonlinear recurrence: a(n) = a(n-1) + (a(n-1)+1)*Product_{j=1..n-2} a(j).
a(n) = least m such that if a/b < c/d where a,b,c,d are integers in [0,n], then a/b < k/m < c/d for some integer k.
Rectangular array of numbers Fibonacci(m(n+1))/Fibonacci(m), m >= 1, n >= 0, read by downward antidiagonals.
Number of terms in Lucas representations of 1,2,...,n.
Triangle where the g.f. for row n equals  d^n/dx^n (1+x+x^2)^n / n!  for n>=0, as read by rows.
Sum of the least divisors of n whose LCM is equal to n.
Irregular triangle read by rows: row n gives list Q(n) of LCMs of 'array-admissible' sets for n.
List of those primes p with p + 2 and 2*p - 5 both prime.
Sum of two digits touching a comma = difference between the two terms separated by that comma; start with a(0)=0, a(1)=5. If there is a choice, choose the smaller value for a(n).
Sorting numbers: maximal number of comparisons for sorting n elements by list merging.
Stone skipping numbers.
Sum of digits in periodic part of decimal expansion of 1/prime(n).
Number of parts in all partitions of n into even number of distinct parts.
Number of ways to place n nonattacking bishops on an n X n board.
Number of ways to place n nonattacking semi-bishops on an n X n board.
Primes of the form p^2 + p + 1 when p is prime.
Rectangular array with all start numbers Me(n, k), k >= 1, for the Collatz operation ud^(2*n), n >= 1, ending in an odd number, read by antidiagonals.
Triangle read by rows, generalized ballot numbers, 0<=k<=n.
Numbers m > 1 such that a record number of numbers k have m as the sum of the proper divisors of k.
a(n) = Sum_{j=0..k-1} (i(j) - j) where n = Sum_{j=0..k-1} 2^i(j).
Number of 1's in n-th generation of 1-D CA using Rule 110, started with a single 1.
Number of ON cells in 3-D cellular automaton described in Comments, after n generations.
Least k such that Lppf(k) > Gpf(k) + n, where Lppf(k) is the largest prime power factor of k and Gpf(k) is the greatest prime factor of k.
Positions of ones in binary expansion of 1/sqrt(2).

(Product of all composite numbers from 1 to n)/ ( product of the prime divisors of all composite numbers up to n). More precisely, denominator = product of the largest squarefree divisors of composite numbers up to n.
a(n) is the smallest integer m such that m-n is composite and phi(m-n) + sigma(m+n) = 2*m.
a(n) is the smallest integer m such that m-n is composite and phi(m+n) + sigma(m-n) = 2*m.
a(n) is the smallest integer m such that m-n is composite and phi(m-n) + sigma(m+n) = phi(m+n) + sigma(m-n).
a(n) = Fibonacci(6*n + 3)/2.
The curvature (rounded down) of touching circles inscribed in a special way in the smaller segment of circle of radius 10/9 divided by a chord of length 4/3.

Triangle t(n,k) = t(n,k-2) + 2 if n > 1 and 2 <= k <= n;  t(0,0) = 1, t(1,0) = 2, t(1,1) = 3; if n > 1 is odd, then t(n,0) = t(n-1,n-2) + 2 and t(n,1) = t(n-1,n-1) + 2; if n > 1 is even, then t(n,0) = t(n-1,n-1) + 2 and t(n,1) = t(n-1,n-2) + 2.
a(n) = floor(prime(n)^(1+1/n)) - prime(n+1).
a(n) = floor(prime(n)^(1+1/n)) - prime(n).
Array A read by upward antidiagonals in which the entry in row n and column k is defined by A(n,k) = (1 + 2^n*(6*k-3+2*(-1)^n))/3, n,k >= 1.
Positive cubefree integers n such that the Diophantine equation X^3 + Y^3 = n*Z^3 has solutions.
Octanacci numbers.
Triangle in which the n-th row contains n distinct semiprimes not listed previously with all prime factors from among the first n primes.
a(n) is the least integer k such that some multiple of sqrt(k) falls strictly between n and n+1.
Coefficient of x^n in (Product_{m=1..n}(1-x^m))^n.

a(1) = 1; for n > 1, let s denote the binary representation of a(n-1) with the first bit omitted. Then a(n) is the smallest number not yet present whose binary representation starts with s, omitting leading zeros.
a(n) = coefficient of x^(2n) in the expansion of the modular form Product_{k>=1} (1-x^k)^n.
a(n) = coefficient of x^n in the expansion of  Product_{k>=1} (1-x^k)^(3*n).
Number of ordered triples (u,v,w) of palindromes such that u+v+w = n.
Numbers k not divisible by 5 such that k^2 written in base 5 has no digit > 1.
Group the natural numbers such that the n-th group contains n terms and the group sum is the smallest possible prime.
Concatenation of 1, 00, 111, 0000, ..., n 1's (if n is odd) or n 0's (if n is even).

Predestined numbers: every n number is generated by at least one pair of products, such as n = a*b = c*d, and the multiset of the digits of a and b coincides with the multiset of the digits of c and d.
Numbers n for which (prime(n+1)-prime(n)) is not a multiple of three.
Numbers n for which prime(n+1)-prime(n) is a multiple of three.
Least prime p such that n = p + q - r for some primes q and r with q > p.
Artiads: the primes p == 1 (mod 5) for which Fibonacci((p-1)/5) is divisible by p.
a(1) = 1; thereafter a(2k) = 4k + a(k); a(2k+1) = k + a(4k+4).
Decimal expansion of 2^(3/2) / (sqrt(Pi)*Gamma(3/4)^2).
Run lengths in the binary expansion of n-1 gives the vector of exponents in prime factorization of a(n), with the least significant run corresponding to the exponent of the least prime, 2.
Numbers n such that n-1 has the same number of prime factors as n (with multiplicity).
Square array A(n,k): A(0, n) = n; A(k, n) = A(k-1, floor(n*(k+1)/k)), for k >= 1, read by descending antidiagonals as A(0,0), A(0,1), A(1,0), A(0,2), A(1,1), A(2,0), ...
Square array constructed from Flavius sieve, shifted version, read by descending antidiagonals.
Triangle giving the area of primitive Pythagorean triangles, with zero entries for non-primitive triangles.
Distance from the origin using the binary expansion of Pi to walk the number line: Start at the origin; subtract one for each '0' digit, and add one for each '1' digit.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->001, 1->011, starting with 00.
Denominator of Sum_{k=0..n^2-1} (-1)^k*sqrt(Pi)/(Gamma(1/2-k)*Gamma(1+k))/n.
Beatty sequence for sqrt(10).
Beatty sequence for sqrt(12).
Fixed point of the mapping 00->001, 1->100, starting with 00.
Fixed point of the mapping 00->001, 1->101, starting with 00.
Triangle T(n,k) read by rows: coefficients of polynomials P_n(t) defined in Formula section.
Expansion of q^(1/24) * eta(q) / eta(q^2) in powers of q.
Coefficients in expansion of E_4/E_2.
Alternating sum of ternary digits in n. Replace 3^k with (-1)^k in ternary expansion of n.
Coefficients of the Omega polynomials of order 2, triangle T(n,k) read by rows with 0<=k<=n.
The lexicographically earliest increasing sequence such that a(n) divides the sum of the first a(n)+1 terms.
a(n) = Sum_{2^m divides n} 2^(3*m).
a(n) = Sum_{j=1..n} floor(j*sqrt(10)); n-th partial sum of Beatty sequence for sqrt(10).
a(n) = Sum_{d|n, d == 3 (mod 4)} d.
Sum of divisors of n that are not of the form 4k+1.
Sum of nonsquare divisors of n.
a(n) = n*denominator(n*Bernoulli(n-1))/denominator(Bernoulli(n-1)).
Least k such that sigma(1) + sigma(2) + sigma(3) +...+ sigma(k) >= n.
Sum of divisors of n weighted by divisor multiplicity in n.
T(n, k) = n! * [x^k] [y^n] sec(z)(x + z*sin(z)/y) where z = y*sqrt(x^2 - 1) for 0 <= k <= n+1 and T(-1, 0) = 1, triangle read by rows.
a(n) is the X-coordinate of the n-th nonattacking queen placed by a greedy algorithm on N^3 (see Comments for details).
Generalized Blasius numbers, square array read by ascending antidiagonals, A(n, k) for n, k >= 0.
Fill an array by antidiagonals upwards; in the top left cell enter a(0)=1; thereafter, in the n-th cell, enter the sum of the entries of those earlier cells that can be seen from that cell.
a(n) is the exponent of the eventual power of 2 reached when starting from n and using the map k -> k + k/p, where p can be any odd prime factor of k, for example, the largest.
4-dimensional centered cube numbers.
r3(n): Size of the largest subset of the numbers [1...n] which does not contain a 3-term arithmetic progression.
Number of iterations of map x -> (x - (largest divisor d < x)) needed to reach 1 or a prime, when starting at x = n.
T(n, k) is the greatest positive integer m such that m^k divides n; square array T(n, k), n, k > 0 read by antidiagonals downwards.
Number of outcomes of unlabeled n-team round-robin tournaments.
Numbers of the form p^q where p and q are either 1 or prime.
First occurrences of gaps between primes 6k - 1: gap sizes.
Let x(n, k) be the exponent of prime(k) in the factorization of n, then a(n) = Max_{k} abs(x(n,k)- x(n-1,k)).
Side length s of the central triangle of zeros in the XOR-triangle T(n).
Let p be the smallest prime not dividing the squarefree part of n. Multiply n by p and divide by the product of all smaller primes.
a(n) is the smallest k > 1 such that there are more primes in the interval [(k-1)*n + 1, k*n] than there are in the interval [(k-2)*n + 1, (k-1)*n].
a(n) is the smallest positive integer such that a(n)*(1^n + 2^n + ... + x^n) is a polynomial in x with integer coefficients.
Let S(n,k) denote the set of primes < 10^n which are the sum of k consecutive primes, and let K = maximum k >= 2 such that S(n,k) is nonempty; then a(n) = max S(n,K).
a(n) is the largest prime < 10^n that is the sum of at least two consecutive primes.
a(n) = k where Z_k is the largest Zimin word that n (read as a binary word) does not avoid.
Number of one bits in binary representation of base i-1 expansion of n (where i = sqrt(-1)).
Numbers that have exactly two different representations as polygonal numbers.
7-smooth numbers not divisible by 10: positive numbers whose prime divisors are all <= 7 but do not contain both 2 and 5.
Number of times the Collatz plot started at n crosses the y = n line, or -1 if the number of crossings is infinite.
The Redstone permutation: a(1) = 2, a(2) = 1, otherwise the smallest number not occurring earlier which is strongly prime to n.
a(n) = Sum_{k = 0..n} binomial(n,floor(k/2))*(-1)^(n-k).
Initial members of prime septuplets (p, p+2, p+6, p+8, p+12, p+18, p+20).
a(n) is the remainder when (n written backwards) is divided by n.
a(n) is the number of ways n can be reached in the following method: we start with 1, then add or multiply alternately, and each operand must be 2 or 3.

Inventory of positions ordered by binary lengths of terms, as an irregular table; the first row contains 1, subsequent rows contains the 1-based positions of terms with binary length 1, followed by positions of terms with binary length 2, 3, etc. in prior rows flattened.

Inventory of positions ordered by odd parts of terms, as an irregular table; the first row contains 1, subsequent rows contains the 1-based positions of terms with odd part 1, followed by positions of terms with odd part 3, 5, etc. in prior rows flattened.

Partial inventory of positions as an irregular table; rows 1 and 2 contain 1, for n > 2, row n contains the 1-based positions of 1's, followed by the positions of 2's, 3's, etc. in rows n-2 and n-1 flattened.

Partial inventory of positions as an irregular table; rows 1 and 2 contain 1, for n > 2, row n contains the 1-based positions of 1's, followed by the positions of 2's, 3's, etc. in rows n-1 and n-2 flattened.
Array read by antidiagonals: let V(m,n) = Sum_{i=1..m, j=1..n, gcd(i,j)=1} (m+1-i)*(n+1-j), then T(m,n) = 2*m*n+m+n+2*V(m,n), for m >= 0, n >= 0.
Array read by antidiagonals: T(n,k) (n>=0, k>=0) = number of lines defining the Farey diagram Farey(n,k) of order (n,k).
Array read by antidiagonals: T(n,k) (n>=0, k>=0) = number of decreasing lines defining the Farey diagram Farey(n,k) of order (n,k).
Least positive integer N such that n+N has the same digits as n and N together (without counting repetitions).
Matula-Goebel number of the n-th standard ordered rooted tree.
a(n) is the number of ways to write n = i^2 + 2*j^2 + 3*k^2 with i,j,k >= 0.
The largest unitary divisor of n that is a cube.
Number of convergent Boolean relation matrices on [n].
Product of a prime and the previous number.
Expansion of q*Product_{k>=1} (1-q^k)^2*(1-q^(11*k))^2.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = Sum_{y=1..n} Sum_{x=1..n} [GCD(f(x,y), n) = k], where f(x,y) = x^3 - x^2 - y^2 - y.
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; for n > 1, a(n) = smallest positive number which has not yet appeared which has a common factor with a(n-2) + a(n-1).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = Sum_{y=1..n} Sum_{x=1..n} [GCD(f(x,y), n) = k], where f(x,y) = x^2 - y^2.
Hypotenuse numbers w of Pythagorean triples (u, v, w) for which (u^2, v^2, w^2) is an 'abc-hit'.
The number of edges minus the number of leaves in the rooted tree with Matula-Goebel number n.
Dirichlet g.f.: 1 / (zeta(s) * zeta(s-1) * (1 - 2^(-s))).
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = n*(k - 1) - k*(k - 3)/2 with 0 < k <= n.
Array read by ascending antidiagonals: p is a term of row A(n) if and only if p is a prime and p is a quadratic residue modulo prime(n).
Greatest number of runs in a permutation of the prime factors of n.
Irregular triangle read by rows: coefficients of polynomial P(n,x) (exponents in increasing order).
Triangle read by rows where T(n,k) is the number of integer compositions of n whose leaders of weakly decreasing runs sum to k.
Decimal expansion of Sum_{p prime} 1/(p*(p-1)).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = T(n-1,k-1) + T(n-1,k), 0 < k < n with T(n,0) = n and T(n,n) = -n.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the product of two consecutive terms is always a factorial number.
Riordan array (1,(1-2x-sqrt(1-4x))/(2x)).
Squarefree numbers > 1.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that if a digit d in the digit stream (ignoring commas) is even, the previous digit is < d.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that if a digit d in the digit stream (ignoring commas) is even, the previous digit is > d.
Number of ways to permute the prime indices of n so that the run-lengths are all equal.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that if a digit d in the digit stream (ignoring commas) is odd, the previous digit is > d.

Values of u in the quartets (3, u, v, w) of type 3; i.e., values of u for solutions to 3*(3 - u) = v*(v - w), in distinct positive integers, with v > 1, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.

Values of u in the quartets (4, u, v, w) of type 3; i.e., values of u for solutions to 4*(4 - u) = v*(v - w), in distinct positive integers, with v > 1, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
Length of shortest loop (in Chebyshev distance) that touches all cells in an n X n grid.
Heinz number of first sums minus 1 of the 1-prepended prime indices of n.
Smallest b >= 2 for which P_{n}(b) = Sum_{k=1..n} b^(prime(n)-prime(k)) is prime or 0 if such a number does not exist.
Sum of two or more consecutive prime numbers.
Partial product of prime gaps: a(n) = a(n-1)*(prime(n+1) - prime(n)).
Number of divisors of n which are not primorials.

Keys added to a map T initialized with T[1] = 1 and updated at each iteration according to T[value] := (T[value] if defined else 0) + key, for all (key, value) pairs already in T; listed in order the keys are added to the map (cf. comments for details).

Irregular triangular array read by rows: the first row is 1, 2. Thereafter, if the last entry of the previous row has greatest prime factor p, the next row is formed from the p smallest unused positive multiples of p.
Recursively defined symmetric multiplication table read by antidiagonals: A(n,k), n>=1, k>=1.
Array read by ascending antidiagonals: A(0,k) = 0 and A(n,k) = A(n-1,k)^2 + k for n > 0.
Irregular triangle read by rows in which row n lists the number of divisions by 2 after tripling steps in the Collatz 3x+1 trajectory of 2n+1 until it reaches 1.
a(n) = second-smallest prime p <= n such that 2n - p is also prime, or 0 if fewer than two such primes exist.
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k + 1) = T(n, k) * (n + k) / (n * (k + 1)) for k <= n, starting at T(n, 0) = n^n, (row recurrence).
Minimum site perimeter of a polyknight with n cells.
Expansion of g.f. Product_{k >= 1} (1 - x^k)^(-k*(k+1)/2).
Nonnegative integers n such that n^2*(n+1)*(2*n+1)^2*(7*n+1)/36 is a square.
Position of rightmost 0 in 2^n increases.
Position of rightmost 0 (including leading 0) in 2^n increases.
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = [x^k] x*Pochhammer(n + x, n)/(n + x).
a(n) = 2*binomial(3*n, n) - Sum_{k=0..n} binomial(3*n, k).
a(0) = 0; for n >= 0, a(n+1) = a(n) + x where x is the smallest nonnegative number that is not equal to a(i) +- a(k) for any 0 <= i <= n, 0 <= k <= n.
a(n) is smallest difference d of an arithmetic progression dk+1 whose first prime occurs at the n-th position.
Cumulative counting sequence: method B (noun,adjective)-pairs with first term 0.
Triangle T(n,k) of number of rooted trees with n nodes and k leaves, 1 <= k <= n.
Triangle of trees with n nodes and k leaves, 2 <= k <= n.
Triangle read by rows: number of mobiles (circular rooted trees) with n nodes and k leaves.
Triangle of asymmetric mobiles (circular rooted trees) with n nodes and k leaves.
a(n) = least nonnegative integer h such that (n,h) is not collinear with any 2 points in the set S(n-1) := {(m,a(m)), (m,b(m)): m = 0,1,...,n-1} for n >= 1.
Coefficient triangle for certain polynomials.
a(1) = 1 and for n > 1 let a(n) = a(n-1) + m, where m is the arithmetic mean of the largest subset of all predecessors such that m is an integer and m is maximal.
Triangle read by rows giving successive states of cellular automaton generated by 'Rule 62'.
Triangle read by rows giving successive states of cellular automaton generated by 'Rule 126'.
Numbers which are multiples of their largest digit (decimal notation).
a(n) = the maximum number of lattice points touched by an origin-centered circle with radius <= n.
a(n) = the maximum number of lattice points touched by an origin-centered sphere with radius <= n.
a(n) is the maximum number of lattice points touched by an origin-centered 4d-sphere with radius <= n.
GCD of n-th primorial number and its totient.
Discriminants of real quadratic fields with unique factorization.
Number of distinct prime factors in binomial(2*n,n).
Runs have lengths 2^n, n >= 0.
Triangle in which first row is {1}; to get n-th row take first n numbers greater than last number in previous row which are relatively prime to n.
A repetition-resistant sequence.
Costé prime expansion of Pi - 3.
Costé prime expansion of e - 2.
Costé prime expansion of sqrt(2) - 1.
Costé prime expansion of Pi^2 - 9.
Costé prime expansion of (sqrt(5)-1)/2.
Costé prime expansion of 2^(1/3) - 1.
Costé prime expansion of sqrt(3) - 1.

Consider the triangle shown below in which the n-th row contains the n smallest terms in increasing order having a common factor > 1, the first term being the n-th composite number; sequence gives the last term of each row.

Consider a triangle in which the 2n-th row contains first 2n positive integers in increasing order and the (2n+1)-st row contains first 2n+1 positive integers in decreasing order; sequence contains concatenation of numbers read upward at a 45-degree angle.
Smallest number such that there are exactly n numbers between a(n) and a(n+1) with n divisors.
Least number > n having one more prime factor than n, not necessarily distinct.
Least number > n having one more distinct prime factor than n.
Number of bounded (<=n) lunar divisors of n.
Multiples of 11.
Replace 2^k in the binary representation of n with k (i.e., if n = 2^b + 2^c + 2^d + ... then a(n) = b + c + d + ...).
Central quadrinomial coefficients: largest coefficient of (1 + x + x^2 + x^3)^n.
Plaindromes: numbers whose digits in base 3 are in nondecreasing order.
Triangle read by rows: n-th row is the smallest set of n numbers in arithmetic progression with the same prime signature.

Define dd(n) = the number formed by concatenating the absolute difference of successive digits. Sequence contains primes p such that dd(p) is also prime. (Primes in which the number formed by successive digit difference is also a prime.).
Consider recurrence b(0) = n/4, b(k) = b(k-1)*floor(b(k-1)); sequence gives number of steps to reach an integer, or -1 if no integer is ever reached.
a(n) = abs(a(n-1) - floor(n*phi)), where phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2, with a(1) = a(2) = 1.
Numbers k for which the quotient q(k)=(k+rev(k))/abs(k-rev(k)) is an integer.
Integers m of the form 4k+3 for which all sums Sum_{i=1..u} J(i/m) (with u ranging from 1 to (m-1)) are nonnegative, where J(i/m) is Jacobi symbol of i and m.

Odd primes p for which all sums Sum_{i=1..u} L(i/p) (with u ranging from 1 to (p-1)) are nonnegative, where L(i/p) is Legendre symbol of i and p, defined to be 1 if i is a quadratic residue (mod p) and -1 if i is a quadratic non-residue (mod p).
Sum of the product of the first ceiling(n/2) odd-indexed primes and the product of the first floor(n/2) even-indexed primes; a(1) = 2.
Absolute difference between the product of the first floor(n/2) even-indexed primes and the product of the first floor(n/2) odd-indexed primes.
Image of 1,1,1,... under the map Q.
Sum of diving indices of all 4k+3 primes in range ]2^n,2^(n+1)].
Sum of maximal Dyck path prefix lengths of all 4k+3 primes in range ]2^n,2^(n+1)].
Sum of diving indices of all 4k+3 integers in range ]2^n,2^(n+1)].
Sum of maximal Motzkin path prefix-lengths of all 4k+3 integers in range ]2^n,2^(n+1)].
Modified juggler map: for even numbers: a(n) = floor(n^(2/3)) and for odd n: a(n) = floor(n^(3/2)) = floor(sqrt(n^3)).
Excess of total number of distinct prime factor digits of n-th repunit over n, the number of digits of n-th repunit itself.
Numerators in Kepler's tree of harmonic fractions.
Maximally asymmetric odd primes in binary.
Second pentagonal numbers: a(n) = n*(3*n + 1)/2.
Largest primitive root modulo n, or 0 if no root exists.
Polynomials interpolating their own integral coefficients, read by row. The leading coefficients are positive and minimal.
A triangle with palindromic cubes, read by rows.
Numbers k such that sum of even digits of k is less than sum of odd digits.
Sum of even digits greater than sum of odd digits.
a(n) is the next natural number (besides 1) which is not congruent to a(i) mod a(j) for any i < j < n.
a(n) = Sum_{p^e | n} F(p^e), where each p^e is the highest power of prime p dividing n (with e > 0), and F(k) is the k-th Fibonacci number.
The following triangle contains n smallest numbers with the prime signature of n!. Sequence contains the triangle by rows.
Sum_{d<n is a divisor of n} tau(n-d).
The n-th row of the following triangle contains n distinct numbers with prime signature of n not included earlier. Sequence contains the triangle read by rows.

Consider the triangle shown below in which the n-th row contains the n smallest numbers greater than those in the previous row such that the arithmetic mean is an integer. Sequence contains the leading diagonal.
Order of the domain D_n (n >= 0) in the inverse limit domain D_infinity.
Nodes in riff (rooted index-functional forest) for n.
Triangle P, read by rows, that satisfies [P^-1](n,k) = P(n+1,k+1) for n >= k >= 0, with P(k,k)=1 and P(k+1,1)=P(k+1,0) for k >= 0, where [P^-1] denotes the matrix inverse of P.
a(n) is the least prime p such that n*p#-1 is prime.
Number triangle T(n,k) = Sum_{j=0..n-k} C(k,3j)*C(n-k,3j).

Let S_n be the infinite sequence formed by starting with n and repeatedly reversing the digits and adding 16 to get the next term. Sequence gives number of steps for S_n to reach a cycle, or -1 if no cycle is ever reached.
Triangle T(n,k) = n!/(n-k)! (0 <= k <= n) read by rows, giving number of permutations of n things k at a time.
a(1) = 1, a(n) = number of divisors of n*a(n-1).
Decimal expansion of largest real root of e^x = Gamma(x+1).

Let T(S,Q) be the sequence obtaining by starting with S and repeatedly reversing the digits and adding Q to get the next term. a(n) is the number of steps for T(n,5) to reach a cycle, or -1 if no cycle is ever reached.
Triangle of denominators of the cube of a certain lower triangular matrix.
Triangle of numerators of the cube of a certain lower triangular matrix.

Rectangular table, read by antidiagonals, defined by the following rule: start with all 1's in row zero; from then on, row n+1 equals the partial sums of row n excluding terms in columns k = m*(m+1)/2 (m>=1).
Triangle, read by rows, defined by: T(n,k) = Sum_{j=0..n-k-1} T(j+k,k)*T(n-j,k+1) for n > k >= 0, with T(n,n) = n+1.
Number of iterations needed before a previous value is reached in the Collatz variation: x_{i+1} = 3x_i+(2n+1) if x_i is odd or x_i/2 if x_i is even, with x_0 = 1.
First tetrahedral coordinate; repeat m (m+1)*(m+2)/2 times.
Second tetrahedral coordinate.
Third tetrahedral coordinate, i.e., tetrahedron with T(t,n,k)=k; succession of growing finite triangles with increasing values towards bottom right.
a(n) = Sum_{d divides n} phi(d)*phi(n/d).
Signature-permutation of Callan's 2006 bijection on Dyck Paths.
a(n) is the coefficient of the linear term in the polynomial (x-prime(n))*(x-prime(n+1))*(x-prime(n+2))*(x-prime(n+3))*(x-prime(n+4)).

Triangle, read by rows of n*(n+1)/2 + 1 terms, generated by the following rule: start with a single '1' in row n=0; subsequently, row n+1 equals the partial sums of row n with the final term repeated n+1 more times at the end.
a(n) is the smallest positive integer which does not occur earlier in the sequence and is such that Sum_{k=1..n} 1/a(k) has a numerator which is prime (or is 1).
a(n) is the smallest positive integer which does not occur earlier in the sequence and is such that Sum_{k=1..n} 1/a(k) has a numerator which is composite (or is 1).
a(1)=1. a(2)=2. For n>=3, a(n) is the smallest positive integer not occurring earlier in the sequence such that (Sum_{k=1..n} a(k)) divides Product_{j=1..n} a(j).

Triangle, read by rows of (n+1)*(n+2)/2 terms, generated by the following rule. Start with a single '1' in row n=0; from then on, obtain row n from row n-1 by inserting zeros in row n-1 at positions: {(j+1)*n - j*(j-1)/2 | j=0..n} and then take partial sums.
Pure hailstone primes.
Least k such that k*2^n - 1 is prime.
a(1) = 2, a(n) = a(n-1)^prime(n) for n > 1.
Triangle of numbers of coincidence-free length n-m lists of m-tuples with all numbers 1,...,n-m in tuple position k, for k=1..m.
Irregular triangle of Section I primes. Row n contains primes p with 2^n < p < 2^(n+1) and phi^n(p) = 2, where phi^n means n iterations of Euler's totient function.
'Magic' numbers: all numbers from 0 to 9 are magic; a number >= 10 is magic if it is divisible by the number of its digits and the number obtained by deleting the final digit is also magic.
a(n) = sum of positive divisors k of n with k <= sqrt(n).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = number of partitions of [1..k] into n nonempty clumps of sizes 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 (n >= 0, 0 <= k <= 5n).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = number of partitions of [1..k] into n nonempty clumps of sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 (n >= 0, 0 <= k <= 6n).
a(n) = 0 for n <= 4; for n >= 5, write n = 2^i + j, 0 <= j < 2^i; if j <= 2^i-2 then a(n) = 2*a(j) + a(j+1); if j = 2^i-1 then a(n) = 2*a(j) + a(j+1) + 1.
Utterly odd numbers: numbers whose binary representation ends in an odd number of ones.
G.f.: A(x) = exp( Sum_{n>=1} 2^(n^2) * x^n/n ), a power series in x with integer coefficients.
a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} binomial(n,k) * gcd(k,n).
a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} binomial(n,k) * gcd(n,k).
Numbers k such that k and 2*k are anagrams.
Triangle read by rows: a(m,m) = 1, for all m. For n < m, a(m,n) = a(m-1,n) + (sum of all terms in rows 1 through m-1).
G.f. A(x) satisfies: Sum_{n>=0} log( A(2^n*x) )^n / n! = 1 + Sum_{n>=0} 2^(2^n-n) * x^(2^n).
G.f. A(x) satisfies: Sum_{n>=0} log(A(3^n*x))^n/n! = 1 + Sum_{n>=0} 3^(3^n-n)*x^(3^n).
Record gaps between nonprime prime powers.
Number triangle T(n,k)=C(n,k)C(2,n-k).
Orderly numbers: a number n is orderly if there exists some number k > tau(n) such that the set of the divisors of n is congruent to the set {1,2,...,tau(n)} mod k.
Riordan array (1-4x+4x^2, x(1-2x)).
a(1) = 2; thereafter a(n) = a(n-1) + gcd(n, a(n-1)) if n is odd, and a(n) = a(n-1) + gcd(n-2, a(n-1)) if n is even.
Number of partitions of n into odd squares.
Number of partitions of n into distinct odd squares.
The single or isolated numbers. The union of single (or isolated or non-twin) primes and single (or isolated or average of twin prime pairs) nonprimes.
Numbers whose base-2 expansion has no run of digits with length < 2.
A positive integer n is included if there is no run of 0's in the binary representation of n that is only one digit long.
A positive integer n is included if every 1 in binary n is next to at least one other 1.
1, followed by list of numbers n such that the number of strong primes and the number of weak primes are equal at the n-th prime.
Primes of the form m^2 + 3m + 9, where m can be positive or negative.
A positive integer n is included if the run-lengths (of runs both of 0's and of 1's) of the binary representation of n form an arithmetic progression (when written in order).
Array F(k, n) read by descending antidiagonals: k-generalized Fibonacci numbers in row k >= 1, starting (0, 1, 1, ...), for column n >= 0.
Number of integer pairs (x,y) satisfying |x|^3 + |y|^3 = n, -n <= x,y <= n.
Number of integer triples (x,y,z) satisfying |x|^3 + |y|^3 + |z|^3 = n, -n <= x,y,z <= n.
Number of integer pairs (x,y) satisfying x^4 + y^4 = n.
Number of integer triples (x,y,z) satisfying x^4+y^4+z^4=n, -n <= x,y,z <= n.
Number of solutions to a^2 + b^2 + 5*c^2 = n.
Those positive integers n such that n = (2^m +1)*k, each for some positive integer m, and k < 2^m.
Primes p such that p-2 is not a prime.
a(n) = sopf(n) + sopf(n+1).
Numbers n with property that sigma(n) < min(sigma(n-2),sigma(n-1),sigma(n+1),sigma(n+2)).
Sum of all parts of the last section of the set of partitions of n.
Triangle, read by rows of n*(n+1)/2 + 1 terms, that starts with a '1' in row 0 with row n consisting of n '1's followed by the partial sums of the prior row.
Second of two complementary trees generated by the Wythoff sequences.
First of two complementary trees generated by the Wythoff sequences.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x-2 and 4x-2 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x-2 and 4x+2 are in a.
a(n) = floor(2*n*Pi) - 2*floor(n*Pi).
a(n) = [6*n*Pi] - 2*[3*n*Pi], where [ ]=floor.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x-1 and 4x-2 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x-1 and 4x-1 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x-1 and 4x are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x-1 and 4x+1 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x-1 and 4x+2 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x-1 and 4x+3 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x and 4x-2 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x and 4x-1 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x and 4x+1 are in a.

Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+1 and 4x-2 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+1 and 4x-1 are in a.
a(n) = floor(8*n*Pi) - 2*floor(4*n*Pi).
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+1 and 4x+1 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+1 and 4x+2 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+1 and 4x+3 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+2 and 4x-2 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+2 and 4x-1 are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+2 and 4x are in a.
Increasing sequence generated by these rules:  a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 3x+2 and 4x+2 are in a.
a(n) = [4*n*Pi] - 2*[2*n*Pi], where [ ]=floor.
Number of Ramanujan primes R_k between triangular numbers T(n-1) < R_k <= T(n).
[4n*e]-2[2n*e], where [ ]=floor.
Fixed point of the morphism 0->01, 1->02, 2->03, 3->001.
Fixed point of the morphism 0 -> 001, 1 -> 02, 2 -> 01.
Numbers k such that k and k^3 are both palindromes.
Riordan matrix (1/(1-3*x^2),x/(1-x)).
Numbers of the form p*q, p and q prime with q=2*p-1.
A problem of Zarankiewicz: maximal number of 1's in an n X n matrix of 0's and 1's with 0's on the main diagonal and no 'rectangle' with 1's at the four corners.
a(n) is smallest number which is uniquely of the form a(j) + a(k) with 1 <= j < k < n and a(1) = 1, a(2) = 4.
a(1)=2, a(2)=3; for n >= 3, a(n) is smallest number that is uniquely of the form a(j) + a(k) with 1 <= j < k < n.
Polya-Vinogradov numbers: a(n) is the maximum over all k > 0 of |#(quadratic residues modulo p up to k) - #(quadratic nonresidues modulo p up to k)| where p is the n-th prime and n > 1.
Allowed values of degrees of minimal polynomials of 2*cos(Pi/N).
Related to Fibonacci numbers, see the Formula section.
Numbers of the form p^2 + q^2, with p and q prime, in exactly one way.
Least number k for which primepi(prime(k+1)/2) - primepi(prime(k)/2) = n.
Least m such that the continued fraction for sqrt(m) has period n.
Least number m such that n is the denominator of sigma_{-1}(m), or zero if no such exists.
Number of partitions of n^2 into three distinct primes.
Compressed nim-multiplication table read by antidiagonals.
Array T(m,n) = nim-product(2^m,2^n) (m>=0, n>=0) read by antidiagonals.
Number of triangles after n-th stage in a cellular automaton based in isosceles triangles of two sizes (see Comments lines for precise definition).
a(n) = f(1)^n + ... + f(n)^n (mod n) where f(i)=i if gcd(i,n)=1 and f(i)=0 otherwise.
The digits of a(n) and a(n+1) together can be reordered to form a square; lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers with this property.
The digits of a(n) and a(n+1) together can be reordered to form a square; lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers with this property.
Jordan function J_6(n).
Number of monosubstituted alkanes C(n-1)H(2n-1)-X with n-1 carbon atoms that are stereoisomers.
