Triangular array: the fission of (p(n,x)) by (q(n,x)), where p(n,x)=x*p(n-1,x)+n+1 with p(0,x)=1, and q(n,x)=x*p(n-1,x)+1 with p(0,x)=1.
Triangular array:  the self-fission of (p(n,x)), where p(n,x)=x*p(n-1,x)+n+1, where p(0,x)=1.
Triangular array:  the fission of (p(n,x)) by (q(n,x)), where p(n,x)=x*p(n-1,x)+n+1 with p(0,x)=1, and q(n,x)=sum{(k+1)*x^k ; 0<=k<=n}.
Triangular array:  the self-fission of (p(n,x)), where p(n,x)=x*p(n-1,x)+n, with p(0,x)=1.
Triangle T of all positive differences of distinct Fibonacci numbers; also, triangle of all sums of consecutive distinct Fibonacci numbers.
Expansion of psi(q^2) / f(-q)^2 in powers of q where psi(), f() are Ramanujan theta functions.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = (n#)/(k#), 1 <= k <= n.
Smallest number a(n) formed from consecutive sequences of digits of Pi and satisfying a(n) > a(n-1); first 3 is omitted.
Values y for infinite sequence x^3-y^2 = d with decreasing coefficient r=sqrt(x)/d which tend to 1/(1350*sqrt(5))or infinity family of solutions Mordell curve with extension sqrt(5).
Values x for infinite sequence x^3-y^2 = d with decreasing coefficient r=sqrt(x)/d which tend to 1/(1350*sqrt(5))or infinity family of solutions Mordell curve with extension sqrt(5).
Coordinates x of Mordell elliptic curves x^3-y^2 for primary extremal points with quadratic extensions over rationals.
a(n) is the least prime p such that p-1 is divisible by 2^n and not by 2^(n+1).
Number of walks of length n on one 60-degree wedge of the equilateral triangular lattice. The walk can go along the walls of the wedge, but cannot cross the walls.
Bit-interleaved number addition table; like binary addition but carries shift 2 instead of 1; addition base sqrt(2).
Let p = n-th prime; a(n) = number of pairs (i,j) with 0 < i < p, 0 < j < p such that i*j == 1 mod p and i and j have opposite parity.
Number of labeled forests of n nodes each component of which is a path.
Second elementary symmetric function of divisors of n.
Smallest pentagonal number with n prime factors (counted with multiplicity).
Primes p which are greater than p reversed.

a(n) is the total size of all the image sets of all functions from [n] to [n]. I.e., a(n) is the sum of the cardinalities of every image set of every function whose domain and co-domain is {1,2,...,n}.
Numbers n such that the next larger number with mutual Hamming distance 1 is prime.
Triangle T(n,k), 0<=k<=n, read by rows defined by: T(n,k) = T(n-1,k-1) + 2*T(n-1,k) + T(n-2,k-2) - T(n-2,k), T(0,0) = 1, T(n,k) = 0 if k < 0 or if n < k.
Triangle defined by g.f. A(x,y) = exp( Sum_{n>=1} x^n/n * Sum_{k=0..n} binomial(n^2, n*k) * y^k ), as read by rows.
Colors of the 88 keys of the standard piano: white keys = 0, black keys = 1, start with A0 = the 0th key.
a(1) = 1 and, for n >= 2, a(n) is the least integer such that both p(n) and q(n) are squarefree where p(n)/q(n) is the n-th convergent of the continued fraction [a(1),a(2),...,a(n)].
Number of practical numbers p<n with n-p and n+p both prime or both practical.
Product of positive odd integers smaller than n and relatively prime to n.
Triangle read by rows, generated from (..., 5, 3, 1).
Pascal's triangle, with the first two columns removed.
Rewrite the binary expansion of n from the most significant end, 1 -> 1, 0+1 (one or more zeros followed by one) -> 0, drop the trailing zeros of the original n.
Square array read by antidiagonals: T(n,p) is the number of linearly independent, homogeneous harmonic polynomials of degree n in p variables (n,p>=1).
The inverse of the constant 1 function under the exponential convolution (also called the exponential Möbius function).
Product of the arithmetic derivatives from 2 to n.
Number of 2 X 2 matrices having all elements in {0,1,...,n} and determinant 2.
Number of 2 X 2 integer matrices with elements from {1,...,n} whose determinant is 1.
Number of 2 X 2 integer matrices with elements from {1,...,n} whose determinant is 2.
Number of 2 X 2 matrices having all elements in {-n,...,n} and determinant 1.
Number of 2 X 2 matrices having all elements in {-n,...n} and determinant 2.
Number of 2 X 2 matrices having all elements in {-n,...n} and determinant 3.
Number of 2 X 2 matrices having all elements in {-n,...n} and determinant 4.
Number of 2 X 2 matrices having all elements in {-n,...n} and determinant 5.
Indices of squares (of primes) in the semiprimes.
a(n) = 1 if 2*n + 1 is prime, otherwise a(n) = 0.
Products of 4 consecutive integers: a(n) = n*(n-1)*(n-2)*(n-3).
Number of series-parallel networks with n labeled edges. Also called yoke-chains by Cayley and MacMahon.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of n^k contains three consecutive identical digits.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of n^k contains four consecutive identical digits.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of n^k contains five consecutive identical digits.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of n^k contains six consecutive identical digits.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of n^k contains seven consecutive identical digits.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of n^k contains eight or more consecutive identical digits.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of n^k contains nine consecutive identical digits.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of Fibonacci(k) contains n consecutive identical digits.
a(n) is the least value of k such that the decimal expansion of Lucas(k) contains n consecutive identical digits.
Triangle read by rows, arising in enumeration of permutations by cyclic valleys, cycles and fixed points.
Triangle read by rows, arising in enumeration of permutations by cyclic peaks.
Triangle read by rows, arising in enumeration of permutations by cyclic peaks, cycles and fixed points.
a(n) = (conjectured) length of longest tail that can be generated by a starting string of 2's and 3's of length n before a 1 is reached, using the rule described in the Comments lines.
Number of tree-rooted bridgeless planar maps with two vertices and n faces.
Sophie Germain triangular numbers tr: 2*tr+1 is also a triangular number.
Smallest number having a power that in decimal has exactly n copies of all ten digits.
Monic integer version of Chebyshev T-polynomials (increasing powers).
Number of assembly trees for the complete tripartite graph K_{n,n,n}.
Numbers k such that the sum of the squares of the first k primes is divisible by k.
After the 51-digit 2^168, a(n) is the number setting a record for non-pandigital right segment length of 2^a(n).
Emirpimes: numbers n such that n and its reversal are distinct semiprimes.
a(n) is the least multiple of n, greater than n, such that all digits of a(n) are even (resp. odd) if n is even (resp. odd).
Primes p such that the octal expansion of 1/p has a unique period length.
Number of primes between prime(n)/2 and prime(n+1)/2.
a(n) produces only composites by concatenating numbers decremented in sequence in all bases from 2 up to a record.
a(1)=2, a(2)=3, a(3)=4; for n>=4, a(n) is the largest number <= prime(n) such that no terms of the sequence are between a(n-1)/2 and a(n)/2.
Numbers with three prime factors, not necessarily distinct, except cubes of primes.

Write n in binary. Consider the 0's and 1 as a list. (*) If the new list consists entirely of 1's, then a(n) = the number of 1's, and end. Otherwise, construct a new list made up of the lengths, written in order, of the runs of similarly-valued terms from the previous list. Go to *.
Triangle read by rows, T(n,k) = T(n-1,k-1) + k*T(n-1,k) + (k+1)*T(n-1,k+1), T(0,0) = 1, n >= 0, k >= 0.
a(n) = total number of binary sequences S of length n and curling number k (so S = XY^k) in which Y can be taken to have length 1.
'Dropping time' in 3x+1 problem starting at n (number of steps to reach a lower number than starting value); a(1) = 0 by convention. Also called glide(n).
Sum of the nonprime proper divisors (or nonprime aliquot parts) of n.
a(1)=2, a(2)=3, for n>=3, a(n) is the n-th number which is obtained by application Eratosthenes-like sieve to sequence: odd part of digit sum of 5^m, m>=1.
Odd part of digit sum of 5^n divided by maximal possible power of 5.
Discriminants D < 0 such that h(D) > h(D') for D < D' < 0, negated.
The odd part of the digit sum of 7^n.
Number of ways n can be represented as a sum of two distinct nontrivial prime powers (numbers of the form p^k where p is a prime number and k >= 2).
Triangular array T read by rows: T(n,k) = k^2 mod n, for 1 <= k <= n, n >= 1.
Integer nearest to (4*((S(n))^(n-1))), where S(n) = Sum_{i=0..2} (C(i)*(log(log(A*(B+n^(8/3)))))^(2i)) (see coefficients A, B, C(i) in comments).
Number of primes p between powers of 2, 2^n < p <= 2^(n+1).
Decimal expansion of the positive root of x^x^x^x = 2.
T(n,k)=Number of distinct values of the sum of n products of a 0..k-1 and a 0..k integer.
T(n,k) = number of distinct values of the sum of n products of two 0..k integers.
T(n,k)=Number of distinct values of the sum of n products of three 0..k integers.
T(n,k)=Number of distinct values of the sum of a*b+a*c+b*c over n sets of three a,b,c 0..k integers.
T(n,k)=Number of distinct values of the sum of i^2 over n realizations of i in 0..k.
T(n,k) = Number of distinct values of the sum of i*(i-1) over n realizations of i in 0..k.
Palindromes in base 3 (written in base 3).
Numbers n such that there is an integer k with the property that k^tau(n) = sigma(n).
Number of nontrivial triangular numbers dividing triangular(n).
Triangle read by rows: Delannoy numbers minus binomial coefficients.
Indices x such that (1/2)(prime(x+1) - prime(x)) is prime.
Strong primes: prime(k) > (prime(k-1) + prime(k+1))/2.
Weak primes: prime(n) < (prime(n-1) + prime(n+1))/2.
Largest number whose factorial is less than (n!)^2.
a(n) is the smallest m for which there appears for the first time a prime p which equals odd part of sum of digits of m^2.
Expansion of 1/(1 - x^3 - x^4 - x^5 + x^8).

Number T(n,k,u) of distinct tilings of an n X k rectangle using integer-sided square tiles containing u nodes that are unconnected to any of their neighbors; irregular triangle T(n,k,u), 1 <= k <= n, u >= 0, read by rows.

Number T(n,k,u) of partitions of an n X k rectangle into integer-sided square parts containing u nodes that are unconnected to any of their neighbors, considering only the number of parts; irregular triangle T(n,k,u), 1 <= k <= n, u >= 0, read by rows.
Largest number m such that 1, 2, ..., m can be represented as the sum of distinct divisors of n.
a(n) = (number of 1's in binary expansion of n)th positive number not among the previous terms.
Triangle generated by Pascal's rule, except begin and end the n-th row with n!.
a(2n+1) = a(2n) + a(2n-1), a(2n)=least number not yet in the sequence, a(1)=1.
Primes p such that p^2 + 1 is squarefree.
Primes p such that p^2 + 1 is not squarefree.
Number of perfect matchings in n-cube.
X-coordinate of the bottom left corner of the n X 1 brick in the greedy tiling of the first quadrant with bricks of height 1 and width 1, 2, 3... (See Comments for precise definition).
Number of cyclic permutations of [n] with no i -> i+1 (mod n).
Numbers n such that all numbers of the form Fib(n)/d + d are prime (or nonexistent), where Fib(n) is the n-th Fibonacci number and d is a nontrivial divisor of Fib(n).
Tree read by levels generated by these rules: 1 is at the top, and the node x has child nodes x+1, 2*x, and 3*x, where duplicates are deleted as they occur.
Denominator of (n+1)*Bernoulli(n).
Concatenation of the first n numbers in binary (converted to base 10).
Canonical parts power representation of n: n = concatenation((1)^k_1,(10)^k_2,...).
T(n, k) = Sum_{j=0..n-k} (-1)^j*binomial(n - k + 1, j)*(n - k + 1 - j)^n. Triangle read by rows, T(n, k) for 1 <= k <= n.
Number of toothpicks and D-toothpicks after n-th stage in the D-toothpick 'wide' triangle of the third kind, second version.
Number of toothpicks and D-toothpicks after n-th stage in the D-toothpick 'narrow' triangle of the third kind, second version.
Number of toothpicks and D-toothpicks after n-th stage in a D-toothpick 'wide' triangle (see Comments lines for definition).
a(n+1) is the sum of digits of (a(n) + a(n-1)).

Number of grid points that are covered on the semi-infinite hexagonal grid after n-th stage in a cellular automaton in which the toothpicks are connected by their endpoints but the toothpicks placed in northwest or northeast direction are prohibited, starting with a(0) = 1.
Exponent of 2 in the prime factorization of prime(n)^2 - 1.
Anti-phi(n).
a(1)=1; for n>1, a(n) = smallest positive integer not among the earlier terms of the sequence that is divisible by a different number of distinct primes than a(n-1).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of k-matchings in the n-sunlet graph (0 <= k <= n).
Numbers k such that, for all m < k, d_i(k) <= d_i(m) for i=1 to Min(d(k),d(m)), where d_i(k) denotes the i-th smallest divisor of k.
a(1)=11. For n>1, a(n) is LCM of a(n-1) and largest integer <= sqrt(a(n-1)).
Start with n; add to it any of its digits; repeat; a(n) = minimal number of steps needed to reach a palindrome.
Start with n; add to it any of its digits; repeat; a(n) = minimal number of steps needed to reach a prime greater than n.
Numbers n such that 4 consecutive terms of binomial(n,k) satisfy a quadratic relation for 0 <= k <= n/2.
a(n) is the least r such that there are n+2 consecutive increasing terms in the r-th row of Pascal's triangle (binomial(r,*)) which satisfy a polynomial of degree n.
Number of partitions p of n such that round(mean(p)) is not a part of p; here, round(x) means floor(x + 1/2).
Arshon's sequence: start from 1 and replace the letters in odd positions using 1 -> 123, 2 -> 231, 3 -> 312 and the letters in even positions using 1 -> 321, 2-> 132, 3 -> 213.
Primes prime(n) such that (prime(n+1)/prime(n))^n > n.
Triangle read by rows, number of orbitals classified with respect to the first zero crossing, n>=1, 1<=k<=n.
a(1) = 1; thereafter a(n+1) = floor(sqrt(2*a(n)*(a(n)+1))).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) (1 <= k <= n) defined by T(n,n) = (n-1)^(n-1), T(n,k) = T(n,k+1) - (n-1)*T(n-1,k) for k = n-1 .. 1.
Partitions listed by alternately incrementing each part and appending a 1.
Number of spanning trees in P_5 x P_n.
Smaller of pair of successive n-digit primes with maximal difference.
Numbers n such that 2n is a sum of two primes, the adding of which requires only one carry in binary.
a(1) = 1, a(n+1) is the sum of a(n) and floor( arithmetic mean of a(1) ... a(n) ).
Denominator of c(n) = (n^2+n+2)/((n+1)*(n+2)*(n+3)).
LCM of n and largest integer <= sqrt(n).
Squarefree integers m such that the fundamental unit of Q(sqrt(m)) has norm -1. Also, squarefree integers m such that the Pell equation x^2 - m*y^2 = -1 is soluble.
P-positions for game of UpMark.
Triangular array read by rows: row n gives the coefficients of the polynomial p(n,x) defined in Comments.
Triangular array read by rows: row n gives the coefficients of the polynomial p(n,x) defined in Comments.
Triangular array: row n gives the coefficients of the polynomial p(n,x) defined in Comments.
Decimal expansion of the largest constant 'beta' for which there exists a solution to the differential equation y''(x)+exp(y(x))=0, with y(0)=y(beta)=0.
Numbers n equal to the sum of all the four-digit numbers formed without repetition from the digits of n.
Least positive integer k for which the Jacobi symbol (k|2*n-1) is less than 1, where 2*n-1 is a nonsquare; a(n)=0 if 2*n-1 is a square.
Lexicographically earliest permutation of the nonnegative integers such that the parity of the first digit of a(n+1) equals that of a(n)'s last digit.
Numbers j such that the sum of the first j terms, Sum_{k=1..j} a(k), is not in this list.
Numbers on the diagonals in Ulam's spiral.
A(n,k) = exponent of the largest power of n-th prime which divides the product of the elements on row (k-1) of Pascal's triangle; a square array read by antidiagonals.
Lexicographically earliest permutation of the positive integers such that the parity of the first digit of a(n+1) equals that of a(n)'s last digit.
Lexically first sequence of distinct positive integers such that a(n) is coprime to the next a(n) elements.
a(1)=1; thereafter a(n) = smallest square m^2 such that m^2 minus (sum of all previous terms) is prime.
Prime numbers that are expressible as the sum of two positive triangular numbers.
Sum of composite numbers between successive primes.
a(0) = 0, a(n+1) = smallest number, not occurring earlier, containing the smallest of the least frequently occurring digits in all preceding terms.
Product_{k=1..n} prime(k)!.
Numbers n such that the sum of n and the largest prime<n is prime, and the sum of n and the least prime>n is also prime.
a(1)=1. a(n) = the smallest positive integer not occurring earlier in the sequence such that the n-th prime is congruent to a(n) (mod n).
Distribute the natural numbers in columns based on the occurrence of '2' in each prime factorization; square array A(row,col) = 2^(row-1) * ((2*col)-1), read by descending antidiagonals.
Number of (not necessarily distinct) multiples of 4 on row n of Pascal's triangle.
Number of (not necessarily distinct) multiples of 9 on row n of Pascal's triangle.
E.g.f.: Sum_{n>=0} Product_{k=1..n} sinh(k*x).
a(n) is the smallest prime q such that n(q+1)+1 is prime, that is, the smallest prime q such that n = (p-1)/(q+1) with p prime; or a(n) = -1 if no such q exists.
a(n) is the smallest prime q such that n(q-1)-1 is prime, that is, the smallest prime q so that n = (p+1)/(q-1) with p prime; or a(n) = -1 if no such q exists.
Smallest number of vertices supporting a graph with exactly n Hamiltonian cycles up to direction.
Integers k such that each of k, k+1, k+2, k+4, k+5, k+6 is the product of two distinct primes.
a(n) = smallest k such that a(n-k) and n have the same number of 1's in their binary expansions, or a(n) = n if no such k exists.
From third root of Riemann zeta function: form Dirichlet series Sum b(n)/n^x whose cube is zeta function; sequence gives denominator of b(n).
From fourth root of Riemann zeta function: form Dirichlet series Sum b(n)/n^x whose fourth power is zeta function; sequence gives denominator of b(n).
From fifth root of Riemann zeta function: form Dirichlet series Sum b(n)/n^x whose fifth power is zeta function; sequence gives denominator of b(n).
Distinct digits of n arranged in decreasing order.
a(0) = 0; a(n) = smallest k such that gcd(a(n-k), n) is not 1.
Least d>0 such that floor(n/d) = floor(n/(d+1)).
Triangle T(n, k) with the natural numbers in columns with nonprime k and the nonnegative numbers in columns with prime k, for 1 <= k <= n.
Random Fibonacci tree defined with the pair(1,1).
a(n+1) = least number not occurring earlier such that max{a(n), a(n+1)} >= 2 min{a(n), a(n+1)}; a(0) = 0.
a(n+1) has a digit that divides a(n) and is the least positive integer not appearing earlier with this property.
a(n) = the smallest positive integer not occurring earlier in the sequence such that floor(max(a(n),a(n-1))/min(a(n),a(n-1))) = 2; a(1) = 1.
Construct spiral of numbers on square grid as in Comments; sequence gives terms along the '3' arm.
Construct spiral of numbers on square grid as in Comments; sequence gives terms along the '7' arm.
Construct spiral of numbers on square grid as in Comments; sequence gives terms along the '2' arm.
Construct spiral of numbers on square grid as in Comments; sequence gives terms along the '5' arm.
Arrange numbers in a single clockwise spiral so that each number is relatively prime to its four (N,S,E,W) neighbors.
a(1)=p_1, a(2)=p_1 + p_1*p_2, a(3)=p_1 + p_1*p_2 + p_1*p_2*p_3, ... where p_i is the i-th prime.
Numbers m with 9*m + 3*r - 1 and 9*m + 3*r + 1 twin prime for some r = 0,1,2.
The slowest increasing sequence of semiprimes with strictly increasing  difference of successive terms.
Numbers n such that genus of group Gamma_0(n) is zero.
Stirling's formula: denominators of asymptotic series for Gamma function.
Sum of the lengths of the arithmetic progressions in {1,2,3,...,n}, including trivial arithmetic progressions of lengths 1 and 2.

Start with 1. For each term m, the next term is the smallest positive integer k such that k - (sum of base 2 digits of k) = m. If no such k exists, use the smallest natural number not already in the sequence.
Let n'= odd part of n. If n' is 1 or prime, then a(n)=1; otherwise a(n) is 1+ the number of times the map x -> (3*x+1)' must be applied to n' in order to reach 1 or a prime.
Decimal expansion of the unique real number a>0 such that the real part of li(-a) is zero.
Decimal expansion of the sixth (of 10) decimal selvage number; the n-th digit of a decimal selvage number, x, is equal to the tenths digit of n*x.
Bihappy numbers: numbers that reach 1 under iteration of the sum-of-squares-of-two-digits map s_2.
Working in binary, write n followed by 0 then n-reversed (including leading zeros); show result in base 10.
a(0) = 1; for n>0, working in binary, write n followed by 1 then n-reversed (including leading zeros); show result in base 10.
Champernowne primes.
Pluritriangular numbers: a(0) = 0; a(n+1) = a(n) + the number of digits in terms a(0)..a(n).
Number of compositions of n into prime parts.
Number of basic semimagic squares of order n that can be formed from the numbers 1, ..., n^2.
Terms satisfy: a(2*n) = a(n)*b(n) and a(2*n+1) = a(n)*b(n+1) for n>=0 with a(0)=1, where A(x)^2 = Sum_{n>=0} b(n)*x^n and g.f. A(x) = Sum_{n>=0} a(n)*x^n.
Terms satisfy: a(2*n) = a(n)*b(n) and a(2*n+1) = a(n+1)*b(n) for n>=0 with a(0)=1, where A(x)^2 = Sum_{n>=0} b(n)*x^n and g.f. A(x) = Sum_{n>=0} a(n)*x^n.
a(1) = 1 and a(n+1) = if a(n) > 2*n+1 then a(n)-2*n-1 else a(n)+2*n+1.
Binary Keith numbers.
Shifts left when INVERT transform applied thrice.
Number of primes with digit sum n whose digit product is maximal among all numbers with digit sum n.
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = k IMPL n, 0 <= k <= n, bitwise logical IMPL.
Define a pair of sequences c_n, d_n by c_0=0, d_0=1 and thereafter c_n = c_{n-1}+d_{n-1}, d_n = c_{n-1}+4*n+2; sequence here is d_n.
Describe the previous term! (method A - initial term is 2).
a(n) = n XOR n^3.
Expansion of Product_{k>=1} (1 + k!*x^k).
Numbers which have only positive entries in the difference table of their divisors.

Triangle entry T(n, m) gives the m-th contribution T(n, m)*sin((2*m+1)*v) to the coefficient of q^n in the Fourier expansion of Jacobi's elliptic sn(u|k) function when expressed in the variables v = u/(2*K(k)/Pi) and q, the Jacobi nome, written as series in (k/4)^2. K is the real quarter period of elliptic functions.
a(n) is the number of nonnegative m < n for which m + n is a perfect square.
Odd numbers n such that n is not coprime to the multiplicative order of 2 mod n.
Largest prime not exceeding the geometric mean of all prime divisors of n counted with multiplicity.
Least prime not less than the geometric mean of all prime divisors of n counted with multiplicity.
Largest prime not exceeding the median of all prime divisors of n counted with multiplicity.
Least prime not less than the median of all prime divisors of n counted with multiplicity.
Smallest composite c such that n^(c-1) != 1 (mod c^2), i.e., smallest composite c that is not a 'Wieferich pseudoprime' to base n.
Number of collections of nonempty multisets with a total of n objects having color set {1,...,k} for some k<=n.
Genus of modular group Gamma_0(n). Or, genus of modular curve X_0(n).
Denominators of an enumeration system of the reduced nonnegative rational numbers.
Numerators of an enumeration system of the reduced nonnegative rational numbers.
Numbers that are the sum of a positive square and a positive cube.
Square array read by antidiagonals: T(n,m) (n>=1, m>=0) is the number of partitions of mn that are the sum of m not necessarily distinct partitions of n.
a(n) = 1 if n is a cube, else 0.
Decimal expansion of arccos(sqrt(1/3)) and of arcsin(sqrt(2/3)) and arctan(sqrt(2)).
a(n) = floor(sqrt(n!)).
Convolutory inverse of signed lower Wythoff sequence.
For n odd, a(n) is the least positive integer not already used. For n even, a(n) is the least positive integer not already used that is not coprime to a(n/2).
Elias's omega code for n.
Elias delta code for n.
Numbers surviving a decaying sieve.
Write 0, 1, ..., n in binary and add as if they were decimal numbers.
Square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals, where column k is the expansion of Product_{j>=1} 1/(1+x^j)^(j*k) in powers of x.
Square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals, where column k is the expansion of Product_{j>=1} (1-x^j)^(j*k) in powers of x.
Square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals, where column k is the expansion of Product_{j>=1} 1/(1+x^j)^(j^k) in powers of x.
Triangle read by rows: number of topologies of n nested circles intersecting at most as binaries, according to number of factors.
Triangle read by rows: number of topologies of n nested circles intersecting at most as triples, according to number of factors.
a(n) = smallest m such that value of odd harmonic series Sum_{j=0..m} 1/(2j+1) is >= n.
'Nachos' sequence based on triangular numbers.
E.g.f. S(x) satisfies: S(x) = Integral (1 + S(x)^2)^(5/2) dx.
Triangle read by rows, coefficients of the polynomials P(m, n) = Sum_{k=1..n} binomial(m*n, m*k)* P(m, n-k)*z with P(m, 0) = 1 and m = 3.
Triangle read by rows, coefficients of the polynomials P(m, n) = Sum_{k=1..n} binomial(m*n, m*k)* P(m, n-k)*z with P(m, 0) = 1 and m = 4.
a(n) = least denominator Y of any proper fraction X/Y which needs n or more terms to be written as a signed sum of distinct unit fractions.

Square array read by antidiagonals upwards in which each term is the sum of prior elements in the same row, column, diagonal, or antidiagonal that divide n; the array is seeded with an initial value a(1)=1.
Composite Fermat numbers.
a(n) = binomial(6*n, 3*n)*binomial(3*n, n)/(2*(2*n+1)*binomial(2*n, n)).
Coefficients of unique normalized cusp form Delta_20 of weight 20 for full modular group.
a(n) = sigma_19(n), the sum of the 19th powers of the divisors of n.
Coefficients of unique normalized cusp form Delta_16 of weight 16 for full modular group.
a(n) = sigma_15(n), the sum of the 15th powers of the divisors of n.
Coefficients of unique normalized cusp form Delta_18 of weight 18 for full modular group.
a(n) = sigma_17(n), the sum of the 17th powers of the divisors of n.
a(n) = sigma_21(n), the sum of the 21st powers of the divisors of n.
Coefficients of unique normalized cusp form Delta_22 of weight 22 for full modular group.
a(n) = sigma_25(n), the sum of the 25th powers of the divisors of n.
Coefficients of unique normalized cusp form Delta_26 of weight 26 for full modular group.
Coefficients in the expansion of 1/([r]-[2*r]*x+[3*r]*x^2-...); [ ]=floor, r=-1+sqrt(7).
Coefficients in the expansion of 1/([r]-[2*r]*x+[3*r]*x^2-...); [ ]=floor, r=sqrt(e).
Number of integers containing n in their base-10 home prime trajectory.
Coefficients in the expansion of 1/([r]-[2*r]*x+[3*r]*x^2-...); [ ]=floor, r=-4/5+sqrt(6).
Coefficients in the expansion of 1/([r]-[2*r]*x+[3*r]*x^2-...); [ ]=floor, r=sqrt(11/4).
Greatest k such that k-th prime < twice n-th prime.
Maximal value of prime divisors of numbers in reduced residue system for n.
Coefficients in the expansion of 1/([r]-[2r]x+[3r]x^2-...); [ ]=floor, r=13/8.
Coefficients in the expansion of 1/([r]-[2r]x+[3r]x^2-...); [ ]=floor, r=11/7.
a(1)=1 and for n>1, a(n) is the smallest number greater than a(n-1) such that a(n) is not divisible by a(d) for any divisor d of n (except 1 and n).
Let f be the multiplicative function satisfying f(p^k) = (1 + p*I)^k for any prime p and k > 0 (where I^2 = -1); a(n) = the imaginary part of f(n).
Let f be the multiplicative function satisfying f(p^k) = (1 + p*I)^k for any prime p and k > 0 (where I^2 = -1); a(n) = the real part of f(n).
Number of polygonal tiles with n sides with two exits per side and n edges connecting pairs of exits, with no edges between exits on the same side and non-isomorphic under rotational symmetry.
Primes p of the form p = 2^k * m + 1, where (i) m is squarefree and odd, (ii) all primes that divide m are in the sequence, and (iii) k is 0, 1, or 2.
Number of immersions of an unoriented circle into the unoriented sphere with n double points.
p-INVERT of (3n), where p(S) = 1 - S - S^2.
a(n) = round(n/2) + 1 = ceiling(n/2) + 1 = floor((n+1)/2) + 1.
Complex cross sequence (see Comments lines for definition).
Fibonacci numbers interspersed with zeros.
Coefficients of 1/(Sum_{k>=0} [-1 + (k+1)*r](-x)^k), where r = (3 + sqrt(5))/2 = 1 + golden ratio and [ ] = floor.
Coefficients of 1/(Sum_{k>=0} round((k+1)*r)(-x)^k), where r = sqrt(2).
Coefficients of 1/(Sum_{k>=0} round((k+1)*r)(-x)^k), where r = 7/5.
Coefficients of 1/(Sum_{k>=0} round((k+1)*r)(-x)^k), where r = 9/7.
Largest convex area that can be tiled with n equilateral triangles whose sides s_k are relatively prime, i.e., gcd(s_1,...,s_n) = 1.
Number of binary Lyndon words containing n letters of each type; periodic binary sequences of period 2n with n zeros and n ones in each period.
Largest m such that we can partition the set {1,2,...,m} into n subsets with the property that we never have a+b=c for any distinct elements a, b, c in one subset.
Unique sequence satisfying SumXOR_{d divides n} a(d) = n for any n>0, where SumXOR is the analog of summation under the binary XOR operation.
a(n) = n^5*H(n) where H() is the Hurwitz class number.
Number of ways to write n as sum of at least 2 consecutive odd positive integers.
Array read by antidiagonals: Pascal-like recursion and self-referential boundaries.
First term = 1 and, for each n > 1, n*a(n) does not appear.
a(n) = min{denominator(r) with r in R} and R = {0 <= r rational <= 1 and [r*k] = n}. Here k = 10^(floor(log_10(n))+1) and [x] = floor(x+1/2) + ceiling((2*x-1)/4) - floor((2*x-1)/4) - 1.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive numbers such that the prime factorizations of two consecutive terms never share a prime exponent >= 1.
Composite values of n such that 2^n == 2 (mod n*(n-1)).
Composite integers k such that 2^k == 2 (mod k*(k+1)).

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that, for any n > 1 with binary expansion (b_1, b_2, ..., b_k) (where b_1 = 1 is the most significant bit of n), a(n) is a multiple of a(i) for each i such that b_i = 1.

Solution (b(n)) of the near-complementary equation a(n) = a(1)*b(n-1) - a(0)*b(n-2) + n, where a(0) = 1, a(1) = 2, b(0) = 3, b(1) = 4, and (b(n)) is the increasing sequence of positive integers not in (a(n)).  See Comments.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that for any n > 0, a(n) XOR a(n+1) XOR a(n+2) is prime (where XOR denotes the bitwise XOR operator).
Solution of the complementary equation a(n) = a(0)*b(n-1) + a(1)*b(n-2), where a(0) = 1, a(1) = 2, b(0) = 3, and (a(n)) and (b(n)) are increasing complementary sequences.
Number of coprime pairs (x,y) with x^2 + y^2 <= n.
Order of the 'inside-out' permutation on 2n+1 letters.
a(1)=1; for n > 1, a(n) = number of earlier terms a(k), 1 <= k <= n-1, such that (a(k)+n) is divisible by k.
One even followed by three odd.
Expansion of 1/(2 - Sum_{k>=0} k!*x^k/(1 + x)^(k+1)).
Smallest k > n whose binary expansion encodes an irreducible (0,1)-polynomial over Q.
a(n) = Fibonacci(6*n+1).
a(n) = Fibonacci(6n+5).
Expansion of Product_{k>=1} (1 - x^(k*(k+1)/2)).
Expansion of Product_{k>=1} (1 - x^(k*(3*k-1)/2)).
Number of finite sets of relatively prime positive integers > 1 with least common multiple n.
a(n) = smallest m such that the sum of digits of n^m is greater than n, or 0 if no such m exists.

Filter sequence: Restricted growth sequence transform of function that gives the least natural number with the same prime signature that (0,1)-polynomial encoded in the binary expansion of n has when it is factored over Q.
a(n) = 1 if n is a prime whose binary expansion encodes a (0,1)-polynomial which is irreducible when factored over GF(2), 0 otherwise.
Functional determinants; partitions of partitions; Euler transform applied twice to all 1's sequence.
Solution a() of the complementary equation a(n) + b(n) = 5*n, where a(1) = 1. See Comments.
Triangle T(n,k) giving number of rooted maps regardless of genus with n edges and k nodes (n >= 0, k = 1..n+1).
Integers k such that 2^(k-1) == 1 (mod k).
Numbers k such that 2k-1 is prime.
Filter sequence for a(primes > 3) = constant sequences.
Number A(n,k) of length-n restricted growth strings (RGS) with growth <= k and fixed first element; square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals.
Number of integers ranging from 2 to n that are not prime-powers.

a(n) is the number of steps needed to reach a stable configuration in the 1D cellular automaton initialized with one cell with mass n and based on the rule 'each cell gives half of its mass, rounded down, to its right neighbor'.

Rectangular array read by downward antidiagonals; row n consists of the numbers m such that n is the denominator of d(k)/d(1) + d(k-1)/d(2) + ... + d(k)/d(1), where d(1),d(2),...,d(k) are the unitary divisors of m.
Let p = prime(n); a(n) = number of pairs of primes (i,j) with i < j < p such that i*j == 1 (mod p).
a(0)=0, a(1)=1; thereafter a(n) = a(n-2)+a(n-1), keeping just the digits that appear exactly once.
a(n) = max{k: f(n),...,f^k(n) are prime}, where f(m) = 2m+1 and f^k denotes composition of f with itself k times.
One of the three successive approximations up to 13^n for 13-adic integer 5^(1/3). This is the 7 (mod 13) case (except for n = 0).
One of the three successive approximations up to 13^n for 13-adic integer 5^(1/3). This is the 8 (mod 13) case (except for n = 0).
One of the three successive approximations up to 13^n for 13-adic integer 5^(1/3). This is the 11 (mod 13) case (except for n = 0).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the unreduced numerator of the k-th weight in the quadrature rule for parabolic runout spline with respect to a mesh of n + 1 points.
Break the infinite word 1232112321... into chunks so that the sum of the digits in the n-th chunk is n.

Triangle read by rows: first row is 2; given row k, define the elements of row k+1 to be the (sorted) elements derived from row k by two recursion rules: (i.) if x is in row k, then (x+3)^2 is in row k+1; (ii.) if x^2 is in row k, then x is in row k+1.
Number of polynomial symmetric functions of matrix of order n under separate row and column permutations.
Numbers of the form (x - y)(x^2 - y^2) with x > y > 0.
Number of partitions of the n-th prime into parts that are all primes.
Describe n from left to right in terms of blocks with the maximum number of repetitions (and then with the maximum size).
Number of composite divisors of n that are < n.
Write n in base 10, lengthen all the runs of successive identical digits by 1.
Write n in base 10, shorten all the runs of successive identical digits by 1.
The Riordan square of the Lucas numbers, triangle read by rows, T(n, k) for 0 <= k <= n.
The Riordan square of the large Schröder numbers, triangle read by rows, T(n, k) for 0 <= k <= n.
The Riordan square of the double factorial of odd numbers. Triangle T(n, k), 0 <= k <= n, read by rows.
The Riordan square of the Euler numbers. Triangle T(n, k), 0 <= k <= n, read by rows.

Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the sum of the number of the arrangements of p_1 1's, p_2 2's, ..., p_k k's (p_1 + p_2 + ... + p_k = n and p_1 >= p_2 >= ... >= p_k) avoiding equal consecutive terms, where 1 <= k <= n.
a(n) = Pi(8,3)(n) + Pi(8,5)(n) - Pi(8,1)(n) - Pi(8,7)(n) where Pi(a,b)(x) denotes the number of primes in the arithmetic progression a*k + b less than or equal to x.
a(n) = Pi(5,2)(n) + Pi(5,3)(n) - Pi(5,1)(n) - Pi(5,4)(n) where Pi(a,b)(x) denotes the number of primes in the arithmetic progression a*k + b less than or equal to x.
a(n) = Pi(12,5)(n) + Pi(12,7)(n) - Pi(12,1)(n) - Pi(12,11)(n) where Pi(a,b)(x) denotes the number of primes in the arithmetic progression a*k + b less than or equal to x.
Number of primes congruent to 3, 5, 6 modulo 7 and <= n minus number of primes congruent to 1, 2, 4 modulo 7 and <= n.
Number of primes congruent to 2, 6, 7, 8, 10 modulo 11 and <= n minus number of primes congruent to 1, 3, 4, 5, 9 modulo 11 and <= n.
Array of sequences read by descending antidiagonals, A(n) the Jacobi square of the sequence n, n+1, n+2, ....
Array of sequences read by descending antidiagonals, row A(n) is Stieltjes generated from the sequence n, n+1, n+2, n+3, ....
(Number of numbers <= n with an odd number of distinct prime factors) - (number of numbers <= n with an even number of distinct prime factors).
Number of primes between successive n's, where n mod 10 = 5.
a(n) is the smallest prime number whose a056240-type is n (see Comments).
Numbers having at least 3 unique partitions into exactly 3 parts with the same product.
Nonnegative integers that can be made by using six sixes (6 6's) and the four basic operators {+, -, *, /}.
Nonnegative integers that can be computed using exactly seven 7's and the four basic arithmetic operations {+, -, *, /}.
Nonnegative integers that can be computed using exactly eight 8's and the four basic arithmetic operations {+, -, *, /}.
1-parking triangle T(r, i, 1) read by rows: T(r, i, k) = (r + 1)^(i-1)*binomial(k*(r + 1) + r - i - 1, r - i) with k = 1 and 0 <= i <= r.
2-parking triangle T(r, i, 2) read by rows: T(r, i, k) = (r + 1)^(i-1)*binomial(k*(r + 1) + r - i - 1, r - i) with k = 2 and 0 <= i <= r.
Ratios of successive terms are 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, ...
Ratios of successive terms are 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, ...
4-parking triangle T(r, i, 4) read by rows: T(r, i, k) = (r + 1)^(i-1)*binomial(k*(r + 1) + r - i - 1, r - i) with k = 4 and 0 <= i <= r.
Composite hypotenuses of primitive Pythagorean triangles.
Circumdiameters of non-Pythagorean primitive Heronian triangles (no repetitions).
Replace in n each nonzero digit d with prime(d).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any n >= 0, the number of 1's in the base 4 expansion of n equals the number of 2's in the base 4 expansion of a(n).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that for any n > 0 there are no more than a(n) numbers k > 0 such that a(n + k) = a(n + 2*k).
Partial sums of numbers that are not squarefree.
Pair addition table cast as diagonal numbers.
Decimal expansion of x = 0.7271601514124259243... solution to 1 + 3^x = 5^x.
Decimal expansion of the solution x = 0.56389552425993647949... to 1 + 2^x = 5^x.
Decimal expansion of the solution x = 0.4895363211996... to 1 + 2^x = 6^x.
Decimal expansion of the solution x = 0.6009668516... to 1 + 3^x = 6^x.
a(n) is the least positive number which yields a multiple of n when its binary digit string, S(n), is read in any numeric base; a(n) is displayed in base 10.
Solution sequence (a(n)) of the complementary equation a(n) = 6 b(n+1) - 2 b(n), with b(0) = 1.
Numbers all of whose divisors are binary palindromes.
Dirichlet g.f.: Product_{p prime} 1 / (1 - p^(-s))^p.

a(1) = 1 and a(2) = 2. Subsequent terms are generated like this: if a(m) is the last term available -- say a(2) -- then a(m+1) = a(m) * a(m-1), a(m+2) = a(m) * a(m-1) * a(m-2), ..., a(2*m-1) = a(m) * a(m-1) * a(m-2) * ... * a(2) * a(1), a(2*m) = a(2*m-1) * a(2*m-2), and so on.
Smallest order of a group with an irreducible complex representation of dimension n.
a(n) is the least prime P such that log(P)/log(p) >= valuation(n,p) for all primes p.
Irregular triangle read by rows: representative solutions of the congruences x^2 - 1 == 0 (mod m) or (inclusive) x^2 + 1 == 0 (mod m), for m >= 1.
Centered cube numbers: n^3 + (n+1)^3.
Centered icosahedral (or cuboctahedral) numbers, also crystal ball sequence for f.c.c. lattice.
Products of distinct odd primes of squarefree index.
The number of regions inside a heptagon formed by the straight line segments mutually connecting all vertices and all points that divide the sides into n equal parts.
a(n) is the smallest m for which there is a sequence n = b_1 < b_2 < ... < b_t = m such that b_1*b_2*...*b_t is a perfect cube.
a(1) = 1; thereafter a(n+1) > a(n) is the smallest multiple of a(n) using only odd digits but not divisible by 3.
a(1) = 1; thereafter a(n+1) > a(n) is the smallest multiple of a(n) using only odd digits but not divisible by 9.
a(n) is the greatest k such that there is an increasing sequence of positive integers j(0),j(1),...,j(k) such that n == i (mod j(i)) for each i.
Runs-resistance minus cuts-resistance of the binary expansion of n.
Numbers that set new records for the most ordered prime factorizations.
Numbers k such that there exist numbers M_k which, when 1 is placed at both ends of M_k, the number M_k is multiplied by k.
Product of first n primes of form 6k-1.
a(n) = Product_{k=1..floor((n-1)/2)} (1 + 8*cos(k*Pi/n)^2) for n >= 0.
Product of the first n primes of the form 6k+1.

a(n) is the number of 'generalized signotopes', i.e., mappings X:{{1..n} choose 3}->{+,-} such that for any four indices a < b < c < d, the sequence X(a,b,c), X(a,b,d), X(a,c,d), X(b,c,d) changes its sign at most twice (equivalently +-+- and -+-+ are forbidden).
Numbers having at least two different ordered partitions p+q and (p+2)+(q-2) where p, q, p+2 and q-2 are all prime.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive numbers such that for any n > 0, a(n) XOR a(n+1) is a prime number (where XOR denotes the bitwise XOR operator).
a(n) = 1 for n < 2; a(n) = freq(a(n-1),n) * freq(a(n-2),n) for n >= 2, where freq(i,j) is the number of times i appears in [a(0),a(1),...,a(j-1)].

Irregular table read by rows; if the binary representation of n encodes the last row of a tiling of a staircase polyomino, then the n-th row contains the numbers k whose binary representation encode possible penultimate rows.
a(n) = minimal positive k such that the concatenation of the binary expansions of n,n+1,...,n+k is divisible by n+k+1, or -1 if no such k exists.
Numbers expressible as the sum of no more than 5 squares of composite numbers, allowing repetitions.
Smallest abundant number (sigma(x) > 2x) which is not divisible by any of the first n primes.
Numbers m such that 4^k*m, for integer k >= 0, are numbers having a unique partition into three squares.

Irregular triangle read by rows: consider the structure formed by drawing the lines connecting any two of the 2*(n+2) perimeter points of an (n+1) X 3 rectangular grid of points (or equally, an n X 2 grid of squares); row n gives number of cells with k sides, for k >= 3.
Geometric Connell sequence: 1 odd, 2 even, 4 odd, 8 even, ...
Numbers having at least one pair (x,y) of divisors with x<y such that x+y is also a divisor.
Numbers whose sum of prime factors is prime (counted with multiplicity).
Number of abundant divisors of n.
Irregular triangle read by rows in which row n lists the differences between consecutive divisors of n.
a(1) = 1, then a(n) is the smallest square not occurring earlier and starting with the last nonzero digit of a(n-1).
a(n) is the maximal number of 1 X 1 squares in an arrangement of n squares, from 1 X 1 to n X n.
Table read by ascending antidiagonals of coefficients in row functions R(n,x) such that [x^k] exp( k^n * x ) / R(n,x) = 0 for k>=1 and n>=1.
Numbers k such that k^2+1 and (k+2)^2+1 are both prime; twin k^2+1 primes.
Numbers k such that k^4 + 1 is prime.
Numbers n such that n^4+1 and (n+2)^4+1 are both prime.
a(1) = 2, a(n) = n * LeastPrimeFactor(n+1) / LeastPrimeFactor(n).
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 1, a(n) = n * LeastPrimeFactor(n-1) / LeastPrimeFactor(n).
a(1) = 2, a(n) = n * LargestPrimeFactor(n+1) / LargestPrimeFactor(n).
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 1, a(n) = n * LargestPrimeFactor(n-1) / LargestPrimeFactor(n).
Number of regions after 2n generations of Jim Conant's iterative dissection of a square.
Triangle read by rows: consider a figure made up of a row of n congruent rectangles and the diagonals of all visible rectangles; T(n,k) (1 <= k <= n) is the number of regions in the k-th rectangle.
The number of permutations p of {1,...,n} such that p(1)=1, p(n)=n, and |p(i)-p(i+1)| is in {1,2,3} for all i from 1 to n-1.
Numbers that can be expressed as both Sum x^y and Sum y^x where the x^y are not equal to y^x for any (x,y) pair and all (x,y) pairs are distinct.
a(n) is the least multiplier k such that n*k has twice as many divisors as n.
Irregular triangle: row n lists the odd numbers of the reduced residue system modulo n.
Non-deficient numbers with even sigma which are not Zumkeller.
Number of regions in a Y-shaped polygon with equal arms of length n (see the Comments for definition).
a(n) is the number formed by removing from n all duplicate digits except the leftmost copy of each.
Numbers m such that the equation m = k*sigma(k) has more than one solution.
Integers that can be written m = k*sigma(k) = q*sigma(q) where (k, q) is a primitive solution of this equation and sigma(m) is the sum of divisors of (m).
a(0) = 0; for n>0, minimal prime factor of n, or 1 if n is 1 or a prime.
Rearrangement of natural numbers so that next n numbers contain n as substring.
T(n, k) = (n + 1)*2^(n + k)*hypergeom([-n, k - n + 1], [2], 1/2), triangle read by rows for 0 <= k <= n.
T(n, k) = (k*(2*k+2)*(2*k+1)*(2*n-1)*binomial(2*(n-1),n-1))/(n*(n+1)*(n+2)) for n, k > 0 and T(0, 0) = 1. Triangle read by rows, for 0 <= k <= n.
Numerators of rationals (in lowest terms) used in a certain high temperature expansion.
If n = Product p(k)^e(k) then a(n) = LCM (p(k)^e(k) - 1).
If n = Product p(k)^e(k) then a(n) = LCM (p(k)-1)^e(k).
a(n) is the least integer k such that e * (n!)^(1/n) < n + k.
Consider the coefficients in the expansion of the n-th cyclotomic polynomial. a(n) is the difference between the extremes.
Irregular table read by rows: T(n,k) is the binary representation of n shifted right k times and incremented if the last bit shifted away was set.
a(n) is the smallest nonnegative number not in a(0..n-1) such that the sequence a(0..n) forms the starting row of an XOR-triangle with only distinct values in each row.
Write the Spanish name for n (ignoring spaces) and add numerical values of letters using a=1, b=2, ..., ñ=15, ..., y=26, z=27, n >= 0.
Irregular triangle read by rows in which row n lists n 1's followed by (n-1) 2's followed by (n-3) 3's ... followed by 1 n.
Number of primes that may be generated by changing any two digits of n simultaneously.

The binary expansion of a(n) is obtained by left-padding the binary expansion of n with 0's so that it has 2^k digits for some k > 0 as small as possible and then reversing the first half and the second half of this binary expansion.
Norms of prime elements in Z[sqrt(-2)], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt(-2)).

Represent the ring of Eisenstein integers E = {x+y*omega: x, y rational integers, omega = exp(2*Pi*i/3)} by the cells of a hexagonal grid; number the cells of the grid along a counterclockwise hexagonal spiral, with the cells 0, 1 numbered 0, 1. Sequence lists the index numbers of the cells which are 0 or a prime in E.

Represent the ring R = {x+y*sqrt(-2): x, y rational integers} by the cells centered at the points (x,y) of a square grid; number the cells of the grid along a counterclockwise square spiral, with the cells at (0,0) and (1,0) numbered 0, 1. Sequence lists the index numbers of the cells which are 0 or a prime in R.
Triangle T(n,k) (n >= 1, 0 <= k <= n-1) read by rows: number of distinct permutations after k steps of the 'optimist' algorithm.
a(n) is the least number k such that k^2+4*n is prime.
Composite numbers whose largest prime substring is greater than the record of all previous terms.
a(n) is half the n-th term of a truncated sesquinary (base 3/2) tree.
Multiplicative with a(p) = a(p-1) and a(p^e) = a(p) + a(e) if e>1.
Table of binary string substitutions: a(i,j) is obtained by substituting i for each 1-bit in j.
a(n) is the least sum of n consecutive primes that has exactly n distinct prime divisors.
Numbers k such that sum of the divisors d of k divides 1 + 2 + ... + k = k(k+1)/2.
10-adic integer x such that x^3 = -7/9.
Composite numbers m such that Product_{k=0..m} binomial(m,k) is divisible by m^(m-1).
Concatenation of all the distinct permutations of the first 1, 2, 3, ... (strictly) positive integers, arranged in ascending numerical order.
Smallest prime factor with minimum exponent in canonical prime factorization of n, a(1)=1.
a(n) = n + sopf(n) - omega(n).
First occurrence of prime gaps which are squares.
Array read by antidiagonals: A(n, k) is the digital root of n*k with n >= 0 and k >= 0.
a(n) is the number of integers k in the interval 0..n such that k and n-k can be added without carries in balanced ternary.

a(1) = 1; a(2) = 3; for n > 2, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not appeared that shares a factor with a(n-1) and whose binary expansion has a 1-bit in common with the binary expansion of a(n-1).
Number of iterations required to reach a power of 2 in the 3x+1 sequence starting at n.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any proper divisor d of n the binary expansions of a(d) and a(n) have no common 1's.
a(n) is the number of positive integers k <= n that have at least one common 1-bit with n.
Number of partitions of n having no parts equal to the size of their Durfee squares.
Stack polyominoes with square core.
Heinz numbers of even-length integer partitions of even numbers.
a(n) = 1 if the prime factorization of n contains as many even as odd prime indices, when counted with multiplicity, otherwise 0.
a(n) = 1 if the prime factorization of n has an even number of prime factors that sum to an even number, otherwise 0.

Let f be the completely multiplicative function from the positive integers to the cube roots of unity defined by f(prime(m)) = w^(2^(m-1)), where w is the cube root with positive imaginary part. a(n) is twice the real part of f(n).

T(n,m) is the number of non-congruent quadrilaterals with integer vertex coordinates (x1,1), (n,y2), (x3,m), (1,y4), 1 < x1, x3 < n, 1 < y2, y4 < m, m <= n, such that the 6 distances between the 4 vertices are distinct and (x3-x1)*(y4-y2) > 0, where T(n,m) is a triangle read by rows.

T(n,m) is the number of non-congruent quadrilaterals with integer vertex coordinates (x1,1), (n,y2), (x3,m), (1,y4), 1 < x1, x3 < n, 1 < y2, y4 < m, m <= n, such that the 6 distances between the 4 vertices are distinct and (x3-x1)*(y4-y2) < 0, where T(n,m) is a triangle read by rows.
The arithmetic derivative of n, modulo 2.
Let b(n) equal the product of the exponents in the prime factorization of n. Then a(n) gives the least k such that b(k) = n.
Primepi-based variant of the arithmetic derivative applied to the prime shadow of n.
a(n) is the least positive integer not occurring earlier in the sequence such that, if a(m) = a(n)+1, then |m - n| >= a(n).
Triangle read by rows, a Narayana related triangle whose rows are refinements of twice the Catalan numbers (for n >= 2).
Smallest k > 1 such that k^(n-1) == 1 (mod n^2).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such for any n > 0, a(n) and a(n+1) are coprime and have no common 1-bits in their binary expansions.
Arithmetic derivative of primorial base exp-function, reduced modulo 4.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that two consecutive terms can be added without carries in balanced ternary.
Number of terms in the Fibonacci-Lucas representation of n.
Number of terms in the Lucas-Fibonacci representation of n.
Numerators in series expansion of log(Product_{m>=0} (1+q^m)).
Denominators in series expansion of log(Product_{m>=1} (1+q^m)).
a(0)=0; thereafter a(n+1) = smallest missing nonnegative integer which is different from a(n)+1 and whose binary expansion has a 1-bit in common with the binary expansion of a(n)+1.
Nonnegative integers in which any odd digit, if present, occurs an even number of times, and any even digit, if present, occurs an odd number of times.
Largest squarefree number dividing sum of divisors of n.
a(n) = LCM_{p^e||n} sigma(p^e), where n = Product_{p^e||n}, with each p^e the maximal power of prime p that divides n.
The positions of nonzero digits in the ternary expansions of n and a(n) are the same, and the k-th leftmost nonzero digit in a(n) equals modulo 3 the product of the k leftmost nonzero digits in n.
The positions of nonzero digits in the ternary expansions of n and a(n) are the same, and the k-th rightmost nonzero digit in a(n) equals modulo 3 the product of the k rightmost nonzero digits in n.
The positions of nonzero digits in the balanced ternary expansions of n and a(n) are the same, and the k-th leftmost nonzero digit in a(n) equals the product of the k leftmost nonzero digits in n.

Irregular table read by rows: for each internal vertex of a regular n-gon with all diagonals drawn remove all the edges connected directly to the vertex and then count the sides in the polygon that surrounds it; row n gives the number of resulting k-sided polygons, for k>=4, for all internal vertices.
Expansion of zeta function of icosian ring.
Table T(i,j), i >= 0, j >= 0, read by antidiagonals giving the smallest number of moves needed to win Integer Lunar Lander, starting from position (i,j). Game rules in comments.
First digit to appear n times in the base-10 expansion of Pi.
Number of monic polynomials with integer coefficients of degree n with all roots in unit disc.
Discriminants of gothic Teichmuller curves.
Lexicographically least increasing sequence of semiprimes a(n) such that a(n) - a(n-1) and a(n) + a(n-1) are also semiprimes.
The n-th run occurs a(n) times, where each run is chosen to be shortest, then lexicographically earliest.
Triangle read by rows: lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that each column contains only multiples of the first number in that column. See example.
Numbers n such that n^d_1 + n^d_2 + ... n^d_k is prime where d_i is the i-th digit in the decimal representation of n.
Denominators of the harmonic means of the infinitary divisors of the positive integers.
Numerators of the harmonic means of the infinitary divisors of the positive integers.
Numbers k such that k/phi(k) equals sigma(x)/x  for some x<=k.

Number of partitions of 4*n into four odd primes (p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4) (p_1 < p_2 <= p_3 < p_4 and p_1 + p_4 = p_2 + p_3 = 2*n) such that (p_1, p_2) and (p_3, p_4) are consecutive pairs of prime numbers with the same difference, d = p_2 - p_1 = p_4 - p_3, and (p_1, p_3), (p_2, p_4) are also consecutive pairs of prime numbers with the same difference, D = p_3 - p_1 = p_4 - p_2.

Infinite triangle T(n, k), n, k >= 0, read and filled by rows the greedy way with distinct integers such that for any n, k >= 0, T(n, k) + T(n+1, k) + T(n+1, k+1) = 0; each term is minimal in absolute value and in case of a tie, preference is given to the positive value.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive base-10 palindromes such that a(n) + a(n+1) is prime.
Array read by ascending antidiagonals:  A(n, k) = (k^n - 1)/(k - 1), with k >= 2.
Smallest initial prime p for at least n primes in increasing arithmetic progression with a common difference less than p.
Array read by descending antidiagonals. A(n, k) is the number of multiset combinations of {0, 1} whose type is defined in the comments. Also A(n, k) = hypergeom([-k, -2], [1], n).
Expansion of g.f. A(x,y) satisfying y/x = Sum_{n=-oo..+oo} x^(n*(3*n+1)/2) * (A(x,y)^(3*n) - 1/A(x,y)^(3*n+1)), as a triangle read by rows.
Expansion of g.f. A(x,y) satisfying x*y = Sum_{n=-oo..+oo} x^(n*(3*n+1)/2) * (A(x,y)^(3*n) - 1/A(x,y)^(3*n+1)), as a triangle read by rows.

a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1; thereafter let b be the least power of 2 that does not appear in the binary expansions of a(n-2) and a(n-1), then a(n) is the smallest multiple of b that is not yet in the sequence.
Number of adjacent identical digits in the binary representation of n.
a(n) is the concatenation of n n times, n-1 n-1 times, ..., 22, 1.
Bi-unitary harmonic numbers.
Numerators of the harmonic means of the bi-unitary divisors of the positive integers.
Denominators of the harmonic means of the bi-unitary divisors of the positive integers.
a(n) is the number of distinct sums of one or more contiguous terms in the sequence thus far.
Numbers of form 3^i * prime(j), i>=0, j>0.

For any number k >= 0, let T_k be the triangle whose base corresponds to the ternary expansion of k (without leading zeros) and other values, say t above u and v, satisfy t = (-u-v) mod 3; the ternary expansion of a(n) corresponds to the left border of T_n (the most significant digit being at the bottom left corner).
a(1) = 2; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive integer > 1 not to share a factor with terms a(n-c .. n-1) where c = gcd(n-1,a(n-1)).
Primitive Zumkeller numbers.
Triangle T(n, k) of distinct positive integers, n > 0, k = 1..n, read by rows and filled in the greedy way such that T(n, k) is a multiple of T(n, 1).
Square array A(n, k) of distinct positive integers, n, k > 0, read and filled by upwards antidiagonals in the greedy way such that A(n, k) is a multiple of A(n, 1).
Square array A(n, k) of distinct positive integers, n, k > 0, read and filled by upwards antidiagonals in the greedy way such that A(n, k) is a multiple of A(n, 1) and of A(1, k).
Numbers that reach 0 after a suitable series of split-and-multiply operations (see Comments for precise definition).
Product of the smallest prime divisors of composite numbers between successive primes.
Matula-Goebel number of the prime tower factorization tree of n.
a(n) is the smallest prime p such that 7^n divides p^6 - 1.
a(n) is the largest index in [n] that maximizes tau.
Number of integers whose arithmetic derivative is equal to the n-th partial sum of primorial numbers.
Numbers of the form p*q*r where p,q,r are (not necessarily distinct) odd primes.
Palindromes with digits strictly increasing up to the middle digit.
Array read by ascending antidiagonals: A(n,k) is the number of words of length n over the alphabet [k] and sortable by a (2,1)-pop stack of depth 2.
Least number of inequivalent cells in a (planar) polyhex with n cells.
Least number of inequivalent cells in a polyiamond with n cells.
Number of representations of 12n-9 as a sum (p*q + p*r + q*r) with three odd primes p <= q <= r.
Number of representations of 12n-5 as a sum (p*q + p*r + q*r) with three odd primes p <= q <= r.
Number of representations of 12n-1 as a sum (p*q + p*r + q*r) with three odd primes p <= q <= r.
a(n) = number of odd divisors of n that have an even number of prime factors with multiplicity.
Table read by rows. T(n, k) = [z^k] LommelR(n, n, 1/z) where LommelR are the Lommel polynomials.
Numbers k such that the primorial base representation of their arithmetic derivative does not contain digits larger than 1.
a(n) is the largest coefficient of P(x) := Product_{k} (x + p_k), where (p_k) are the primes dividing n listed with multiplicity.

The number of terms beyond the first term for the series starting at k(1) = n and then iteratively finding the smallest k(i+1) such that k(i+1) - k(i) = sopfr(k(i+1) + k(i)), where i >= 1 and sopfr(m) is the sum of the primes dividing m, with repetition.

The sequence is a succession of triples of nonnegative integers. In each triple, the digits form a palindromic pattern. The sequence starts with a(0)=0 and is always extended with the smallest available integer not yet present in the sequence.
Largest cube <= n.
Cube excess: difference between n and largest cube <= n.
Short leg of more than one primitive Pythagorean triangle.
An infinite sequence over {0,1,2,3} without palindromes of length more than 1.
The largest noncomposite number k such that n is divisible by all the primes that do not exceed k.
a(n) is the maximum integer for which some minimum-length sum equaling a(n) of perfect squares less than n^2 excludes (n-1)^2.
Irregular table read by rows; for any n > 0, let u(n) be the least positive integer not among the first n-1 rows; the n-th row lists the u(n) least multiples of u(n) not yet in the sequence.
Carlitz-Riordan q-Catalan numbers (recurrence version) for q=2.
a(n) is the numerator of the probability that a self-avoiding random walk on the cubic lattice is trapped after n steps.
Numbers k such that both k+2 and k-2 are prime.
Signed denominators of Leibniz series for Pi/4.

Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct positive integers such that, for n > 2, a(n) shares a factor with a(n-2) mod a(n-1) while a(n-1) mod a(n) has not previously occurred as the mod value for any consecutive pair of terms.
Associated Stirling numbers.
Binary polynomials p(x) that are fixed points of the map p(x) -> p(x+1), evaluated as polynomials over Z at x=2.
A prime mountain: peaks and valleys beyond the origin correspond to prime abscissa (see Comments for precise definition).
Table read by ascending antidiagonals: T(k, n) is the number of distinct values of the magic constant in a perimeter-magic k-gon of order n.

Infinite sequence of integers a(1), a(2), ... such that for any n > 0, a(n) is as small as possible (in absolute value) and the means of consecutive terms are all distinct; in case of a tie, preference is given to the positive value.
Change every other 1 bit in binary expansion of n to 0.
Table read by ascending antidiagonals: T(k, n) is the maximum vertex sum in a perimeter-magic k-gon of order n.
Dirichlet g.f.: zeta(s-1) * (1 - 2^(-s)) / zeta(s).
Array read by ascending antidiagonals: A(n, k) = Sum_{j=0..k} tan(j*Pi/(1 + 2*k))^(2*n).
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = e*Gamma(n - k + 1, 1)*binomial(n, k)^2.
Smallest prime power greater than the n-th prime.
Smallest prime power >= n.
Largest power of a prime < prime(n).
Largest prime power <= n.
a(n) = n! (mod nextprime(n)).

Squares visited by a knight moving on a square-spiral numbered board where the knight moves to a square which has been previously visited the fewest number of times. If two or more such squares exist the smallest numbered square is chosen.
a(n) is the least k > n such that n is a primitive root modulo k, or -1 if there is no such k.
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 + x*A(x)/A(-x*A(x)^2).
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 + x*A(x)/A(-x*A(x))^2.
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 + x*A(x)/A(-x*A(x))^3.
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 + x*A(x)/A(-x*A(x))^4.
E.g.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = exp(x*A(x)/A(-x*A(x))).
E.g.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = exp(x*A(x)/A(-x*A(x))^2).
E.g.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = exp(x*A(x)/A(-x*A(x))^3).
Number of 4-dimensional cubic lattice walks that start and end at the origin after 2n steps, free to pass through origin at intermediate stages.
The number of divisors d of n such that (-d)^d == d (mod n).
Odd numbers producing 4 odd numbers in the Collatz iteration.
Sum of the divisors, except for the largest, of the n-th positive even number.
Number of factors over Q in the factorization of T_n(x) - 1 where T_n(x) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.
Sums of two nonnegative cubes.

Values of u in the quartets (1, u, v, w) of type 3; i.e., values of u for solutions to (1 - u) = v(v - w), in distinct positive integers, with v > 1, sorted by nondecreasing values of u; see Comments.
Numerators of partial sums for Liouville's constant.
a(n) = gcd_{primes P >= prime(n+1)} Product_{i=1..n} (P^2-i^2).
Triangle of Gaussian binomial coefficients (or q-binomial coefficients) [n,k] for q = 2, reduced mod 3.
Triangle read by rows where T(n,k), for 1 <= k < n, is the column number where (n-k)^2 occurs in an n X n grid filled rowwise with the numbers 1 to n^2.
The number of divisors d of n such that -(d^d) == d (mod n).
Number of rooted chains starting with the cycle (1)(2)(3)...(n) in the permutation poset of [n].
Primes of the form floor(kr+h), where r=(1+sqrt(5))/2 and h=1/2.
a(n) is the nearest integer to n/log_10(Pi).
The point numbers encountered by a rotating marker following the process described in the Comments.
Array read by ascending antidiagonals: A(n,k) is the number obtained by concatenation of n with k in that order, with k >= 0.
Graham-Sloane-type lower bound on the size of a ternary (n,3,3) constant-weight code.
a(n) = floor(3/5 * n^2), with a(1)=1.
Denominators of h(n) which is the minimum among the maxima of period n cycles of T(x) = 1 - 2 * |x-1/2|.
Numerator of h(n) which is the minimum among the maxima of period n cycles of T(x) = 1 - 2 * |x-1/2|.
Busy Beaver for lambda calculus BBλ: the maximum beta normal form size of any closed lambda term of size n, or 0 if no closed term of size n exists.
Binomial coefficient C(6n,n).
a(1) = prime(1) = 2, a(n) = 10*a(n-1) + (prime(n) mod 10).
Positive integers setting a new record for the sum of the square roots of the prime exponents.
Triangle read by rows: the numerators of the Lucas triangle.
Triangle read by rows: the denominators of the Lucas triangle.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers that can be partitioned into runs of pairwise coprime integers, the n-th such run having a(n) terms.
Numbers k with a unique combination of bigomega(k) and sopfr(k).
Numbers m >= 1 such that Sum_{k = 1..m} gcd(m, floor(m / k)) = Sum_{k = 1..m} gcd(m, ceiling(m / k)).
Perimeters of nondegenerate triangles with integer areas, whose side lengths are triangular numbers.
Irregular triangle read by rows where row n is the Stolarsky representation of n.
Triangle of coefficients T(n,k) of x^n*y^k in g.f. A(x,y) where A(x,y) = A(x^3 + 3*x*y*A(x,y)^3, y) / A(x^2 + 2*x*y*A(x,y)^2, y), read by rows.
Numbers that are congruent to {0, 1, 4, 5, 6} mod 8.
Numbers that can be written as s_1^x_1 + ... + s_t^x_t, with 1 < s_1 < ... < s_t and {s_1,..., s_t} = {x_1,..., x_t} for some t > 0.
a(1) = 2, and for any n > 1, a(n) is the largest k < n such that a(1) + ... + a(k) is prime.
Triangular irregular array: T(n,k) is the number of permutations on n letters with cycle type set [k].
Triangular irregular array: T(n,k) is the number of permutations on n letters with k cycles where the cycle type set is [m] for some m.
Numbers whose smallest prime factor is not 3, while the least prime not dividing their arithmetic derivative is 3.
a(n) = 1 if the least prime not dividing the arithmetic derivative of n is equal to the least prime dividing n, otherwise 0. a(1) = 1 by convention.
Distance from 2^n to the nearest base-10 palindrome.
Number of primitive Pythagorean triangles with long leg n.
Numbers k such that there exists m < k/2 such that 10^k - 10^m - 1 is a reversible prime; i.e., a palindromic prime or an emirp.
Triangle read by rows. T(n, k) = Sum_{i=0..k} C(k, i) * C(n - i, floor((n - i) / 2)).
Square 'central binomial coefficients'-array read by antidiagonals.
Numbers that are the smaller of two distinct positive integers with opposite abundances, where this pair of abundances occurs for the first time; sorted by the larger term.
Numbers that are the larger of two distinct positive integers with opposite abundances, where this pair of abundances occurs for the first time; sorted by the larger term.
Smallest integer m > 1 such that gcd(m^(prime(n)*k) - 1, m! - 1) > 1 holds for each positive integer k.
Manhattan distance from 0 to n in perfect shuffle array of base-2 expansions.
List giving least odd integer of each prime signature.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct prime numbers such that for any n > 0, the bottom entry in the absolute difference triangle of the first n terms is different from 1.
Number of divisors d of n which also divide (n/d)^2 - 1.
Decimal expansion of the smallest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 4.
Decimal expansion of the largest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 4.
Decimal expansion of the smallest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 5.
Decimal expansion of the largest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 5.
Decimal expansion of the smallest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 6.
Decimal expansion of the second smallest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 6.
Decimal expansion of the largest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 6.
Decimal expansion of the smallest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 7.
Decimal expansion of the second smallest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 7.
Decimal expansion of the largest positive zero of the Hermite polynomial of degree 7.
Decimal expansion of (2^8*Pi^2)^(1/3).
The grid points at integer Euclidean distance from the central point of an infinite square spiral.
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = numerator(8*n^3*k/(k^2+4*n^2)).
Number of prime factors of n-th Fibonacci number, counted with multiplicity.
Greatest integer b such that the sum of the integer digits of n in bases 2..b strictly increases.
Rectangular table, read by ascending antidiagonals, in which the n-th row o.g.f. R(n,x) satisfies: [x^m] exp( m*(m+1) * x*R(n,x)^n ) / R(n,x)^(m+1) = 0 for m >= 1, n >= 0.
Halting time for Wolfram's 2-state 3-symbol Turing machine 840971 when started with n on the tape.
a(n) is the number of unit squares in the square lattice, divided by 4, that have 1 vertex strictly inside and 3 vertices strictly outside the circle x^2 + y^2 = n.
a(n) is the number of unit squares in the square lattice, divided by 8, that have 2 vertices strictly inside and 2 vertices strictly outside the circle x^2 + y^2 = n.
Number of composites of the form n^2 + 1 between two successive primes of this form.
Rectangular array, read by ascending antidiagonals, where the n-th row o.g.f. R(n,x) satisfies: [x^m] exp( m^2*(m + n)*x - m*R(n,x) ) = 0 for m >= 1, n >= 0.
A variant of Sierpinski carpet, read by antidiagonals.
Least m such that (2k+1)*2^m + 1 is a prime factor of the Fermat number 2^(2^n) + 1.
Nonnegative integers that have only one largest digit m and the sum of the digits equal to 2*m.

Start with a point at (0,0). At each iteration, add a new point by going one step up or to the right from the current point, choosing the option that gives the least maximum number of points on a line through the new point. In case of ties, compare the number of points on the line with the next largest number of points, etc. If there is still a tie, go to the right. a(n) is 0 if the n-th step is to the right, 1 if the step is upwards.

Start with a point at (0,0,0). At each iteration, add a new point by increasing one of the coordinates of the current point by 1, choosing the option that gives the least maximum number of points on a line through the new point. In case of ties, compare the number of points on the line with the next largest number of points, etc. If there is still a tie, choose the first among the optimal coordinates. a(n) is the zero-based index of the coordinate that is increased in the n-th step.
Largest number of distinct lines determined by pairs of cell centers of a polycube with n cells.
a(n) is the difference of n and the product of the indices of prime factors of n with multiplicity, a(1) = 0.
Numbers k with the property that k^2, k^2+1 and k^2+2 are all semiprimes.
Number of new penny-penny contacts when putting pennies on a table following a spiral pattern.
a(n) = 3*n + 2^v(n) where v(n) denotes the 2-adic valuation of n.
Circuit cost of the hardest Boolean function of n variables; metric: 2-input AND-gates cost 1, NOT is free, fanout is free, inputs are free, no feedback allowed.
The total sum of infinitary divisors of the infinitary divisors of n.
Half the number of changes in the cyclic column words of the Gosper-Lafitte triangle.
Prime powers p^e where p is a prime and e is odd.
Decimal expansion of abs(Gamma(1 - exp(2*Pi*i/3)/2))^2, where i = sqrt(-1).
Triangle read by rows in which row n lists divisors d of n such that n divides d^n.
Product of all primes up to 3^n.
a(n) = -(-1)^n times sum of divisors of n.
a(0) = 1, a(1) = 0, a(2) = -1; for n >= 3, a(n) = - a(n-2) + Sum_{ primes p with 3 <= p <= n} a(n-p).
Number of compositions of n into a sum of odd primes.
Primes with record values of the least positive primitive root.
Primes with record values of the least positive prime primitive root.
Number of permutations p on the set [n] with the properties that abs(p(i)-i) <= 3 for all i and p(1) <= 2.
E.g.f.: exp(x)/sqrt(1-x^2).
Number of maximal collections of pairwise disjoint subsets {X,Y,Z} of {1, 2, ..., n}, each satisfying X + Y = Z.
Numbers of the form (p^2 - 49)/120 where p is prime.
Numbers of the form (p^2 - 1)/120 where p is 1 or prime.
The minimum number of nodes of a tree with a cutting center of n nodes.
Numbers k such that the continued fraction for sqrt(k) has odd period length.
Smallest number that takes n steps to reach 1 under iteration of sum-of-squares-of-digits map (= smallest 'happy number' of height n).
Primes reached after k iterations of sum of n and its prime divisors = t (where t replaces n in each iteration).
Waring's problem: conjectured values for G(n), the smallest number m such that every sufficiently large number is the sum of at most m n-th powers of positive integers.
Beginning with the natural numbers, swap the k-th prime and k-th composite.
a(n) = j if n = [ j*sqrt(2) ], else a(n) = k if n = [ k*(2 + sqrt(2)) ].
a(n) = a(m) if a(m) has already occurred exactly once and n = a(m)+m-1, else a(n) = least positive integer that has not yet occurred.
a(n) = least positive integer > a(n-1) and not a(i)*a(j) for 1<=i<j<=n, with initial terms 1,3.
Triangular array T read by rows: T(n,k) = number of partitions of n into distinct parts, the greatest being k, for k=1,2,...,n.
Summarize the previous term! (in decreasing order).
One half of triple factorial numbers.
a(n) = (n+1)*binomial(n+6,6).
a(n) = k, where k/(product of digits of k) is least possible integer for k with n digits.
a(n) = that n-digit number m which gives minimal integral value of m/(sum of digits of m); in case of a tie pick the smallest.
Numbers that are the product of two distinct Lucas numbers.
Numbers that are the product of two Lucas numbers.
Numbers of the form Fibonacci(i)*Lucas(j), 0 <= i < j.
Numbers of the form Fibonacci(i)*Lucas(j), i <= j.
Keith numbers, or Repfigit (REPlicating FIbonacci diGIT) numbers.
Indices of consecutive squares palindromic primes; x such that x^2 + (x+1)^2 is palindromic and prime.
a(n) is the number of ways to write n as an mterm, where an mterm is an unordered sum which is either 2, or 1 + an unordered product of mterms.
One even number followed by two odd numbers.
Number of ways n is a product of squarefree numbers > 1.
Number of factorizations of n into distinct squarefree numbers > 1.
