The square sieve.
Put and say how often: a(n) = n/2 if n is even, else a(n) = number of matches of 'a(n-1)' in the concatenation of all 'a(i)' with i < n, where 'x' denotes the decimal string of x.
a(n) = nearest integer to n^2 * cos(sqrt(n)).
a(n) = nearest integer to n^2 * sin(sqrt(n)).
Triangle of coefficients in expansion of (1 + x + x^2 + x^3 + x^4)^n.
Irregular triangular array having n-th row g(n) defined in Comments.
Triangular array read by rows: g(n,k) = 1 for n >= 0; g(n,k) = 0 if k > n; g(n,k) = g(n-1,k-1) + g(n-1,2k) for n > 0, k > 1.
Decimal expansion of limiting ratio described in Comments.
Decimal expansion of limiting ratio described in Comments.
Decimal expansion of limiting ratio described in Comments.
Numbers k = p_1^s_1...p_m^s_m such that k/p_i^s_i  == 1 (mod p_i) for all 0 < i <= m.
Numbers that have a unique representation as a sum of three nonzero squares, and furthermore in this representation the squares are distinct.
Triangle of the natural numbers written by decreasing antidiagonals.
Number of representations of n as a sum of Fibonacci numbers (1 is allowed twice as a part).
Number of binary vectors of length n containing no singletons.
a(n) = F(n+1) + L(n), where F(n) and L(n) are Fibonacci and Lucas numbers, respectively.
Numbers k such that numerator(Bernoulli(2*k)/(2*k)) is different from numerator(Bernoulli(2*k)/(2*k*(2*k-1))).
Order of group generated by perfect shuffles of 2n cards.
Number of parts in all partitions of n into distinct parts.
Numbers that are a product of distinct Lucas numbers (2,1,3,4,7,11,...)

Lexicographically first sequence of nonprime terms (with no duplicates) that turns into a sequence of prime terms (with no duplicates) by applying the 'comma-permutation' simultaneously at every comma. [The 'comma-permutation' is explained in the Comments section.].
Numbers that are a product of two distinct Fibonacci numbers >1 or two distinct Lucas numbers > 0 (excluding 2).
Numbers that are the sum of 4 positive cubes in 1 or more way.
Numbers n for which the generalized Pell equation x^2 - n*y^2 = n(n-1)(n+1)/3 has an integer solution for x and y.

Triangle T, read by rows, where T(n,k) = [T^(3^k)](n-k,0) * (3^k)^(n-k) for n>=k>=0 such that row n of the 3^(n-1)-th root of T consists solely of integers given by: [T^( 1/3^(n-1) )](n,k) = (3^k)^(n-k) for n>=0.
Odd prime factors of generalized Fermat numbers of the form 3^(2^m) + 1 with m >= 0.
Odd prime factors of generalized Fermat numbers of the form 5^(2^m) + 1 with m >= 0.
Prime factors of generalized Fermat numbers of the form 6^(2^m) + 1 with m >= 0.
Odd prime factors of generalized Fermat numbers of the form 7^(2^m) + 1 with m >= 0.
Odd prime factors of generalized Fermat numbers of the form 11^(2^m) + 1 with m >= 0.
Prime factors of generalized Fermat numbers of the form 12^(2^m) + 1 with m >= 0.
Successively larger gaps in Ulam numbers start at this Ulam number.
Irregular triangular array read by rows: coefficients in expansion of Gosper's q-sine function sin_q(Pi*z).
Irregular triangular array read by rows: coefficients in expansion of Gosper's q-cosine function cos_q(Pi*z).
Nathanson's orphan-counting function h(n).
Number of inequivalent labeled Hamiltonian circuits on n-octahedron. Interlacing chords joining 2n points on circle.
Square array read by antidiagonals: T(m,n) (m>=0, n>=0) = (2^floor(m/2)-1)*(2^ceiling(n/2)+1).
Irregular triangle which lists in row n the divisors of 2*n+1.
At stage 1, start with a unit square. At each successive stage add 4*(n-1) new squares around outside with edge-to-edge contacts. Sequence gives number of squares (regardless of size) at n-th stage.
Triangle read by rows: the q-analog of the swinging factorial which is defined as q-multinomial([floor(n/2), n mod 2, floor(n/2)]).
Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) (n>=0, 0 <= k <= n^2) = least number of squares attacked by k queens on an n X n board.
a(n) = F[n]_n(2), main diagonal of fast-iteration function applied to 2.
A positive integer n is included if d(n+d(n)) = d(n), where d(n) is the number of divisors of n.
Square array read by antidiagonals downwards (see Comments for definition).
Number of squares in triangle-shaped polyominoes obtained by adding three identical polyominoes to the previous one, starting with one L-tetromino.
Smallest odd number k divisible by 3 such that k*2^n-1 is a prime.
Smallest odd number k divisible by 3 such that k*2^n + 1 is prime.
Q-toothpick sequence with Q-toothpicks of radius 1 and 2 (see Comments for precise definition).
Squarefree palindromes.
(Twice product of first n primes) - 1.
Even numbers not divisible by 3 which are not of the form p + 3^x with p prime.
Prime power decimal palindromes.
Lexicographic-first permutation of the nonnegative integers such that the partial sums (-1)^issquare(a(n))*a(n) always remain nonnegative.
Expansion of Product_{n>=1} (1-x^n)^5.
Expansion of Product_{n>=1} (1 - x^n)^7.
Numbers m > 0 that have a divisor d > 1 with binomial(m+d, d) == 1 mod m.
a(n) = product of n consecutive primes starting with nextprime(a(n-1)), with a(0) = 1.
Numbers whose base-3 representation consists entirely of 0's and 2's, except possibly for a single pair of adjacent 1's among them.
a(n) = gcd(r) where r ranges over the orders of all subgroups whose direct product gives the multiplicative group modulo n.
a(n) = product of indices of distinct prime factors of n, where index(prime(k)) = k.
Linear recurrence sequence with infrequent pseudoprimes, a(n) = -a(n-1) + a(n-2) - a(n-3) + a(n-5), with initial terms (5, -1, 3, -7, 11).
Numbers n that have a record maximum (> n) in their aliquot sequence.
Numbers n such that transient part of the unitary aliquot sequence for n sets a new record.
Numbers n that have a record maximum in their unitary aliquot sequence.
Number of iterations of phi(n) needed to reach 2.
Perfect totient numbers.
Maximal number of zeros that can be inserted one-by-one between the digits of prime(n) such that the number resulting from each step remains prime.
Narrow cross sequence (see Comments lines for definition).
Numbers which when chopped into two parts with equal length, added and squared result in the same number.
a(n) is the least integer k in the interval [2, sqrt(n)] such that k^n == k (mod n), or 0 if no such integer exists.
'Convex' primes: extremal primes in the sense of Tutaj.
Number of distinct values of X*(3*X-1)/2 mod n.
a(n) = 0 unless n = 3j^2+2j or 3j^2+4j+1 for some j>=0, in which case a(n) = (-1)^(j+1).
Weighted count of partitions of 2n+1 into odd parts in which the largest part appears an odd number of times and all other parts appear twice, with respect to a certain weight.
a(n) = weighted sum over all the self-conjugate partitions of 4n + 1 into odd parts, with respect to a certain weight.
Triangle read by rows: Polynomial coefficients per comment.
p-INVERT of the positive integers, where p(S) = 1 - 2*S^2.
p-INVERT of the positive integers, where p(S) = 1 - 3*S^2.
p-INVERT of the positive integers, where p(S) = 1 - 5*S^2.
p-INVERT of the positive integers, where p(S) = 1 - 6*S^2.
p-INVERT of the positive integers, where p(S) = 1 - 7*S^2.
p-INVERT of the positive integers, where p(S) = 1 - 8*S^2.
p-INVERT of the positive integers, where p(S) = 1 - 2*S - 2*S^2.
Zeroless numbers n with digits d_1, d_2, ... d_k such that d_1^2 + ... + d_k^2 is a square.
Number of cycles in all derangement permutations of {1,2,...,n}.
Number of labeled series-reduced mobiles (circular rooted trees) with n leaves (root has degree 0 or >= 2).
Coordination sequence of snub-632 tiling with respect to a trivalent node of type short-short-long.
Coordination sequence of snub-632 tiling with respect to a trivalent node of type short-short-short.
Coordination sequence of snub-632 tiling with respect to a hexavalent node.
Coordination sequence for Dual(3^3.4^2) tiling with respect to a trivalent node.
Coordination sequence of Dual(3.6.3.6) tiling with respect to a hexavalent node.
Coordination sequence of Dual(3.4.6.4) tiling with respect to a trivalent node.
Coordination sequence of Dual(3.4.6.4) tiling with respect to a tetravalent node.
Coordination sequence of the Dual(3.4.6.4) tiling with respect to a hexavalent node.
Coordination sequence of Dual(4.6.12) tiling with respect to a 12-valent node.
Coordination sequence of Dual(4.6.12) tiling with respect to a hexavalent node.
Coordination sequence of Dual(4.6.12) tiling with respect to a tetravalent node.
Either two less than a square or two more than a square.
Minimal size of a palindromic partition of the binary representation of n.
Let the decimal expansion of n be d_1 d_2 ... d_k; then a(n) = Sum_{i=1..k} d_i^(k+1-i).
Triangle read by rows: row n gives coefficients C(n,j) for a Sheffer sequence (binomial-type) with lowering operator (D-1)/2 + T{ (1/2) * exp[(D-1)/2] } where T(x) is Cayley's Tree function.
Rectangular array read by (upward) antidiagonals: A(n,k) = Sum_{j=0..k} (-1)^floor(j/2)*binomial(k-floor((j+1)/2), floor(j/2))*n^(k-j), n >= 1, k >= 0.
a(n) = n 2's sandwiched between two 1's.
Least strong pseudoprime to base n.
Coordination sequence for bey tiling (or net) with respect to a trivalent node.
Coordination sequence for bey tiling (or net) with respect to a tetravalent node.
Number of integer triangles with an integer area having relatively prime sides a, b and c such that a + b + c = n.
Number of times that i and 2n-i are both prime, for i = 1, ..., 2n-1.
a(n) = ceiling(sqrt(n!)).
Number A(n,k) of length-n restricted growth strings (RGS) with growth <= k and first element in [k]; square array A(n,k), n>=0, k>=0, read by antidiagonals.
Exponential series expansion of (exp(x*y) + sinh(x) - cosh(x))/(1 - x).
Number of convex triangular polyominoes containing n cells.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that for any n > 0 and any k > 0, floor((2^k) / a(n)) AND floor((2^k) / a(n+1)) = 0 (where AND denotes the bitwise AND operator).
Decimal representation of permutations of lengths 1, 2, 3, ...
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2, and for any n > 2, a(n) = o(n-1) + o(n-2) where o(k) is the number of occurrences of a(k) among a(1), ..., a(k).
Numbers k such that k, 2*k, and 3*k are anagrams of each other.
a(n) is the smallest k such that there exists a permutation b_0, b_1, ... of the maximal prime powers dividing n satisfying b_i | k+i for all i.
a(n) = (2/n), where (k/n) is the Kronecker symbol.
Primes which have fewer primitive roots than any larger prime.
Delete all consecutive identical decimal digits of n; write 0 if all digits disappear.
Numbers expressible in more than one way as i^2 + j^2 + k^2, where 1 <= i <= j <= k.
8 times triangular numbers: a(n) = 4*n*(n+1).
Smallest number m such that 2^m*n has 2 or more identical adjacent decimal digits or -1 if no such m exists.
Non-coprime pseudoprimes or primes to base 3: numbers k that are multiples of 3 and are such that k divides 3^k - 3.
Least d for which the number with continued fraction [n,n,n,n...] is in Q(sqrt(d)).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that the product of any two consecutive terms can be computed without carry by long multiplication in base 10.
Lychrel numbers k that set a new record for the number of 'Reverse and Add' steps in base 2 needed to reach a Lychrel number m < k (i.e., its seed).
Smallest number m such that n*3^m has 2 or more identical adjacent decimal digits.
Number T(n,k) of occurrences of k in a (signed) displacement set of a permutation of [n] divided by |k|!; triangle T(n,k), n>=1, 1-n<=k<=n-1, read by rows.
Least multiple of n consisting of a succession of 1's followed by a succession of 0's.
Numbers k such that, for any divisor d of k, the Hamming weight of d divides k.
Totally multiplicative sequence with a(p) = (p-1)*(p+1) = p^2-1 for prime p.
a(n) = sigma(n)*phi(n).
The number of exponential infinitary divisors of n.
The bottom entry in the difference table of the binary digits of n.
Square array T(n,k), n > 0, k > 1, read by antidiagonals: T(n, k) = 1 when n <= 2 or k <= 2, T(n, k) = T(n-T(n-1, k-1), k-T(n-2, k-2)) + T(n-T(n-2, k-2), k-T(n-1, k-1)) otherwise.
a(n) = (denominator of B(n,x)) / (the squarefree kernel of n+1), where B(n,x) is the n-th Bernoulli polynomial.
Maximum number of unbordered conjugates for a binary word of length n.
a(n) = (k-1)/lambda(k), the index of the n-th Carmichael number k.
The Lychrel number a(n) sets a new record for the 'Reverse and Add' steps in base 8 needed to reach a Lychrel number m < a(n) (i.e., its seed).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that the product of two consecutive terms has at least 5 distinct Fermi-Dirac prime factors.
a(n) = Sum_{d|n} 2^d*phi(2*n/d).
Numbers that are the perimeter of a primitive Heronian isosceles triangle.
Self-stuffable numbers (see the Comments section for definition).
Square array T(n,k) (n >= 0, k >= 2) read by antidiagonals, where T(n,k) is the number of ways of writing n as Sum_{i>=0} c_i 2^i, c_i in {0,1,...,k-1}.
Let p1 <= p2 <= ... <= pk be the prime factors of n, with repetition; let s = 1/p1 + 1/(p1*p2) + 1/(p1*p2*p3) + ... + 1/(p1*p2*...*pk); a(n) = numerator of s. a(1)=0 by convention.
Let p1 <= p2 <= ... <= pk be the prime factors of n, with repetition; let s = 1/p1 + 1/(p1*p2) + 1/(p1*p2*p3) + ... + 1/(p1*p2*...*pk); a(n) = denominator of s. a(1)=1 by convention.

Triangle read by rows: let E denote the standard triangular 6-valent grid in the plane, regarded as a graph with the Eisenstein integers as vertices; row n gives the coordination sequence of the quotient graph E/nE.
Number of ON cells after n generations of two-dimensional automaton based on knight moves (see Comments for definition; here a cell is turned ON if 1 or 2 neighbors are ON).
Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) is the largest integer m such that m*k^k <= 2*n^k.
Numerator of the least possible squared diameter of an enclosing circle of a strictly convex lattice n-gon.

G.f. A(x,y) satisfies:  Sum_{n=-oo...+oo} (x^n + y)^n = exp( (1-y) * A(x,y) ) / (1-y), where A(x,y) = Sum_{n>=1} x^n/n * Sum{k=0..n-1} T(n,k)*y^k, written here as a flattened triangle of coefficients T(n,k) read by rows.
Scaled Chebyshev U-polynomials evaluated at sqrt(2).
Minimum number of shaded cells in an n X n Hitori solution grid.
a(n) = Sum_{i=1..phi(n)-1} (r(i+1)-r(i))^2 where r(1) = 1 < ... < n-1 = r(phi(n)) are the phi(n) integers relatively prime to n.
a(1) = 11. For all subsequent terms a(n), take a(n-1) and substitute for the k-th digit the binary number of times that digit has appeared in a(n-1), reading left to right from the 1st to k-th digit.
a(n) = sigma(2*n) * binomial(2*n,n)/2, for n >= 1.
a(n) is the coefficient of x^n*y^n/n in log( Product_{n>=1} 1/(1 - x^(2*n-1) - y^(2*n-1)) ), for n >= 1.
a(n) = coefficient of x^n*y^n/n in log( Product_{n>=1} 1/(1 - (x^(2*n) - y^(2*n))/(x - y)) ), for n >= 1.
a(n) = coefficient of x^n*y^n/n in Sum_{n>=1} -log(1 - (x^n + y^n)), for n >= 1.
a(n) = coefficient of x^(2*n)*y^n/n in Sum_{n>=1} -log(1 - (x^n + y^n)) for n >= 1.
a(n) = coefficient of x^(3*n)*y^n/n in Sum_{n>=1} -log(1 - (x^n + y^n)).

E.g.f. C(x,y) = 1 + Integral S(x,y)*C(y,x) dx such that C(x,y)^2 - S(x,y)^2 = 1 and C(y,x) = Integral S(y,x)*C(x,y) dy, where C(x,y) = Sum_{n>=0} Sum_{k=0..n} T(n,k) * x^(2*n-2*k)*y^(2*k)/((2*n-2*k)!*(2*k)!), as a triangle of coefficients T(n,k) read by rows.
a(n) = [x^(n-1)] Product_{k=1..n} (k + x - k*x^2), for n >= 1.
a(n) = [x^(n-1)] Product_{k=1..n} (k + x + k*x^2), for n >= 1.
Expansion of g.f. 1/sqrt(1 - 6*x - 7*x^2).
Expansion of g.f. 1/sqrt(1 - 10*x - 11*x^2).
Number of subgroups of dihedral group: sigma(n) + d(n).
a(n) is the largest minimal prime P such that, for any odd number b, the product P*b is a nonzero square modulo 8 and modulo each of the first n primes.
a(n) = Max_{c composite, c < n} (c + least prime factor of c).
Let d_i be the i-th divisor of n. Then a(n) is the largest k such that gcd(d_k, ..., d_tau(n)) = 1.
Sum of the first n*(n+1) primes.
a(n) = Product_{k=1..n-1} n!k, where n!k is k-tuple factorial of n.
a(n) is the value of the node of the Collatz tree encoded by the number n (see Comments for precise definition).
One of the two successive approximations up to 17^n for 17-adic integer sqrt(2). This is the 6 (mod 17) case (except for n = 0).
One of the two successive approximations up to 17^n for 17-adic integer sqrt(2). This is the 11 (mod 17) case (except for n = 0).
One of the two successive approximations up to 17^n for 17-adic integer sqrt(-2). This is the 7 (mod 17) case (except for n = 0).
One of the two successive approximations up to 17^n for 17-adic integer sqrt(-2). This is the 10 (mod 17) case (except for n = 0).
Prime divisors of Mersenne numbers. Primes p such that the multiplicative order of 2 modulo p is prime.
Minimum number of bit inversions to convert n into a prime.
Number of divisors d of n such that d-1 is prime.

E.g.f. S(x,y) = Integral C(x,y)*C(y,x) dx such that C(x,y)^2 - S(x,y)^2 = 1 and C(y,x) = 1 + Integral S(y,x)*C(x,y) dy, where S(x,y) = Sum_{n>=0} Sum_{k=0..n} T(n,k) * x^(2*n+1-2*k)*y^(2*k)/(2*n+1)!, as a triangle of coefficients T(n,k) read by rows.

E.g.f. C(x,y) = 1 + Integral S(x,y)*C(y,x) dx such that C(x,y)^2 - S(x,y)^2 = 1 and C(y,x) = Integral S(y,x)*C(x,y) dy, where C(x,y) = Sum_{n>=0} Sum_{k=0..n} T(n,k) * x^(2*n-2*k)*y^(2*k)/(2*n)!, as a triangle of coefficients T(n,k) read by rows.
Numbers k such that 141*2^k+1 is prime.
Irregular triangle read by rows in which n-th row lists all partitions of n, in graded reverse lexicographic ordering, using a compressed notation.
Values of x in the solutions to x^2 - 8*x*y + y^2 + 11 = 0, where 0 < x < y.
Number of hands a bartender needs to have in order to win at the blind bartender's problem with n glasses in a cycle.
a(n) = [x^(n-1)] Product_{k=1..n} (k + x + 2*k*x^2), for n >= 1.
Sequence (a(n): n >= 1) that shifts left 2 places under the 'CHK' (necklace, identity, unlabeled) transform and has initial terms a(1) = a(2) = 1.
a(n) contains the nonzero frequencies f(d) of digits d=0 .. 9 in all terms up to a(n-1) in concatenated form sorted with respect to d: f(0)//0//f(1)//1//...//f(9)//9. Initial term a(1)=0.
Numerator of average number of swaps needed to bubble sort a string of n distinct letters.
If the binary expansion of n is (b(1), ..., b(w)), then the binary expansion of a(n) is (b(1), b(3), b(5), ..., b(6), b(4), b(2)).
If the run lengths in binary expansion of n are (r(1), ..., r(w)), then the run lengths in binary expansion of a(n) are (r(1), r(3), r(5), ..., r(6), r(4), r(2)).
a(n) is the smallest integer k > 1 such that k cannot be expressed as a sum of distinct earlier terms nor is a multiple of any earlier term.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) = 2 if the concatenation of all the previous terms is prime and a(n) = 1 otherwise.
Negated discriminants of orders of imaginary quadratic fields with 1 class per genus (a finite sequence).
Integers k such that the length of decimal expansion of k^k is a repdigit.

Start with an empty stack S; for n = 1, 2, 3, ..., interpret the binary representation of n from left to right as follows: in case of bit 1, push the number 1 on top of S, in case of bit 0, replace the two numbers on top of S with their sum; a(n) gives the number on top of S after processing n.

Start with an empty stack S; for n = 1, 2, 3, ..., interpret the binary representation of n from left to right as follows: in case of bit 1, push the number 1 on top of S, in case of bit 0, replace the two numbers on top of S, say u on top of v, with u-v; a(n) gives the number on top of S after processing n.

Start with an empty stack S; for n = 1, 2, 3, ..., interpret the binary representation of n from left to right as follows: in case of bit 1, push the number 1 on top of S, in case of bit 0, replace the two numbers on top of S, say u on top of v, with v-u; a(n) gives the number on top of S after processing n.
Rearrangement of primes such that the sum of two consecutive terms is a square.
Palindromes in base 3 (written in base 10).
a(1) = 1 and for n > 0, a(n+1) = a(k) - a(n) where k is the number of terms equal to a(n) among the first n terms.
In the decimal expansion of n, replace each digit d with 2*d.
Add the odd terms and subtract the even ones, the result must always be a square. This is the lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers with this property.
Numbers whose k digits can be permuted into a new k-digit number according to rules explained in the Comments section.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms with an associate sequence t such that t(0) = 0, and for any n > 0, at least one of t(n-1) - a(n) or t(n-1) + a(n) is a palindrome; in case t(n-1) - a(n) is a palindrome, set t(n) = t(n-1) - a(n), otherwise set t(n) = t(n-1) + a(n).

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms with an associate sequence t such that t(0) = 0, and for any n > 0, at least one of t(n-1) - a(n) or t(n-1) + a(n) is a prime number; in case t(n-1) - a(n) is a prime number, set t(n) = t(n-1) - a(n), otherwise set t(n) = t(n-1) + a(n).

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms with an associate sequence t such that t(0) = 0, and for any n > 0, at least one of t(n-1) - a(n) or t(n-1) + a(n) is a square; in case t(n-1) - a(n) is a square, set t(n) = t(n-1) - a(n), otherwise set t(n) = t(n-1) + a(n).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive terms such that a(4n+1) is the sum of the next three terms, those three terms having the property that each of them is a substring of a(4n+1).
Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = gcd {x^n - x^k : x is an integer}, 0 < k < n.
Primes for which the sum of all preceding odd-indexed prime gaps is exactly one greater than the sum of all preceding even-indexed prime gaps.
Positive numbers k with property that if d is any nonzero digit of k then k mod d is also a digit of k.
Cyclotomic fields with class number 1 (or with unique factorization).
a(n) = Sum_{d dividing n} tau(d)^3 = (Sum_{d dividing n} tau(d))^2.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the product of two consecutive terms is always divisible by 4.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the product of two consecutive terms is always divisible by 6.
The orders, with repetition, of the non-cyclic finite simple groups that are subquotients of the sporadic finite simple groups.
The orders, with repetition, of the non-cyclic finite simple groups that are subquotients of the automorphism groups of sublattices of the Leech lattice.

The sequence (a(n) - a(n+1); n such that a(n) is prime) yields the original sequence: lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers with this property and no two nonprime terms in a row.
The concatenation of the products of every pair of consecutive digits of n (with a(n) = 0 for 0 <= n <= 9).

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms with an associate sequence t such that a(1) = t(1) = 1 and for n > 1, either a(n) divides t(n-1) (and in that case set t(n) = t(n-1)/a(n)) or a(n) is coprime to t(n-1) (and in that case set t(n) = t(n-1)*a(n)).
Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of colored digraphs on n nodes with color scheme given by the partitions of n in canonical ordering.
Length of trajectory of n under the map n -> n - 1 + n/gpf(n) or 0 if no fixed point is reached, where gpf(n) is the greatest prime factor of n.
Partial sums of sequence {1/(i^2+1): i=0..n} (denominators).
Tersum n + n.
Irregular table read by rows. The n-th row is the permutation of {0, 1, 2, ..., 2^n-1} given by T(n,k) = k(k+1)/2 (mod 2^n).

The squares visited on the 2D square (Ulam) spiral when starting at square 1 and then stepping to the closest unvisited square which contains a composite number. If two or more squares are the same distance from the current square then the one with the smallest composite number is chosen.
Formal inverse of triangle A080246. Unsigned version of A080245.
Number of divisors of n that are perfect powers.
This viral sequence dies if any single term is increased by 1 (the virus). See how the contamination quickly spreads in the Comments section.
Square array T(n,k) = (n - 2)*(k - 1)*k/2 + k, with n >= 0, k >= 0, read by antidiagonals upwards.
Numbers whose set of divisors contains a Pythagorean quadruple.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that for any m > 0, gaps between consecutive m's are all distinct.
Numbers with at least two prime factors such that the sum of the prime factors is prime.

Triangle read by rows, T(n,k) = Sum_{p in P(n,k)} Aut(p) where P(n,k) are the partitions of n with largest part k and Aut(p) = 1^j[1]*j[1]!*...*n^j[n]*j[n]! where j[m] is the number of parts in the partition p equal to m; for n>=0 and 0<=k<=n.
Members p of a pair of primes (p,q) such that the decimal digits of q are the 9's complement of the decimal digits of p.

Number of ON cells after n generations of cellular automaton based on a hexagonal grid and starting with two adjacent ON cells where an OFF cell is turned ON if exactly two of its six neighbors are ON.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that for any distinct m and n, Product_{k = m+1-a(m)..m} a(k) <> Product_{k = n+1-a(n)..n} a(k).
Minimum value of the cyclic self-convolution of the first n terms of the characteristic function of primes.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the nested cube root (a(n) + (a(n-1) + ... + (a(1))^(1/3)...)^(1/3))^(1/3) is an integer.

Initial terms are the first 11 odd prime numbers. After that each new term in the sequence is the sum of whichever subset of the previous 11 terms gives the smallest prime number that is larger than the largest term so far.
Let f(n) be the number of segments shown on a digital calculator to display n. Then a(n) is the number of terms in the sequence formed by iteration n -> f(n) until n = f(n).
a(n) = n + pi(n) - pi(n + pi(n)), where pi(n) is the prime count of n (n>=1).
Primes p such that the sum of p and the average of the primes immediately before and after p is prime.
Table read by antidiagonals upward: T(n,k) is the number of ways to move a chess queen from (1,1) to (n,k) in the first quadrant using only right, diagonal up-right, and diagonal up-left moves.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that for any distinct m and n, Sum_{k = m+1-a(m)..m} a(k) <> Sum_{k = n+1-a(n)..n} a(k).
a(n) is the largest number of squares of unit area connected only at corners and without holes that can be inscribed in an n X n square.
Irregular triangle T(n,k) read by rows: first row is 0, n-th row (n > 1) lists indices of distinct primes dividing n.
Numbers m such that the equation m = k*tau(k) has more than one solution, where tau(k) is the number of divisors of k.
Integers that can be written m = k*tau(k) = q*tau(q) where (k, q) is a primitive solution of this equation and tau(k) is the number of divisors of k.
Numbers k such that there is no square m^2 such that m^2 and k^2 have no common decimal digits but together use all 10 digits.
Primes p such that (p+2)/3 and (p+3)/2 are prime.
Numbers that can be written as a sum of at least three consecutive positive integers.

Irregular triangle T(n, m) read by rows: row n gives the distinct length ratios diagonal/side of regular n-gons, DSR(n, k), for n >= 2, k = 1, 2, ..., floor(n/2), expressed by the coefficients in the power basis of the Galois group Gal(Q(rho(n))/Q), where rho(n) = 2*cos(Pi/n), for n >= 2. T(1, 1) is set to 1.
a(n) = ceiling(10*log_10(n)).

a(n) is the number of iterations for n to reach 1 under the following scheme. If k == 0 (mod 3), then k -> k/3, if k == 1 (mod 3) k -> 2k, and if k == 2 (mod 3) add the middle two divisors of k and divide the result by 3.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any n > 0, a(1) XOR ... XOR a(n) is a square (where XOR denotes the bitwise XOR operator).
Numbers m with the property that the symmetric representation of sigma(m) has three parts of width one.
Least prime p such that p*n is not a totient number.
Difference between n and the second-smallest prime larger than n.
Decimal expansion of the smallest positive number 'c' such that numbers of the form 1+floor(c^(n^1.5)) for all n >= 0 are distinct primes.
a(1)=1 and a(2)=2. For all n > 2, a(n) is the smallest number > a(n-1) by a number > the difference between a(n-1) and a(n-2) so that consecutive terms of sequence are always relatively prime.
Number of sequences of consecutive nonnegative integers (including sequences of length 1) that sum to n.
Triangle of numbers generated by the Nekrasov-Okounkov formula.
a(n) is the sum of primes of the form n - 2*p for primes p < n/2.
a(n) is the greatest k such that 0 <= k < n and the k latest terms so far sum up to a square number.
Distance between consecutive pairs of primes differing by 6 (p, p+6).
Triangle T(n,m) = 1 + m*(m-n) read by rows, 0 <= m <= n.
Numbers m such that m^2 = i^2 + 2*j^2 + k^2 and i^2 + j^2 and j^2 + k^2 are square numbers and i, j, k > 0.
Numbers one less than composite numbers.
a(n) = Sum_{d|n} (d^2 mod n).
Least k such that n divides phi(k^2).
a(n) is the least prime divisor p_j of n such that if n = Product_{i=1..k} p_i^e_i and p_1 < p_2 < ... < p_k, then Product_{i=1..j-1} p_i^e_i <= sqrt(n) < Product_{i=j..k} p_i^e_i. a(1) = 1.

Base-10 numbers k whose number of divisors equals the number of divisors in R(k), where k is written in all bases from base-2 to base-10 and R(k), the digit reversal of k, is read as a number in the same base.
a(n) = 6 * GaussBinomial(2*n, 2, 2) / denominator(Bernoulli(2*n, 1)).
Sides s of squares that can be tiled with squares of two different sizes so that the number of large or small squares is the same.
Numbers n such that phi(n) = phi(n + phi(n)).
Number of nonnegative walks of n steps with step sizes 1 and 2, starting and ending at 0.
Sum of odd numbers in range 10*n to 10*n+9.
a(1)=1; for n>1, a(n) gives number of ways to write n as n = x^y, 2 <= x, 1 <= y.
The least common multiple of all divisors d of n-1 such that d+1 is a prime divisor of n; a(1) = 1.
Number of squares between n and 2*n inclusive.
Numerators of the n-th iteration of the alternating continued fraction formed from the positive integers, starting with (1 - ...).
Denominators of the n-th iteration of the alternating continued fraction formed from the positive integers, starting with (1 - ...).
Primes such that the previous two primes are a twin prime pair.
Numbers k such that phi(k) = phi(k - phi(k)).
a(n) is the number of positive Euler permutations of order n.
a(n) is the number of negative Euler permutations of order n.
Number of steps to reach 1 in `3x+1' (or Collatz) problem starting with n!.
Smallest number whose sum of cubes of digits is n.
Number of divisors of the n-th GF(2)[X]-polynomial.
a(n) = (PolyLog(-n, -i) - exp(i*Pi*n)*PolyLog(-n, i)) * i / exp(i*Pi*n/2).
Decimal expansion of x = 3*Sum_{n in E} 1/10^n where E is the set of numbers whose base-4 representation consists of only 0's and 1's.
Numbers, other than prime powers, whose distinct prime factors are consecutive primes.
Numbers of the form x*(x+1) * y*(y+1) ('bipronics') with x and y nonnegative integers.

Triangle T(n,k) read by rows: Sum_{k=0..binomial(n,2)} T(n,k)*q^k = n!*Sum_{pi} faq(n,q)/Product_{i=1..n} e(i)!*faq(i,q)^e(i), where pi runs over all nonnegative integer solutions to e(1) + 2*e(2) + ... + n*e(n) = n and faq(i,q) = Product_{j=1..i} (q^j-1)/(q-1), i = 1..n.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any n >= 0, the binary expansions of a(n) and a(n + a(n)) have no 1's in common.
a(0)=0, a(1)=1; for k >= 1, a(2*k+1) and a(2*k+2) are the two smallest numbers not yet in the sequence whose binary expansions have no 1's in common with the binary expansion of a(k).
Total variation of base-10 digits of n; see Comments.
Primes p such that the number of distinct prime factors omega of the product of the composite numbers between p and the next prime after p sets a new record.
a(n) is the least prime p such that the numerator of the sum of reciprocals of the 2*n+1 consecutive primes starting with p is a prime.
E.g.f.: Integral exp(-x*tan(x)) / cos(x) dx.
The stripe enumeration of N X N where N = {0, 1, 2, ...}, also called boustrophedonic Cantor enumeration. Terms are interleaved x and y coordinates.
If n is odd, then a(n) = 0; otherwise, a(n) = n.
The odd numbers interlaced with the constant-2 sequence.
Solutions to phi(n) = phi(sigma(n)) that are not given by Theorem 3 of Golomb's manuscript.
a(n) = LCM_{p^e||n} (q^(e+1)-1)/(q-1), when n = Product_{p^e||n}, with each p^e the maximal power of prime p that divides n, and q = nextPrime(p).
Expansion of e.g.f. exp(x*tanh(x)) (even powers only).
Triangle read by rows of generalized ménage numbers: T(n,k) is the number of permutations pi in S_n such that pi(i) != i and pi(i) != i+k (mod n) for all i; n, 1 <= k < n.
a(n) is the smallest positive integer which does not occur in any Lucas sequence in which the first term is at most n and the second term is at most the first term.
E.g.f. exp(tanh(x)^2) (even powers only).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers on a square spiral such that any 3X3 square of numbers sums to a prime.

Irregular triangle read by rows in which row n lists the partial sums of shell numbers and respective number of electrons for all occupied shells of the n-th element of the periodic table of the elements.

Table of A(n,k) read by antidiagonals, where A(n,1)=2, and every n+1 consecutive terms in row n are pairwise coprime. Terms are chosen to be the least increasing value compatible with these constraints.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers on a square spiral such that any 2 X 2 square of numbers sums to a prime, and that prime is unique for all such squares. Start with a(1) = 0.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers on a square spiral such that any 3 X 3 square of numbers sums to a prime, and these primes are distinct.
The Rijndael S-box used in the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES).
a(n) is the least nonnegative integer k for which there does not exist i < j with i+j=n and a(i)=a(j)=k.
Numbers k such that k and k+1 are both divisible by the square of their largest prime factor.
Primes p starting a sequence of 4 consecutive primes whose final digits are 1,3,7,9 (in any order).
Expansion of e.g.f. (1 - x)^x.
Expansion of e.g.f. (1 + x)^x.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not yet appeared that is coprime to a(n-1) and the difference a(n) - a(n-1) is distinct from all previous differences.

T(w,h) is the number of non-congruent quadrilaterals whose vertices with integer coordinates (x_i, y_i) all lie on the perimeter of a rectangle of width w and height h, with no 3 points on the same edge of the rectangle, max(x_i) - min(x_i) = w and max(y_i) - min(y_i) = h, such that the 6 distances between the 4 vertices are distinct.
Fixed point when iterating the function f on n, where f(x) = x + product of digits of x.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not yet appeared that shares a factor with a(n-1) and the difference | a(n) - a(n-1) | is distinct from all previous differences.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not yet appeared that is coprime to a(n-1) and the difference | a(n) - a(n-1) | is distinct from all previous differences.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not yet appeared that shares a factor with a(n-1) and the difference a(n) - a(n-1) is distinct from all previous differences.
Start with 2*n-1; repeatedly triple and add 2 until reaching a prime. a(n) = number of steps until reaching a prime > 2*n-1, or 0 if no prime is ever reached.
a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; for n > 2, a(n) is the smallest positive number that shares a factor with a(n-1) and the product a(n) * a(n-1) is distinct from all previous products a(i) * a(i-1), i=2..n-1.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number greater than 1 that is coprime to a(n-1) and the product a(n) * a(n-1) is distinct from all previous products a(i) * a(i-1), i=2..n-1.
a(n) is the greatest sum i + j + k + l where i^2 + j^2 + k^2 + l^2 = n and 0 <= i <= j <= k <= l.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number that is coprime to a(n-1) and the product a(n) * a(n-1) is distinct from all previous products a(i) * a(i-1), i=2..n-1.
Number of primes between n and n+log(n)^2.
Number of primes between n and n+log(n), exclusive.
Smallest highly composite number that has n prime factors counted with multiplicity.
Number of ways to choose a divisor of each part of the n-th composition in standard order such that no adjacent divisors are equal.
Number of distinct lengths of runs in the n-th composition in standard order.
Perfect powers j^k, such that k is the exponent of 2 in the factorization of j^k.
Largest quadratic nonresidue modulo n (with n >= 3).
Triangle read by rows. T(n, k) = Sum_{j=0..n}((-1)^(n-j)*binomial(n, j)*j^(n+k)) / n!.
Triangle read by rows. T(n, k) = |Stirling1(k + n, n)|.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) = n / the largest divisor of n that is coprime to a larger divisor of n.
Bases with smallest unhappy number (in that base) > 2.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is number of terms in the first n-1 terms of the sequence that have the same number of prime factors, counted with multiplicity, as a(n-1).
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is number of terms in the first n-1 terms of the sequence that have the same number of distinct prime factors as a(n-1).
Numbers k such that the digits of k are a subsequence of the digits of prime(k).
Table read by antidiagonals: T(n, k) = digitsum(n*k) with n >= 0 and k >= 0.
a(n) = Sum_{k = 0..w and t_k > 0} (-1)^t_k * 2^k, where Sum_{k = 0..w} t_k * 3^k is the ternary representation of n.
The base-3 expansion of a(n) is obtained by inserting a zero before each nonzero digit of the base-3 expansion of n.
Numbers k such that tau(sigma(k)) = tau(k) where tau(k) is the number of divisors of k and sigma(k) their sum.
Numbers k such that 2*k+1 divides 2^k+1.
Busy Beaver problem: a(n) is the maximal number of steps that an n-state Turing machine can make on an initially blank tape before eventually halting.
Irregular triangle read by rows: strictly decreasing sequences of nonnegative numbers given in lexicographic order.

Triangle read by rows. T(n, k) = ([x^k] P(n, x)) // k! where P(n, x) = Sum_{k=1..n} P(n - k, x) * x if n >= 1 and P(0, x) = 1. The notation 's // t' means integer division and is a shortcut for 'floor(s/t)'.
Expansion of (1-x)/(1-x-2*x^2+x^3).
Concatenate the binary strings for 1,2,...,n-1, n, n-1, ..., 2,1.
a(n) is the least number of 2 or more consecutive signed primes whose sum equals n.
Nonnegative numbers of the form x*y where x and y have the same set of decimal digits.
Square of the sum of the prime factors of n (with repetition).
The number of steps, starting from n, to reach k<=2 in an iteration k -> 2*k - (sum of proper factors of 2*k).
Triangle read by rows. T(n, k) = FallingFactorial(n - k, k) * Stirling2(n - k, k), for n >= 0 and 0 <= k <= n//2, where '//' denotes integer division.
a(n) is the number of ways in which the set of divisors of n can be partitioned into disjoint parts, all of length > 1 and with integer harmonic mean.
Numbers k such that the set of divisors {d | k, BitOr(k, d) = k} has an integer harmonic mean.
Triangle read by rows, T(n, k) = (-1)^k * RisingFactorial(n, k) * FallingFactorial(k - n, k).
Triangle read by rows, T(n, k) = 4^k * Gamma(n + k + 1/2) / Gamma(n - k + 1/2).
Number of 3-packed words of degree n.
a(0)=1, a(1)=1, a(n) = largest prime <= a(n-1) + a(n-2).
a(0)=0, a(1)=1, a(n) = smallest prime >= a(n-1) + a(n-2).
Array read by ascending antidiagonals: A(n, k) = (1 + 2*n)*k^n.
a(n) is the length of the longest arithmetic progression ending at a(n-1); a(1)=1.
a(n) is the right portion (reversed) of the base-phi representation of n in Knott's representation which uses the least number of 0's, the most 1's, and in which the right-hand portion is finite.
The part of n to the left of the decimal point in the Dekking-van-Loon-canonical base phi representation of n.
Decimal expansion of -2*cos(5*Pi/7).
Triangle read by rows: number of labeled partitions of n with maximin m.
n sets a record for the number of primes in {n, f(n), f(f(n)), ..., 1}, where f is the Collatz function defined by f(x) = x/2 if x is even; f(x) = 3x + 1 if x is odd.
The x-coordinates of the even-ranked elements of the lexicographically earliest sequence of points satisfying staircase and no-three-in-a-line conditions (see comments).
The greatest common divisor of the first and the second arithmetic derivative of n.
x such that x^2 - 27*y^2 = 1.
Number of idempotent Boolean relation matrices on [n] that have no proper power primitive.
Number of the rightmost decimal digits of n^(n^n) that are the same as those of n^(n^(n^n)).
Triangle read by rows. T(n, k) = (n - k + 1) * binomial(n + k + 1, 2*k)^2 / (n + k + 1).
Numbers with an even number of prime factors not of the form 8m+-1 (counting repetitions).
G.f. satisfies A(x) = sqrt( (1 + 2*x*A(x)) / (1 - 2*x*A(x)) ).
Difference between the bound provided by Dirichlet's Simultaneous Approximation Theorem applied to Z_n (for d=3) and the best possible bound.
Least number of vertices of a graph that contains an induced cycle of length k_i + 3 for i = 1, 2, ..., where n = 2^k_1 + 2^k_2 + ... is the binary expansion of n.
a(n) = binomial(3n-1, n-1).
Denominator of the continued fraction 1/(2-3/(3-4/(4-5/(...(n-1)-n/(n+2))))).
Numbers k such that there are fewer divisors of prime indices of k than there are prime indices of k.
Expansion of g.f. A(x) satisfying A( x*(1 + 2*x)*A(x) )^3 = A( x^2*(1 + 3*x)*A(x) )^2.
a(n) is the atomic number of the nuclide with the lowest energy among the isobars of mass number n.
n times n+4 gives the concatenation of two numbers m and m-4.
Dirichlet convolution of the identity function with omega.
Expansion of g.f. A(x) satisfying A( x*(1 + 3*x)*A(x)^2 )^5 = A( x^2*(1 + 5*x)*A(x)^3 )^3.
Expansion of g.f. A(x) satisfying A( x^2*(1 + 3*x)*A(x) )^5 = A( x^3*(1 + 5*x)*A(x)^2 )^3.
Expansion of g.f. A(x) satisfying A( x*(1 + 2*x)*A(x) )^3 = A( x*(1 + 3*x)*A(x)^2 )^2.
Number of distinct n-digit suffixes generated by iteratively multiplying an integer by 6, where the initial integer is 1.
Primes p such that valuation(p-1,2) is a record.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the Zeckendorf expansions of two consecutive terms have at least one common term.
Least prime p such that the sum of squares of the 2n + 1 consecutive primes starting with p is prime, or -1 if no such p exists.
Maximal power of 3 that divides n-th Catalan number.
Expansion of g.f. A(x) satisfying A(x) = exp(x*A(x) + L(x)), where L'(x) = is the least nonnegative integer series such that A(x) is an integer series with A'(0) = 1.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that for any n > 0, prime(n) AND a(n) = a(n) (where prime(n) denotes the n-th prime number and AND denotes the bitwise AND operator).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any n >= 0, a(n) AND a(n+1) equals 0, a(n) or a(n+1) (where AND denotes the bitwise AND operator).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any n >= 0, a(n) AND a(n+1) equals 0 or a(n) (where AND denotes the bitwise AND operator).

a(n) is the numerator of the ratio of winning probabilities P_A/P_B of winning in a 2-player game with a ratio of odds for A and B in a single round of 3:2. To win the game it is necessary to win n rounds in a row.
Given n-th prime p, a(n)=number of primes of the form p+q+1 where q is any prime < p.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that for any n > 1, a(n) is neither coprime to a(2*n) nor to a(2*n+1).
A(n, k) = 4^n*Pochhammer(k/4, n). Square array read by ascending antidiagonals.
Numbers k such that tau(k) | k'.

Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of nonempty, longest nonoverlapping properly nested substrings into which the k-th string of parentheses of length n can be split, where strings within a row are in reverse lexicographical order.
Decimal expansion of sqrt(3).
Lexicographically earliest sequence such that for any n>1, n=u*v, where u/v = a(n)/a(n-1) in reduced form.
A(n, k) = 2^n*Pochhammer(k/2, n). Square array read by ascending antidiagonals.
Decimal expansion of lemniscate constant A.
a(1) = a(2) = 1; a(n>2) is the greatest nonsquarefree number < prime(n).
Greatest nonsquarefree number <= n, or 1 if there is none (the case n <= 3).
Largest squarefree integer < the n-th prime.
Smallest nonsquarefree number >= n.
Numbers that are congruent to {0, 4} mod 6.
The smallest positive integer that produces a product that contains the digit 2 when multiplied by 2 a total of n times.
a(n) = floor(log_2(prime(n))).
Triangle read by rows, where row n is a block of length n*(n^2 + 1)/2, which is a permutation of the numbers of its constituents; see Comments.
Hypersigma(n), definition 1: sum of the divisors of n plus the recursive sum of the divisors of the restricted divisors.
Number of nonempty chains in the divides relation on the divisors of n.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of nonnegative integers such that each term does not belong to a Fibonacci-like sequence starting with two earlier terms.
Numbers such that the three numbers before and the three numbers after are squarefree semiprimes.
Irregular triangular T: (row 1) = (1); (row n+1) = inverse runlength sequence of row n, starting with 2 if r = 3k for some k, and 1 otherwise. See Comments.
Irregular triangular T: (row 1) = (1); (row n+1) = inverse runlength sequence of row n, starting with 1 if r = 3k for some k, and  2 otherwise. See Comments.
Greatest perfect power < prime(n).
An 'eta-sequence': floor((n+1)*sqrt(2) + 1/2) - floor(n*sqrt(2) + 1/2).
Sufficient number of monominoes to exclude X-pentominoes from an n X n board.
a(0)=1. a(n) = a(prime(n)(mod n)) + 1, where prime(n) is the n-th prime.
Domination number of the Cartesian product of two n-cycles.
Domination number for kings' graph K(n).
Modular phase shift of the tetration base n written by juxtaposing its representative congruence classes modulo 10 taken by starting from height 2 + v(n), and a(n) = -1 if n is a multiple of 10.
Sum of the integers from 1 to n that are not antidivisors of n.
In the binary expansion of n, arrange bits row-wise in a binary tree which is complete except for the last row and then read those bits in pre-order.
a(n) = phi(phi(n)), where phi is the Euler totient function.
Sum of divisors d of n such that n/d is odd with an even number of prime factors (counted with multiplicity).
Numbers which can be written in precisely one way as sum of a subset of their proper divisors and that have exactly one subset of their divisors such that the complement has the same sum.
Lowest weight of rational fraction with denominator n.
Decimal expansion of Norton's constant.
a(n) is the number of positive numbers k <= sigma(n) that are not a sum of any subset of distinct divisors of n.
Least perfect power > prime(n).
Positive numbers k such that -k is properly represented by the Pell Form x^2 - 15*y^2.
The number of root fires on a rooted undirected infinite ternary tree with a self-loop at the root, when the chip-firing process starts with 3n chips at the root.
The least k such that prime(1+n)^k > 2 * prime(n)^k.
a(n)^n is the least n-th power containing every digit.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the count of integers between a(n) and a(n-1), excluding values already in the sequence, is distinct from the same count for any other a(k) and a(k-1) at the time they occurred.
a(n) = number of non-Pythagorean primes in the prime factorization of n (including multiplicities).
Numbers k such that the prime gap between the consecutive primes p1 < k^2 < p2 sets a new record.
The total number of fires on a rooted undirected infinite ternary tree with a self-loop at the root, when the chip-firing process starts with 3n chips at the root.
Number of stable digits of the integer tetration n^^n (i.e., maximum nonnegative integer m such that n^^n is congruent modulo 10^m to n^^(n + 1)), or -1 if n is a multiple of 10.
Pair up the numbers.
Orders of non-Abelian groups: n such that some group of order n is non-Abelian.
Numbers k such that prime(k) + prime(k+1) + prime(k+2) is prime.
Number of divisors d of n such that (-d)^d == -d^d (mod n).
The smallest cardinality of a difference-basis in the cyclic group of order n.
n appears 2n times, for n >= 1; also nearest integer to square root of n.

On a graph with points (k, prime(k)), k>=1, consider if prime(n) is on any previously drawn infinite line between prime(j) and prime(j-1), where 2<=j<=n-1. If not, add one to the count of primes not on any such line, and then, regardless of if prime(n) is on a line, draw an infinite line between prime(n) and prime(n-1). The sequence gives the total number of primes not on any previously drawn infinite line, starting from prime(2).

Additive function a(n) defined by the recursive formula a(1)=1 and a(p^k)=a(k) for any prime p.

Triangle T(n,k) read by rows in which the n-th row begins with T(n,1) = n and contains n terms of an arithmetic progression with a common difference of (n-1).
Theta series of cubic lattice with respect to deep hole.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that for any n > 0, a(k) + ... + a(n) is a prime number for some k in 1..n.

LQTL Lean Quaternary Temporal Logic: a terse form of temporal logic created by assigning four descriptors such that false, becoming true, true and becoming false are represented and become a linear sequence. Take the sequence bb with two integer 'seeds', e.g. a(1)=0, a(2)=1 and the relating list cc consisting of all digits of bb, e.g. cc={0,1}. Take n=3, calculate d=abs[cc(n-1)-cc(n-2)] = abs(2-3)=1; then next term of bb, a(n), is the smallest 'new' (not in bb) number containing digit d, e.g. a(3)=10 => bb={0,1,10} and cc={0,1,1,0}; we proceed: n=4, d = 0, a(4)=20, bb={0,1,10,20}, cc={0,1,1,0,2,0}, n=5, d = 1, a(5)=11, bb={0,1,10,20,11}, cc={0,1,1,0,2,0,1,1}, etc.

Triangle read by rows: T(i,j) = F(i)*F(j)*C(i,j) for 1 <= j <= i, where F(n) is the n-th Fibonacci number and C(n,m) is a binomial coefficient.
a(1)=1 and a(n)=least positive integer not yet in sequence, if n is even and a(n) = sum of least two positive integers not yet in sequence, if n is odd.
Sum of the n-th powers of the roots of the (reduced) weight enumerator of the extended Golay code (1 + 759*x^2 + 2576*x^3 + 759*x^4 + x^6).
T(n,k) = binomial(n - k - 1, k), 0 <= k < n, and T(n,n) = (-1)^n, triangle read by rows.

Smallest prime q such that (p^q+1)/(p+1) is a prime, where p = prime(n).

Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the coefficient of x^k in the polynomial p(n,x) defined by p(0,x)=1, p(1,x)=1+x, p(n,x)=xp(n-1,x)+(-1)^(n+1)p(n-2,x) for n>=2.

Two decks each have n kinds of cards, 2 of each kind. The first deck is laid out in order. The second deck is shuffled and laid out next to the first. A match occurs if a card from the second deck is next to a card of the same kind from the first deck. a(n) is the number of ways of achieving no matches.
Triangle read by rows giving Whitney numbers T(n,k) of Fibonacci lattices.
a(n) = least k such that 2ik + 1 is prime for all 1 <= i <= n.
Sum of the n-th powers of the roots of the polynomial x^6 + 14*x^5 + 87*x^4 + 148*x^3 + 87*x^2 + 14*x + 1.
Largest primes < numbers of the form 6k (duplicates removed).

Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = number of specially labeled bicolored connected graphs with k points in one color class and n-k points in the other class . 'Special' means there are separate labels 1,2, ...,k and 1,2, ...,n-k for the two color classes (n >= 1, k = floor((n+1)/2), ..., n).
a(n) = Sum_{i=1..n} ( Sum_{j=1..n} i^j ).
Sum of first prime(n) primes.
Topswops (1): start by shuffling n cards labeled 1..n. If top card is m, reverse order of top m cards, then repeat. a(n) is the maximal number of steps before top card is 1.
Smallest prime q such that (q^p-1)/(q-1) is prime, where p = prime(n); or 0 if no such prime q exists.
Triangle whose k-th column satisfies a(n) = (k+3)*a(n-1)-(k+2)*a(n-2).
Sequence generated from the first nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function.
Sequence generated from the second nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function.
Sorting numbers: maximal number of comparisons for sorting n elements by binary insertion.
Sum of numerator and denominator in n-th harmonic number, 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 +...+ 1/n.

a(1)=1. For n>=2, a(n) = n + (largest integer which is <= n and is missing from the earlier terms of the sequence).
Smallest b such that all digits are distinct in base b representation of n.

Product of signed and unsigned Morgan-Voyce triangles.
a(1)=1, a(2)=2. a(n) = the smallest positive integer that does not occur earlier in the sequence and is coprime to the second-largest term occurring earlier in the sequence.
Number of binary Lyndon words with an even number of 1's.
Triangle T(n,k) with the coefficient [x^k] of the characteristic polynomial of the following n X n triangular matrix: 4 on the main diagonal, -1 of the two adjacent subdiagonals, 0 otherwise.
Numbers k such that k^3 is a sum of three successive primes.

Value of Vandermonde determinant for the first n prime numbers: V[prime(1), ..., prime(n)].
Reciprocal of Vandermonde determinant of (1/2,1/3,...,1/(n+1)).
Reciprocal of Vandermonde determinant of (1/2,1/4,...,1/(2n)).
Reciprocal of Vandermonde determinant of (1/4,1/6,...,1/(2n+2)).
Reciprocal of Vandermonde determinant of (1/3,1/6,...,1/(3n)).
Vandermonde determinant of the first n terms of (2,3,5,6,8,9,...) = (j+floor((j+1)/2)).
a(n) = Product_{2 <= i < j <= n+1} (i + j).
Vandermonde sequence using x^2 - xy + y^2 applied to (1,2,...,n).
Vandermonde sequence using x^2 + xy + y^2 applied to (1,3,5,...,2n-1).
a(n) = Product_{1 <= i < j <= n} 2*(i+j-1).
Binary representation of n-th iteration of the Rule 220 elementary cellular automaton starting with a single black cell.
n 0's followed by n 1's.
Number of partitions of n into distinct parts, the greatest being odd.
Number of partitions of n into distinct parts, the greatest being even.

Vandermonde sequence using x^2 - xy + y^2 applied to (1,3,5,...,2n-1).

Vandermonde sequence using x^2 + xy + y^2 applied to (1,4,9,...,n^2).
Vandermonde sequence using x^2 - xy + y^2 applied to (1,4,9,...,n^2).

Vandermonde sequence using x^2 + y^2 applied to (1,2,4,...,2^(n-1)).
Vandermonde sequence using x^2 + xy + y^2 applied to (1,2,6,...,n!).
Vandermonde sequence using x^2 - x*y + y^2 applied to (1,2,6,...,n!).
Vandermonde sequence using x^2 + y^2 applied to (1,2,6,...,n!).

Vandermonde sequence using x^2 + y^2 applied to the first n triangular numbers: 1,3,6,10,...,n(n+1)/2.
Vandermonde sequence using x^2 + xy + y^2 applied to the Fibonacci numbers (1,2,3,5,...F(n+1)).
Vandermonde sequence using x^2 - xy + y^2 applied to the Fibonacci numbers (1,2,3,5,...F(n+1)).
